This evaluation is crisp and checks for the absence of Permafrost in the soil profile.  The terms_terms_used_in-lieu_of_texture are examined for all layers. 

Where terms_used_in_lieu_of_texture equals cpf for any layer the evaluation is absolutely false and permafrost is not absent in the soil profile.
    AND
Where terms_used_in_lieu_of_texture does not equal cpf or is NULL for all layers the evaluation is absolutely true and permafrost is absent in the soil profile.

 1. USDA TEXTURE           ---        ---        ICE     PERMAFROST
 
 
The textures given on the Soils-5 are examined for all layers.
 
     If ICE is listed as a texture on any layer, then a SEVERE rating is given.
 
     Otherwise a SLIGHT rating is given.

This evaluation checks the filtering capacity of the soil.  The minimum high, low, and representative values for  sat_hydraulic_conductivity are selected to a depth of 60 inches. 

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
  Where the soil horizon property sat_hydraulic_conductivity >= 42 micrometers/second (6.0 inches/hr), the evaluaton is absolutely true and the restrictive feature is poor effulent filter field.
        AND
  Where the soil horizon property sat_hydraulic_conductivity <= 14 micrometers/second (2.0 inches/hour), the evaluation is absolutely false and the restrictive feature is not poor effulent filter field.

If no data is entered, then an artificial default value(s) is used.

Ames Description Prior to 1996
 ___________________________________________________________________
                       |             LIMITS             |RESTRICTIVE
+                       ________________________________
     PROPERTY          |  SLIGHT  | MODERATE |  SEVERE  |  FEATURE
                       |          |          |          |
+___________________________________________________________________
 
 2.  PERMEABILITY           ---      2.0-6.0     >6.0    POOR FILTER
     (0-60", IN/HR)
  
 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________
 
The values given on the Soils-5 for permeability are examined and a low value for each layer is determined.  The low value used for comparison depends on which of the following conditions is met first. If no data is entered, then an artificial value of 100 is used.  If the entry is of the form '<xx', then an artificial value of 0 is used.  Otherwise the low value is used.
 
The layers within the given depths are examined.  The surface layers are each rated separately.  The lowest value found from all the sublayers is rated.  The rating algorithm used is as follows:
 
   A value >= 6.0 gets a SEVERE rating.
   A value >= 2.0 and < 6.0 gets a MODERATE rating.
 
If the sublayer rating is SEVERE, then this property is rated SEVERE and no phasing will be done, regardless of the surface layer ratings.
 
If the sublayer rating is MODERATE, then this property is rated MODERATE if there is any SLIGHT or MODERATE surface layer rating, and it is rated SEVERE if there is any SEVERE surface layer rating.  Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.

evaldesc: wet stuff -- for developing picnic sites

This evaluation checks for a saturated or wet condition within a depth of 30 cm (1 foot) of the soil surface.  The water moisture status for all layers are examined and those saturated or wet layers are evalutated for depth.

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
  Where soil_moisture_status is wet and the depth to soil_moist_depth_to_top is less than 30 cm (1.0 feet) the evaluation is absolutely true and WETNESS is a restrictive feature.
   OR
  Where soil_moisture_status is wet and the depth to  soil_moist_depth_to_top  is greater than 75 cm (2.5 feet) the evaluation is absolutely false  and WETNESS is not a restrictive feature.

If the soil_moisture_status is not wet or null, then the property asumption is that soil_moist_depth_to_top is NULL and no water table is present.

     PROPERTY                             |  SLIGHT  | MODERATE |  SEVERE  |  FEATURE
 4. WATER TABLE (FT)                >2.5              1.0-2.5               <1.0             WETNESS
  
 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________
 
The low value in the range of values given on the Soils-5 for depth to high water table is examined.  If a '+' occurs in this field, then there is ponding and a SEVERE rating is given.  Otherwise the value used for comparison depends on which of the following conditions is met first.
 
If no data is entered, then an artificial value of 99.9 is used.
 
Otherwise the low value is used.
 
           A value < 1.0 gets a SEVERE rating.

evalname: Wet, Ground Water Within 105 to 150 cm (3.5 to 5 ft.)
evaldesc:
This evaluation checks for a saturated or wet condition within a depth of 105cm (3.5 feet) of the soil surface.  The water moisture status for all layers are examined and those saturated or wet layers are evalutated for depth.

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
  Where soil_moisture_status is wet and the depth to soil_moist_depth_to_top is less than 105 cm (3.5 feet) the evaluation is absolutely true and WETNESS is a restrictive feature.
   OR
  Where soil_moisture_status is wet and the depth to  soil_moist_depth_to_top  is greater than >= 150 cm (5 feet) the evaluation is absolutely false  and WETNESS is not a restrictive feature.
  
If the soil_moisture_status is not wet or null, then the property asumption is that soil_moist_depth_to_top is NULL and no water table is present.

NOTE:
The following CRITERIA was used in the AMES 3SD legacy system.  I have tested this rule as presented in the AMES documentation and the permeability exclusion fails in several respects.

First there is no accounting for water table position.
If the water table is below the slowly permeable layer than WETNESS is not included in the rating.
If the water table is above the slowly permeable layer than this may be a perched condition and depending on the thickness of the water table may or may not be a hazard.

I have been unable to locate any documentation that would verify the intent or purpose of this exclusion.  In the absence of such documentation, it is my opinion that the contribution of water table to the Sewage Lagoon interpretation is greatly reduced by this exclusion.  This may result in insertion of Sewage Lagoons into soils that have significant water tables and the may lead to serious ground water contamination hazards.  Robert D Nielsen 3/99.

Ames Description Prior to 1996:

NOTE:  DUE TO LACK OF TECHNICAL DOCUMENTATION THE PERMEABILITY EXCLUSION (Footnote 2/) IN THE LEGACY (AMES 3SD) VERSION OF THE CRITERIA WAS NOT CARRIED FORWARD DURING THE  CONVERSION.


                                                     |                             LIMITS                            |  RESTRICTIVE
     PROPERTY                        |  SLIGHT  | MODERATE |  SEVERE  |  FEATURE
 8. DEPTH TO HIGH                  ---                  ---                    +              PONDING
    WATER TABLE (FT)               >5              2/3.5-5               2/<3.5        WETNESS
 
 2/Disregard wetness if a layer at least 20 inches thick has
   permeability of less than 0.2 in/hr.
 
 
 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________
 
 The low value in the range of values given on the Soils-5 for depth to high water table is examined.  If a '+' occurs in this field, then there is ponding and a SEVERE rating is given.  Otherwise the value used for comparison depends on which of the following conditions is met first.
 
 If no data is entered, then an artificial value of 99.9 is used.
 
 Otherwise the low value is used. 
           A value < 3.5 gets a SEVERE rating.
           A value >= 3.5 and < 5 gets a MODERATE rating.
           A value >= 5 gets a SLIGHT rating.


 PORTION NOT CONVERTED.

 After the above rating is made, the following calculations occur to take care of Footnote 2.  This is only done if the above rating was MODERATE or SEVERE with a WETNESS restrictive feature.
 
 The values given on the Soils-5 for permeability are examined and a high value for each layer is determined.  The high value used for first.
 
 If no data is entered, then an artificial value of 0 is used.
 
 If the entry is a single number or is of the form '<xx', then the single value entered is used.
 
 If the entry is of the form '>xx', then an artificial value of 100 is used.
 
 Otherwise the high value is used.
 
 Each layer with a permeability value <= 0.2 is "flagged".  Next, the thickness of each layer is computed.  If there is a single flagged layer or more than one adjacent flagged layers with a total thickness of 20 inches or more, then the MODERATE or SEVERE rating for DEPTH TO HIGH WATER TABLE is cancelled.

The water moisture status for all layers are examined and those saturated or wet layers are evalutated for depth.  If a saturated condition occurs within 30 cm (1 foot) of the soil surface than wetness is a limitation.

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
  Where soil_moisture_status is wet and the depth to soil_moist_depth_to_top is greater than 90 cm (3 foot) the evaluation is absolutely true.
   OR
  Where soil_moisture_status is wet and the depth to  soil_moist_depth_to_top  is less than 30 cm (1 feet) the evaluation is absolutely false.

If the soil_moisture_status is not wet or null, then the property asumption is that soil_moist_depth_to_top is NULL and no water table is present.

Ames Description Prior to 1996:

+                                                   ________________________________
     PROPERTY                        |   GOOD   |   FAIR   |   POOR   |                        FEATURE
 +___________________________________________________________________

 8. DEPTH TO HIGH WATER
    WATER TABLE (FT)           >3             1-3             <1                                   WETNESS

 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________

 The low value in the range of values given on the Soils-5 for depth to high water table is examined.  The value used for comparison depends on which of the following conditions is met first.

 If no data is entered, then an artificial value of 99.9 is used.

 Otherwise the low value is used.

           A value < 1 gets a POOR rating.
           A value >= 1 and < 3 gets a FAIR rating.
           A value >= 3 gets a GOOD rating.

evaldesc:
dmoore3/6/00 changed 105 depth to 107 for fined tuned accuracy.  Tested aainst matsu*, copper river, north star, upper tana*, genstle, yentna with good results


This evaluation checks for a saturated or wet condition within a depth of 105cm (3.5 feet) of the soil surface.  The water moisture status for all layers are examined and those saturated or wet layers are evalutated for depth.

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
  Where soil_moisture_status is wet and the depth to soil_moist_depth_to_top is less than 105 cm (3.5 feet) the evaluation is absolutely true and WETNESS is a restrictive feature.
   OR
  Where soil_moisture_status is wet and the depth to  soil_moist_depth_to_top  is greater than >= 150 cm (5 feet) the evaluation is absolutely false  and WETNESS is not a restrictive feature.
  
If the soil_moisture_status is not wet or null, then the property asumption is that soil_moist_depth_to_top is NULL and no water table is present.

NOTE:
The following CRITERIA was used in the AMES 3SD legacy system.  I have tested this rule as presented in the AMES documentation and the permeability exclusion fails in several respects.

First there is no accounting for water table position.
If the water table is below the slowly permeable layer than WETNESS is not included in the rating.
If the water table is above the slowly permeable layer than this may be a perched condition and depending on the thickness of the water table may or may not be a hazard.

I have been unable to locate any documentation that would verify the intent or purpose of this exclusion.  In the absence of such documentation, it is my opinion that the contribution of water table to the Sewage Lagoon interpretation is greatly reduced by this exclusion.  This may result in insertion of Sewage Lagoons into soils that have significant water tables and the may lead to serious ground water contamination hazards.  Robert D Nielsen 3/99.

Ames Description Prior to 1996:

NOTE:  DUE TO LACK OF TECHNICAL DOCUMENTATION THE PERMEABILITY EXCLUSION (Footnote 2/) IN THE LEGACY (AMES 3SD) VERSION OF THE CRITERIA WAS NOT CARRIED FORWARD DURING THE  CONVERSION.


                                                     |                             LIMITS                            |  RESTRICTIVE
     PROPERTY                        |  SLIGHT  | MODERATE |  SEVERE  |  FEATURE
 8. DEPTH TO HIGH                  ---                  ---                    +              PONDING
    WATER TABLE (FT)               >5              2/3.5-5               2/<3.5        WETNESS
 
 2/Disregard wetness if a layer at least 20 inches thick has
   permeability of less than 0.2 in/hr.
 
 
 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________
 
 The low value in the range of values given on the Soils-5 for depth to high water table is examined.  If a '+' occurs in this field, then there is ponding and a SEVERE rating is given.  Otherwise the value used for comparison depends on which of the following conditions is met first.
 
 If no data is entered, then an artificial value of 99.9 is used.
 
 Otherwise the low value is used. 
           A value < 3.5 gets a SEVERE rating.
           A value >= 3.5 and < 5 gets a MODERATE rating.
           A value >= 5 gets a SLIGHT rating.


 PORTION NOT CONVERTED.

 After the above rating is made, the following calculations occur to take care of Footnote 2.  This is only done if the above rating was MODERATE or SEVERE with a WETNESS restrictive feature.
 
 The values given on the Soils-5 for permeability are examined and a high value for each layer is determined.  The high value used for first.
 
 If no data is entered, then an artificial value of 0 is used.
 
 If the entry is a single number or is of the form '<xx', then the single value entered is used.
 
 If the entry is of the form '>xx', then an artificial value of 100 is used.
 
 Otherwise the high value is used.
 
 Each layer with a permeability value <= 0.2 is "flagged".  Next, the thickness of each layer is computed.  If there is a single flagged layer or more than one adjacent flagged layers with a total thickness of 20 inches or more, then the MODERATE or SEVERE rating for DEPTH TO HIGH WATER TABLE is cancelled.

evalname: Cecil Wet, Ground Water Near Surface (50 - 100cm)
evaldesc:
This evaluation checks for the presence of a water table and if present evaluates water table depth.

A soil can be a complete or partial member of the set of soils that are limited by the depth to water table and DEPTH to SATURATED ZONE is the set's restrictive feature.  If the depth to water table is less than 50cm (20 inches), then the soil is a complete member of the set.  If the depth to water table is greater than 50cm (20 inches) and less than 100cm (40 inches) then the soil is a partial member of the set.  A soil that has water table at a depth of more than 100cm (40 inches) is not a member of the set.

This evaluation is used in the LCC 7s subrule in the SSR 12 NIRR Land Capability Class interpretation.

The scoring curve for slope was based on the study by Lui et al. (1994). They showed that for slopes between 9 and 50%, the soil loss was linearly related to the sine of the slope angle, similar to what is used in RULSE but takes into account steeper slopes. The shape of the curve in plot of slope percent versus soil loss normalized to 9% is slightly convex from 9 to 50% slopes. The Y axis (soil loss normalized to 9%) was replaced with 0 to 1 to produce the scoring curve. Below 9%, the shape is still convex but less steep.  The scoring curve is as follows:

	Slope score = (a + cx + ex2 + gx3)/(1 + bx + dx2 + fx3)
	a = -0.00097169878; b = -0.085569059; c = 0.022525266; d = 0.0068975356; e = -0.0036133219; f = 8.00000689E-05; g = 0.00024152235; x = slope gradient (%)


Lui et al. (1994) - equation 2 in Figure 2.

evalname: Shallow to Bedrock (50 to 180cm (20 to 72")), PA regs
evaldesc:
This evaluation checks for the presence of bedrock within a specified depth.  The component data are check for restriction_kind = "bedrock (lithic)" or "bedrock (paralithic)" and restriction_depth_to_top is evaluated.

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
  Where the soil component property restriction_kind = "bedrock (lithic)" or "bedrock (paralithic)" and the restriction_depth_to_top is less then 100 cm (40 inches) then the evaluation is absolutely true and depth to bedrock is a restrictive feature.
     AND
  Where the soil component property restriction_kind = "bedrock (lithic)" or "bedrock (paralithic)" and the restriction_depth_to_top is greater then 182 cm (72 inches) then the evaluation is absolutely false and depth to bedrock is not a restrictive feature.

This evaluation checks for the presence of sodium within 50 cm (20 in) of the soil surface.  The component horizon sodium_adsorption_ratio data are check and evaluated.

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
 
  Where the soil component horizon property sodium_adsorption_ratio within 50 cm (20 in) of the surface is greater than 13 then the evaluation is absolutely false and "EXCESS SODIUM" is a restrictive feature.
     AND
  Where the soil component horizon property sodium_adsorption_ratio within 50 cm (20 in) of the surface is less than 4 then the evaluation is absolutely true and "EXCESS SODIUM" is not a restrictive feature.


Ames Description prior to  1996:
                                                           |                            LIMITS                             |   RESTRICTIVE
     PROPERTY                              |  SLIGHT  | MODERATE |  SEVERE  |  FEATURE
 8. SODIUM ADSORPTION           <4                    4-13                 >13             EXCESS SODIUM
    RATIO (0-20") 
+___________________________
 
The values given on the Soils-5 for sodium adsorption ratio are examined and an average of the low and high values is found.

If no data is entered, then the layer is skipped.
 
If the entry is a single number, then the single value entered is used as the average.
 
If the entry is of the form '<xxx', then the average is taken using 0 and xxx.
 
If the entry is of the form '>xxx', then the average is taken using xxx and 200.
 
A separate weighted average to 20 inches is calculated for each surface layer.
 
     A weighted average > 13 gets a SEVERE rating.
     A weighted average >= 4 and <= 13 gets a MODERATE rating.
 
Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.
 
NOTE:  If all layers on the Soils-5 are missing sodium adsorption ratio entries, the component is flagged in the final output table.

 13. SALINITY (MMHOS/CM)    <4        4-8        >8      EXCESS SALT
     (SURFACE LAYER)
 
 
 
 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________
 
 The values given on the Soils-5 for salinity are examined for each surface layer.  A high value is determined for each surface layer depending on which of the following conditions is met first.
 
 If the entry is a normal range, then the high value is used.
 
 If the entry is of the form '>xx', then an artificial value of 99 is used.
 
 Otherwise an artificial value of 0 is used.
 
 The maximum value over all surface layers is determined.
 
        A maximum value > 8 gets a SEVERE rating.
        A maximum value > 4 and <= 8 gets a MODERATE rating.
        A maximum value <= 4 gets a SLIGHT rating.

evalname: Clay Activity (.05 to .15 cec/clay ratio) demo
evaldesc:
This evaluation checks the clay activity of the soil.  The component horizon cation_exch_capcty_nh4oacph7 is divided by clay_total_separate and the result is check and evaluated.

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
 
  Where the result of the soil component horizon property cation_exch_capcty_nh4oacph7 divided by clay_total_separate is less than 0.05 the evaluation is absolutely true and "LOW ADSORPTION" is a restrictive feature.
     AND
  Where the result of the soil component horizon property cation_exch_capcty_nh4oacph7 divided by clay_total_separate is greater than 0.15 the evaluation is absolutely false and "LOW ADSORPTION" is not a restrictive feature.

Ames Description prior to  1996:
___________________________________________________________________
                       |             LIMITS             |RESTRICTIVE
+                       ________________________________
     PROPERTY          |  SLIGHT  | MODERATE |  SEVERE  |  FEATURE
                       |          |          |          |
+___________________________________________________________________
 
 11. CLAY ACTIVITY         >.15     .05-.15      <.05     LOW ADSORPTION
 
 
 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________
 
 The values given on the Soils-5 for clay and CEC are examined and an
 average of the low and high values is found for both.
 
 Clay:
+_____
 
 If no data is entered, then the layer is skipped.
 
 If the entry is a single number, then the single value entered is used as the average.
 
 If the entry is of the form '<xx', then the average is taken using
 
 
 If the entry is of the form '>xx', then the average is taken using xx and 99.
 
 CEC:
+____
 
 If no data is entered, then the layer is skipped.
 
 If the entry is a single number, then the single value entered is used as the average.
 
 If the entry is of the form '<xxx', then the average is taken using 0 and xxx.
 
 If the entry is of the form '>xxx', then the average is taken using xxx and 200.
 
 
 After each average is found for a layer, the clay activity is calculated.  Clay Activity = CEC ave. / Clay ave.

     A weighted average < .05 gets a SEVERE rating.
     A weighted average >= .05 and <= .15 gets a MODERATE rating.
     A weighted average > .15 gets a SLIGHT rating.
 
 Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.

 NOTE:  If all layers on the Soils-5 are missing CEC entries, the component is flagged in the final output table.

evalname: TN Filter Field 60 to 180 cm (24 to 72")
evaldesc:
7/99 Modification:
This evaluation checks the filtering capacity of the soil.  The maximum high, low, and representative values for sat_hydraulic_conductivity are selected for each horizon between 24 to 72 inches and above any restrictive layer. 

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
  Where the soil horizon property sat_hydraulic_conductivity > 42 micrometers/second (6.0 inches/hr), the evaluaton is absolutely true and the restrictive feature is poor effluent filter field.
        AND
  Where the soil horizon property sat_hydraulic_conductivity <= 42 micrometers/second (6.0 inches/hour), the evaluation is absolutely false and the restrictive feature is not poor effluent filter field.

If no data is entered, then an artificial default value(s) is used.

In 1990 the evaluation depth was extended from a base of 40 inches to a base of 60 inches.

Ames Description Prior to 1996

                                              |                           LIMITS                              |  RESTRICTIVE
     PROPERTY                 |  SLIGHT  | MODERATE |  SEVERE  |  FEATURE
 7. PERMEABILITY          ---                 ---                  >6.0             POOR FILTER
    (IN/HR):    (24-40")            
 
 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________
   
 The values given on the Soils-5 for permeability are examined and a
 high value for each layer is determined.  The high value used for
 comparison depends on which of the following conditions is met
 first.
 
 If no data is entered, then an artificial value of 0 is used.
 
 If the entry is a single number or is of the form '<xx', then the
  single value entered is used.
 
 If the entry is of the form '>xx', then an artificial value of 100
  is used.
 
 Otherwise the high value is used.
 
 The layers within the given depths are examined.  If surface layers are included in these depths, each is rated separately.  Then each sublayer is rated to determine the worst sublayer rating.  The rating algorithm used on each layer is as follows:
 
           A value > 6.0 gets a SEVERE rating.
           A value <= 6.0 gets a SLIGHT rating.
 
 If surface layers are not involved, then this property is rated the
 same as the worst sublayer rating.
 
 If surface layers are involved, then the following applies.  If the
 worst sublayer rating is SEVERE, then this property is rated SEVERE
 and no phasing will be done, regardless of the surface layer
 ratings.
 
 If the worst sublayer rating is SLIGHT, then this property is rated
 SLIGHT if there is any SLIGHT surface layer rating, and it is rated
 SEVERE if there is any SEVERE surface layer rating.  Phasing will be
 done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.

           A value > .2 and <= .6 gets a MODERATE rating.
           A value <= .2 gets a SLIGHT rating.

evalname: Missouri Soil Reaction Below the Surface
evaldesc:
If reaction is 6.8 then phosphorous loading potential is optimum.

We disagreed with the national rule on this property. The national rule was set up to evaluate the topsoil only with a full rating if the surface ph was high or low. The national rule favored P to be fixed and P retention maximized in the topsoil. Our logic as with free carbonate was that it would be better to retain the P in the subsoil and have lower P retention values in the surface where is available for transport by runoff. We also used the logic that ph values ideal for most of the forages and grain crops would provide more plant growth, increase residue levels, reduce erosion, and be acceptable for the farmer to make a profit

evalname: 12 USDA Texture Class & Modifiers - Sands and Sandy Gravels
evaldesc:
MO12 version: national evaluation modified to correctly include actual textures from standard, Shallow Excavations NSSH 620-1. National evaluation uses wildcards and can include gravelly modifiers of loamy textures, which is not the standard.
SFinn 9/2008
============
This evaluation is crisp and checks the texture_modifier_and_class for all layers. 
 
Where texture_class equals coarse sands, fine sands, very fine sands or sandy gravel for any layer the evaluation is absolutely true and the restrictive feature is CUTBANKS CAVE.
    AND
Where texture_class does not equal coarse sands, fine sands, very fine sands or sandy gravel or is NULL for all layers the evaluation is absolutely false and the restrictive feature is not CUTBANKS CAVE.
 
 
 Ames Description prior to 1996: 

                                   	    |             LIMITS      		               |RESTRICTIVE
     PROPERTY       	    |  SLIGHT  | MODERATE |  SEVERE  |  FEATURE
 4. USDA TEXTURE       	              ---                COS, S,     CUTBANKS
    (20-60")                                  		                 FS, VFS,    CAVE
                                             		                 LCOS, LS,
			                                       LFS, LVFS,
			                                       G, SG
 
 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________
 
The textures given on the Soils-5 are examined for the layers within 20-60 inches.  If surface layers are included in these depths, each is rated separately.  Then each sublayer is rated to determine the worst sublayer rating.  The rating algorithm used on each layer is as follows:
 
If COS, S, FS, VFS, LCOS, LS, LFS, LVFS, G, or SG is listed as a texture, then a SEVERE rating is given.

Otherwise a SLIGHT rating is given.
 
If surface layers are not involved, then this property is rated the same as the worst sublayer rating.
 
If surface layers are involved, then the following applies.  If the worst sublayer rating is SEVERE, then this property is rated SEVERE and no phasing will be done, regardless of the surface layer ratings.
 
If the worst sublayer rating is MODERATE, then this property is rated MODERATE if there is any SLIGHT or MODERATE surface layer rating, and it is rated SEVERE if there is any SEVERE surface layer
 rating.  Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.
 
If the worst sublayer rating is SLIGHT, then this property is rated SLIGHT if there is any SLIGHT surface layer rating, MODERATE if there is any MODERATE surface layer rating, and SEVERE if there is any SEVERE surface layer rating.  Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given. rating, and it is rated SEVERE if there is any SEVERE surface layer rating.  Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.

evaldesc:
The fuzzy space is defined as the condition: 
  Where the total number of months the soil property flooding_frequency_class is "occasional" is <2 for all months corresponding to a "growing season month" as determined by the soil property taxonomic_temp_regime, the evaluation returns a value of 1

Growing season months are derived from the temperature regime of the soil component as follows:

taxonomic_temp_regime		growing season months
---------------------		---------------------
cryic, isofrigid, or pergelic	July and August

frigid or mesic			May, June, July, 
				August, and September

thermic or			March, April, May, 
hyperthermic			June, July, August,
				September, and October

isothermic,			February, March, April,
isohyperthermic,		May, June, July, August,
or isomesic			September, October, and
				November

evaldesc:
This evaluation is crisp and checks for UNIFIED equal to "OL", "OH", or "PT".

Where unified_soil_classification equals "OL", "OH", or "PT" the evaluation is absolutely true and EXCESS HUMUS is a restrictive feature.
    AND
Where unified_soil_classification does not equal "OL", "OH", or "PT" the evaluation is absolutely false and EXCESS HUMUS is not a restrictive feature
 Ames prior to 1996

                                               |                         LIMITS                                       | RESTRICTIVE
     PROPERTY                  |  SLIGHT  | MODERATE |  SEVERE         | FEATURE
 8. UNIFIED (20-60")         ---                     ---          OL, OH, PT      EXCESS HUMUS
 
 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________
 
 The unified values given on the Soils-5 are examined for the layers within 20-60 inches.  If surface layers are included in these depths, each is rated separately.  Then each sublayer is rated to determine the worst sublayer rating.  The rating algorithm used on each layer is as follows:
 
 If OL, OH, or PT is listed as a texture, then a SEVERE rating is given.
 Otherwise a SLIGHT rating is given.
 
 If surface layers are not involved, then this property is rated the same as the worst sublayer rating.
 
 If surface layers are involved, then the following applies.  If the worst sublayer rating is SEVERE, then this property is rated SEVERE and no phasing will be done, regardless of the surface layer ratings.
 
 
 If the worst sublayer rating is SLIGHT, then this property is rated SLIGHT if there is any SLIGHT surface layer rating, and it is rated SEVERE if there is any SEVERE surface layer rating.  Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.

This evaluation is crisp and checks the bulk_density_one_third_bar  for all layers within a depth of 50 to 150 cm (20 to 60 inches).
 
Where bulk_density_one_third_bar is greater then 1.8 for any layer within a depth of 50 to 150 cm (20 to 60 inches) the evaluation is true and the restrictive feature is DENSE LAYER.  However, this restriction has only a moderate inpact on the interpretation.
    AND
Where bulk_density_one_third_bar is less than 1.8 or is NULL for all layers within a depth of 50 to 150 cm (20 to 60 inches) the evaluation is absolutely false and the restrictive feature is not DENSE LAYER.
 
 
 Ames Description prior to 1996: 
1___________________________________________________________________
                                                                |                           LIMITS                               | RESTRICTIVE
     PROPERTY     		|  SLIGHT  | MODERATE |  SEVERE  |  FEATURE
 
 7. BULK DENSITY (G/CC)    	     ---                  >1.8                   ---            DENSE LAYER
    (20-60")

 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________
 
 The values given on the Soils-5 for bulk density are examined.  A high value is determined for each layer within 20-60 inches depending on which of the following conditions is met first.
 
 If the entry is a normal range, then the high value is used.
 
 If the entry is of the form '>xx', then an artificial value of 99.99 is used.
 
 If the entry is a single number or is of the form '<xx', then the single value entered is used.
 
 Otherwise an artificial value of 0 is used.
 
 If any of the determined values is > 1.8, then this property is rated SEVERE.  Otherwise it is rated SLIGHT.

+___________________________ 
 
 The textures given on the Soils-5 are examined for the layers within 20-60 inches.  If surface layers are included in these depths, each is rated separately.  Then each sublayer is rated to determine the worst sublayer rating.  The rating algorithm used on each layer is as follows:

If surface layers are not involved, then this property is rated the same as the worst sublayer rating.

If the worst sublayer rating is SLIGHT, then this property is rated  SLIGHT if there is any SLIGHT surface layer rating, and it is rated MODERATE if there is any MODERATE surface layer rating.  Phasing  will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.

evalname: Shrink-Swell Thickest Layer Above Bedrock or to 41"
evaldesc:
This evaluation checks for soil shrink-swell potential for the thickest layer within a depth of 0 to 150cm (60 inches) or from the surface to bedrock.  The linear_extensibility_percent for the thickest layer is examined and evalutated for the depth conditions.

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
  Where linear_extensibility_percent of the thickest layer is greater than  9 evaluation is absolutely true and SHRINK-SWELL is a restrictive feature.
   OR
  Where linear_extensibility_percent of the thickest layer is less than 3 the evaluation is absolutely false and SHRINK-SWELL is not a restrictive feature.

If the linear_extensibility_percent of the thickest layer is NULL then LE is assumed to be less than 3.

Ames Description Prior to 1996:
 
 1___________________________________________________________________
                                                         |             LIMITS                                                                    |RESTRICTIVE
+                                                      ________________________________
     PROPERTY                            |   GOOD   |   FAIR            |           POOR                           |  FEATURE
 +___________________________________________________________________

 4. 12/SHRINK-SWELL        LOW          MODERATE    HIGH, VERY HIGH           SHRINK -SWELL
                                                          (LE <3)        (LE 3-6)                   ( LE>6)

 12/Evaluate the thickest layer between 10 and 60 inches and also the bottom layer.  Choose the best rating.  When rating is based on bottom layer, verify thickness.



 According to footnote 12, calculations are done for both the thickest layer and the bottom layer.  Further description follows Property No. 5.

 Description of Calculation for Thickest Layer:
+______________________________________________

 The layer with the most inches between 10 and 60 inches is determined.  This could be a surface layer or a sublayer.  The shrink-swell values given on the Soils-5 are examined for the appropriate layer(s).

 The layer(s) being examined are rated according to the following algorithm:

 If the shrink-swell value equals '1' (HIGH) or '5' (VERY HIGH), then a POOR rating is given.
 If the shrink-swell value equals '3' (MODERATE), then a FAIR rating is given.
 Otherwise a GOOD rating is given.

 If the thickest layer is a sublayer, then this property is rated the same as this sublayer's rating.

 If the thickest layer is a surface layer, then this property is rated GOOD if there is any GOOD surface layer rating, FAIR if there is any FAIR surface layer rating, and POOR if there is any POOR surface layer rating.  Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.



 Description of Calculation for Bottom Layer:
+____________________________________________

 If the bottom layer has no data, then this calculation is skipped and the ratings for the thickest layer are chosen.

 Otherwise, this calculation is the same as above, except it is done for the bottom layer.  The bottom layer, like the thickest layer, may be a surface layer or a sublayer.

 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________
 
 The layer with the most inches between 10 and 40 inches is determined.  This could be a surface layer or a sublayer.  The GIN is calculated for the appropriate layer(s) according to the given algorithm.
 
 To calculate the GIN, median values are needed for the following: percent passing No. 200 sieve (F), liquid limit (LL), and plasticity index (PI).  A median is calculated by adding the low and high values, then dividing by 2, unless special conditions exist.  The median calculation is given below for each of these three variables.
 
 Percent passing No. 200 sieve:
+______________________________
 
 If no valid data is entered, then an artificial value of 0 is used as the median.
 
 If a single value is entered, then this value is used as the median.
 
 Otherwise the median is calculated using the low and high values.
 

 
 Liquid limit:
+_____________
 
 If the entry is of the form '<xxx', then a median is calculated using 0 and xxx. 
 If the entry is of the form '>xxx', then a median is calculated using xxx and 100.
  If no valid data is entered, then an artificial value of 0 is used as the median. 
 If a single value is entered, then this value is used as the median. 
 Otherwise the median is calculated using the low and high values.
 
 Plasticity index:
+_________________
 
 If the entry is of the form '<xxx', then a median is calculated using 0 and xxx. 
 If the entry is of the form '>xxx', then a median is calculated using xxx and 100. 
 If the entry is of the form 'NP', then an artificial value of 0 is used as the median. 
 
 If the entry is of the form 'NP-xxx', then a median is calculated using 0 and xxx. 
 If no valid data is entered, then an artificial value of 0 is used as the median. 
 If a single value is entered, then this value is used as the median. 
 Otherwise the median is calculated using the low and high values. 
 After the GIN is calculated, the layer(s) being examined are rated according to the following algorithm: 
    If GIN > 8, then a SEVERE rating is given.
    If GIN > 5 and <= 8, then a MODERATE rating is given.
    If GIN <= 5, then a SLIGHT rating is given.
 
 If the thickest layer is a sublayer, then this property is rated the same as this sublayer's rating.  If minerology on the Soils-5 equals '28' (Kaolinitic), then a MODERATE rating is upgraded to SLIGHT, and a SEVERE rating is upgraded to MODERATE.
 
 If the thickest layer is a surface layer, then this property is rated SLIGHT if there is any SLIGHT surface layer rating, MODERATE if there is any MODERATE surface layer rating, and SEVERE if there is any SEVERE surface layer rating.  If minerology on the Soils-5 equals '28' (Kaolinitic), then a MODERATE rating is upgraded to SLIGHT, and a SEVERE rating is upgraded to MODERATE.  Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.

evaldesc:
This evaluation checks the values of greater than  3" (75mm) fraction for the surface horizon. 

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
 
  Where the total of the soil component horizon coarse fragment property > 75mm is greater than 75% the evaluation is absolutely true and "LARGE STONES" is a restrictive feature.
     AND
  Where the total of the soil component horizon coarse fragment property > 75mm is less than 25% the evaluation is absolutely false and "LARGE STONES" is not a restrictive feature.

Intent is  rocks > 75mm in diameter between 15 and 60% by volume in the surface layer.  Conversion to by weight is  approximately 25 to 75%.  Criteria was modified to reflect intent.  4/99 rdn.

Ames Description prior to  1996:

                                                            |                             LIMITS                                  |  RESTRICTIVE
     PROPERTY                               |  SLIGHT  |   MODERATE   |  SEVERE    |  FEATURE
 4. USDA TEXTURE                          ---          STV, BYV,           STX, BYX,    LARGE STONES
    MODIFIER (SURFACE                                  CB, FL                  CBX, FLX, 
    LAYER)                                                                                                CBV, FLV,
                                                                                                                     CNX, CRX
                                                                                                                      SHX, SYX
 Description of Calculation:

 The modifiers and textures given on the Soils-5 for each surface layer are examined.

 The surface layers are each rated separately using the following algorithm.

 If STX, BYX, CBX, FLX, CBV, FLV, CNX, CRX, SHX or SYX is listed as a modifier, then a SEVERE rating is given.

 If STV, BYV, CB or FL is listed as a modifier, then a MODERATE rating is given.

 Otherwise a SLIGHT rating is given.

 This property is rated SLIGHT if there is any SLIGHT surface layer rating, MODERATE if there is any MODERATE surface layer rating, and SEVERE if there is any SEVERE surface layer rating.  Phasing will be done using modifier terms (texture is used if no modifier is entered) if more than one rating is given.

This evaluation checks the greater than 3 inch fraction of the soil.  The component horizon rock_frag_3_to_10_in and rock_frag_greater_than_10_in is calculated for the surface layer of the soil and the result is checked and evaluated.

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
 
  Where the total of the soil component surface horizon properties rock_frag_3_to_10_in and rock_frag_greater_than_10_in is greater than 30% the evaluation is absolutely true and "LARGE STONES" is a restrictive feature.
     AND
  Where the total of the soil component surface horizon properties rock_frag_3_to_10_in and rock_frag_greater_than_10_in is less than 5% the evaluation is absolutely false and "LARGE STONES" is not a restrictive feature.

Ames Description prior to  1996:

                                                  |                             LIMIT                               |  RESTRICTIVE
     PROPERTY                     |  SLIGHT  | MODERATE |  SEVERE  |  FEATURE
 7. FRACTION >3 IN                  <5                 5-30                >30            LARGE STONES
    (WT PCT) (SURFACE 
    LAYER)
 
 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________
 
 The values given on the Soils-5 for fraction 3-10 inches are examined and a high value for each layer is determined.  The high value used in the calculation depends on which of the following conditions is met first.
 
 If a single value of '99' is entered, then an artificial value of 100 is used. 
 If a single value not equal to '99' is entered, then an artificial value of 0 is used. 
 Otherwise the high value is used.
 
 A separate weighted average is calculated for each surface layer. 
       A weighted average > 30 gets a SEVERE rating.
       A weighted average > 5 and <= 30 gets a MODERATE rating.
       A weighted average <= 5 gets a SLIGHT rating.

evaldesc:
This evaluation checks the available water of the soil within 40 inches or within a root limiting layer if less than 40 inches.  The weight average of the component horizon available_water_capacity is calculated for the soil and the result is check and evaluated.

The fuzzy space is defined in Connecticut as the condition:
 
  Where the total of each layers weighted average of the soil component horizon property available_water_capacity to a depth of 100cm (40in) is less than 3.19cm (1.25in) the evaluation is absolutely true and "DROUGHTY" is a restrictive feature.
     AND
  Where the total of each layers weighted average of the soil component horizon property available_water_capacity to a depth of 100cm (40in) is greater than 10cm (4in) the evaluation is absolutely false and "DROUGHTY" is not a restrictive feature.

Ames Description prior to  1996:
                                                                                            LIMITS                                RESTRICTIVE
     PROPERTY                                 |  SLIGHT  | MODERATE |  SEVERE  |  FEATURE
 9. 1/AVAILABLE WATER             >.10               .05-.10              <.05            DROUGHTY
      CAPACITY (IN/IN)                    
 
 1/Weighted average to 40 inches.
  
 Description of Calculation:
 
 The values given on the Soils-5 for available water are examined and a low value for each layer is determined.  The low value for each layer is used in a weighted average calculation to 40 inches.  Each low value used in the calculation depends on which of the following conditions is met first.
 
 If no data is entered, then the layer is skipped. 
 If the entry is of the form '<xx', then an artificial value of 0 is  used.
 
 Otherwise the low value is used.
 
 A separate weighted average to 40 inches is calculated for each surface layer and then rated.  If for some reason the total thickness used in the weighted average calculation is 0, then it is assumed that a weighted average of 1 was calculated.  If a weighted average could not be calculated due to missing data, then it is assumed that a weighted average of 100 was calculated.
 
      A weighted average < .05 gets a SEVERE rating.
      A weighted average >= .05 and < .10 gets a MODERATE rating.
      A weighted average >= .10 gets a SLIGHT rating.

 If there is a weighted average rating of SEVERE, then this property is rated SEVERE.  If there is a weighted average rating of MODERATE, then this property is rated MODERATE.  If there is a weighted average rating of SLIGHT, then this property is rated SLIGHT.  Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.

 The values given on the Soils-5 for available water are examined and a low value for each layer is determined.  The low value for each layer is used in a weighted average calculation to 40 inches.  Each low value used in the calculation depends on which of the following conditions is met first.
 
 If no data is entered, then the layer is skipped. 
 If the entry is of the form '<xx', then an artificial value of 0 is  used.
 
 Otherwise the low value is used.
 
 A separate weighted average to 40 inches is calculated for each surface layer and then rated.  If for some reason the total thickness used in the weighted average calculation is 0, then it is assumed that a weighted average of 1 was calculated.  If a weighted average could not be calculated due to missing data, then it is assumed that a weighted average of 100 was calculated.
 
      A weighted average < .05 gets a SEVERE rating.
      A weighted average >= .05 and < .10 gets a MODERATE rating.
      A weighted average >= .10 gets a SLIGHT rating.

 If there is a weighted average rating of SEVERE, then this property is rated SEVERE.  If there is a weighted average rating of MODERATE, then this property is rated MODERATE.  If there is a weighted average rating of SLIGHT, then this property is rated SLIGHT.  Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.

+___________________________
 
 If not disregarded, the bottom-most layer with a valid permeability entry is found.  This could be a surface layer or a sublayer.  For example, if there are no sublayers, or all the sublayers are missing permeability entries, then the surface layers will be examined. Otherwise, just the bottom single sublayer will be examined.
 
 The values given on the Soils-5 for permeability are examined and a high value determined for the appropriate layer(s).  The high value used for comparison depends on which of the following conditions is
 met first.
 
 If no data is entered, then an artificial value of 0 is used. 
 If the entry is a single number or is of the form '<xx', then the  single value entered is used.
 
 If the entry is of the form '>xx', then an artificial value of 100 
 
 Otherwise the high value is used.
 
 The layer(s) being examined are rated according to the following algorithm: 
           A value > 2.0 gets a SEVERE rating.
           A value <= 2.0 gets a SLIGHT rating.
 
 If the bottom layer is a sublayer, then this property is rated the same as this sublayer's rating.
 
 If the bottom layer is a surface layer, then this property is rated SLIGHT if there is any SLIGHT surface layer rating, and it is rated SEVERE if there is any SEVERE surface layer rating.  Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.

The fuzzy space is defined as:

If the soil surface SAR is greater than 4 the evaluations becomes increasingly false and plant growth is adversely affected by excess sodium.

Missouri separated the rating of the topsoil and subsoil for this property. The national rule we started with gave higher ratings for surface soils with free carbonates that would render phosphorus insoluble. We used the logic that it is better to have the phosphorus stored in the subsoil and not have a high concentration at the surface where it is available for transport by runoff to the streams and lakes.

Soils with free carbonates at some depth below the surface layer will tie up the phosphorus. Missouri has some karst landscapes with skeletal soils.  It also has loosing streams and shallow depth to bedrock soils. It is favorable to have free carbonates in the subsoil tie up the phosphorus before it leaches down into the cave systems and cave streams. These caves and streams eventually supply surface water to our lakes and streams.

If the soil profile pH is greater than 5.5 and less than 8.5 then the soil surface is optimum for plant growth and the evaluation is nearly true.  Thus, slightly acid surface layers are optimal for plant growth but medium acid and neutral soils are also well suited for supporting plant growth.

If the soil profile pH is less than 5.5 or greater than 8.5 then the soil surface pH is not optimal for plant growth.  When the pH of the soil surface is more acid or alkaline then the optimum pH range, reduced availability of nutrients and the affects of heavy metals and salt concentrations limit plant growth.

evalname: BW and BC Available Water Capacity 0 to 150cm or first restr
evaldesc:
This evaluation checks the available water of the soil.  The weight average of the component horizon available_water_capacity is calculated for the soil and the result is check and evaluated.

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
 
  Where the total of each layers weighted average of the soil component horizon property available_water_capacity to a depth of 100cm (40in) is less than 5.0cm (2in) the evaluation is absolutely true and "DROUGHTY" is a restrictive feature.
     AND
  Where the total of each layers weighted average of the soil component horizon property available_water_capacity to a depth of 100cm (40in) is greater than 10cm (4in) the evaluation is absolutely false and "DROUGHTY" is not a restrictive feature.

Ames Description prior to  1996:
                                                                                            LIMITS                                RESTRICTIVE
     PROPERTY                                 |  SLIGHT  | MODERATE |  SEVERE  |  FEATURE
 9. 1/AVAILABLE WATER             >.10               .05-.10              <.05            DROUGHTY
      CAPACITY (IN/IN)                    
 
 1/Weighted average to 40 inches.
  
 Description of Calculation:
 
 The values given on the Soils-5 for available water are examined and a low value for each layer is determined.  The low value for each layer is used in a weighted average calculation to 40 inches.  Each low value used in the calculation depends on which of the following conditions is met first.
 
 If no data is entered, then the layer is skipped. 
 If the entry is of the form '<xx', then an artificial value of 0 is  used.
 
 Otherwise the low value is used.
 
 A separate weighted average to 40 inches is calculated for each surface layer and then rated.  If for some reason the total thickness used in the weighted average calculation is 0, then it is assumed that a weighted average of 1 was calculated.  If a weighted average could not be calculated due to missing data, then it is assumed that a weighted average of 100 was calculated.
 
      A weighted average < .05 gets a SEVERE rating.
      A weighted average >= .05 and < .10 gets a MODERATE rating.
      A weighted average >= .10 gets a SLIGHT rating.

 If there is a weighted average rating of SEVERE, then this property is rated SEVERE.  If there is a weighted average rating of MODERATE, then this property is rated MODERATE.  If there is a weighted average rating of SLIGHT, then this property is rated SLIGHT.  Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.

Growing season months are derived from the temperature regime of the soil component as follows:

taxonomic_temp_regime		growing season months
---------------------		---------------------
cryic, isofrigid, or pergelic	July and August

frigid or mesic			May, June, July, 
				August, and September

thermic or			March, April, May, 
hyperthermic			June, July, August,
				September, and October

isothermic,			February, March, April,
isohyperthermic,		May, June, July, August,
or isomesic			September, October, and
				November

evaldesc:
This evaluation checks percolation capacity of the soil.  The high, low, and representative values for sat_hydraulic_conductivity are selected for each horizon to a depth of 60 inches. 

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
  Where the soil horizon property sat_hydraulic_conductivity <= 4 micrometers/second (0.6 inches/hour), the evaluation is absolutely true and the restrictive feature is slow percolation.
        AND
  Where the soil horizon property sat_hydraulic_conductivity >= 42 micrometers/second (6.0 inches/hour), the evaluation is absolutely false and the restrictive feature is not slow percolation.

If no data is entered, thn an artificial default value(s) is used. 

Ames Description Prior to 1996:
 ___________________________________________________________________
                       |             LIMITS             |RESTRICTIVE
+                       ________________________________
     PROPERTY          |  SLIGHT  | MODERATE |  SEVERE  |  FEATURE
                       |          |          |          |
+___________________________________________________________________
 
 3. PERMEABILITY            >6      2.0-6.0     <2.0     PERCS
    (0-60", IN/HR)                                       SLOWLY
 
 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________
 
 The values given on the Soils-5 for permeability are examined and a low value for each layer is determined.  The low value used for low value for each layer is determined.  The low value used for first.
 
 If no data is entered, then an artificial value of 100 is used.
 
 If the entry is of the form '<xx', then an artificial value of 0 is used.
 
 Otherwise the low value is used.
 
 The layers within the given depths are examined.  The surface layers are each rated separately.  The lowest value found from all the sublayers is rated.  The rating algorithm used is as follows:
 
           A value < 2.0 gets a SEVERE rating.
           A value >= 2.0 and < 6.0 gets a MODERATE rating.
           A value >= 6.0 gets a SLIGHT rating.
 
 If the sublayer rating is SEVERE, then this property is rated SEVERE and no phasing will be done, regardless of the surface layer ratings.
 
 If the sublayer rating is MODERATE, then this property is rated MODERATE if there is any SLIGHT or MODERATE surface layer rating, and it is rated SEVERE if there is any SEVERE surface layer rating.  Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.
 
 If the sublayer rating is SLIGHT, then this property is rated SLIGHT if there is any SLIGHT surface layer rating, MODERATE if there is any MODERATE surface layer rating, and SEVERE if there is any SEVERE surface layer rating.  Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.
propname: KSAT MIN LOW, 0-150CM OR FIRST RESTRICTION

Growing season months are derived from the temperature regime of the soil component as follows:

taxonomic_temp_regime		growing season months
---------------------		---------------------
cryic, isofrigid, or pergelic	July and August

frigid or mesic			May, June, July, 
				August, and September

thermic or			March, April, May, 
hyperthermic			June, July, August,
				September, and October

isothermic,			February, March, April,
isohyperthermic,		May, June, July, August,
or isomesic			September, October, and
				November

This evaluation evaluates the product of the shrink-swell value of the thickest horizon in the 0 to 90cm range multiplied by the depth, in centimeters, of the thickest horizon.

Where the product of the shrink-swell value multiplied by the depth in centimeters is equal to or greater than 180 for the thickest layer between 0 to 60cm the evaluation is absolutely true and the restrictive feature is SHRINK-SWELL.
	AND
Where the product of the shrink-swell value multiplied by the depth in centimeters is equal to or less th 90 for the thickest layer between 0 to 90cm the evaluation is absolutely false and the restrictive feature is not SHRINK-SWELL.
propname: GRL-SHRINK-SWELL OF THICKEST LAYER IN DEPTH 0-90cm

propname: GRL-SHRINK-SWELL OF THICKEST LAYER IN DEPTH 0-90cm

evalname: GRL-Water Table, RV >75cm in Growing Season
evaldesc:
This evaluation looks at the condition: 
  Where the RV value of the soil property soil_moisture_depth_to_top is greater than 75cm AND the soil property soil_moisture_status is "wet" for any month corresponding to a "growing season month" as determined by the soil property taxonomic_temp_regime, the evaluation returns a value of 1.

Growing season months are derived from the temperature regime of the soil component as follows:

taxonomic_temp_regime	growing season months
---------------------	---------------------
cryic or pergelic	July and August

frigid or mesic		May, June, July, 
			August, and September

thermic or		March, April, May, 
hyperthermic		June, July, August,
			September, and October

isothermic,		February, March, April,
isohyperthermic,	May, June, July, August,
or isomesic		September, October, and
			November

evaldesc:
This evaluation looks at the condition:
    Where if in the soil surface layer coarse fragment (2mm to 10") is equal to or greater than 75 percent by weight (greater than 60% by volume, extremely gravelly or cobbly) then the soil surface is not optimum for plant growth and the evaluation returns a 1.


The conversion from weight to volume is from the "USDA SCS Chart for Estimating Rock Fragment Conversion & Textural Class Modifiers Related to Rock Fragments & Percent Passing No. 10 Sieve".

This evaluation looks at the condition:
   Where if in the soil surface layer coarse fragment (2mm to 10") is greater than 50 percent and less than 75 percent by weight (35 to 60% by volume, very gravelly or cobbly) then the soil surface is limited for plant growth and the evaluation returns a value of 1.


The conversion from weight to volume is from the "USDA SCS Chart for Estimating Rock Fragment Conversion & Textural Class Modifiers Related to Rock Fragments & Percent Passing No. 10 Sieve".

This evaluation checks the seepage potential of the soil.  The high, low, and representative values for sat_hydraulic_conductivity are selected for each horizon between 20 to 72 inches. 

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
  Where the soil horizon property sat_hydraulic_conductivity > 14 micrometers/second (2.0 inches/hr), the evaluaton is absolutely true and the restrictive feature is seepage.
        AND
  Where the soil horizon property sat_hydraulic_conductivity <= 1 micrometers/second (.2 inches/hour), the evaluation is absolutely false and the restrictive feature is not seepage.

If no data is entered, then an artificial default value(s) is used.

In 1990 the evaluation depth was extended from a base of 40 inches to a base of 60 inches.

Ames Description Prior to 1996

                                                               |                              LIMITS                           |  RESTRICTIVE
     PROPERTY                                  |  SLIGHT  | MODERATE |  SEVERE  |  FEATURE
 2. PERMEABILITY (IN/HR)             <0.6                0.6-2.0             >2.0               SEEPAGE
    (20-60")

 Description of Calculation:

 The values given on the Soils-5 for permeability are examined and a high value for each layer is determined.  The high value used for comparison depends on which of the following conditions is met first.

 If no data is entered, then an artificial value of 0 is used.

 If the entry is a single number or is of the form '<xx', then the  single value entered is used.

 If the entry is of the form '>xx', then an artificial value of 100  is used.

 Otherwise the high value is used.

 The layers within the given depths are examined.  If surface layers are included in these depths, each is rated separately.  Then each sublayer is rated to determine the worst sublayer rating.  The rating algorithm used on each layer is as follows:

           A value > 2.0 gets a SEVERE rating.
           A value > 0.6 and <= 2.0 gets a MODERATE rating.
           A value <= 0.6 gets a SLIGHT rating.

 If surface layers are not involved, then this property is rated the same as the worst sublayer rating.

 If surface layers are involved, then the following applies.  If the worst sublayer rating is SEVERE, then this property is rated SEVERE
 and no phasing will be done, regardless of the surface layer ratings.

 If the worst sublayer rating is MODERATE, then this property is rated MODERATE if there is any SLIGHT or MODERATE surface layer rating, and it is rated SEVERE if there is any SEVERE surface layer rating.  Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.

 If the worst sublayer rating is SLIGHT, then this property is rated SLIGHT if there is any SLIGHT surface layer rating, MODERATE if there is any MODERATE surface layer rating, and SEVERE if there is any SEVERE surface layer rating.  Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.

This evaluation is crisp and checks the maximum EC (salinity) between 25 and 150 cm.

The soil is a member of the set of soils that have high EC if the maximum salinity is more than 16 mmhos/cm.  The soil is not a member of this set if the salinity is 13 mmhos/cm or less.

This evaluation tests for salinity of the thickest layer within a depth of 25 to 150cm (10 to 60 inches).

Where the thickest layer salinity (ec) is greater than 16 mmhos the evaluation is absolutely true and "EXCESS SALT" is a restrictive feature.
     AND
Where the thickest layer salinity (ec) is less than 4 mmhos the evaluation is absolutely false and "EXCESS SALT" is  not a restrictive feature.

 inches are examined.  A high value is determined for each layer
 depending on which of the following conditions is met first.

evaldesc:

    AND

Growing season months are derived from the temperature regime of the soil component as follows:

taxonomic_temp_regime	growing season months
---------------------	---------------------
cryic or pergelic	July and August

frigid or mesic		May, June, July, 
			August, and September

thermic or		March, April, May, 
hyperthermic		June, July, August,
			September, and October

isothermic,		February, March, April,
isohyperthermic,	May, June, July, August,
or isomesic		September, October, and
			November
propname: AGR-DEPTH TO WATER TABLE DURING THE GROWING SEASON

evalname: Unified, PT OL OH (25 to 180cm) - MO2
evaldesc:
This evaluation is crisp and checks for UNIFIED equal to "OL", "OH", or "PT".

Where unified_soil_classification equals "OL", "OH", or "PT" the evaluation is absolutely true and EXCESS HUMUS is a restrictive feature.
    AND
Where unified_soil_classification does not equal "OL", "OH", or "PT" the evaluation is absolutely false and EXCESS HUMUS is not a restrictive feature.

 Ames prior to 1996

                                                |                           LIMITS                              |  RESTRICTIVE
     PROPERTY                   |  SLIGHT  | MODERATE |  SEVERE  |  FEATURE
 8. UNIFIED (10-72")         ---                ---               OL, OH, PT   EXCESS HUMUS
 
 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________
 
 The unified values given on the Soils-5 are examined for the layers within 10-72 inches.  If surface layers are included in these depths, each is rated separately.  Then each sublayer is rated to determine the worst sublayer rating.  The rating algorithm used on each layer is as follows:
 
 If OL, OH, or PT is listed as a texture, then a SEVERE rating is given.
 Otherwise a SLIGHT rating is given.
 
 If surface layers are not involved, then this property is rated the same as the worst sublayer rating.
 
 If surface layers are involved, then the following applies.  If the worst sublayer rating is SEVERE, then this property is rated SEVERE and no phasing will be done, regardless of the surface layer ratings.
 
 
 If the worst sublayer rating is SLIGHT, then this property is rated SLIGHT if there is any SLIGHT surface layer rating, and it is rated SEVERE if there is any SEVERE surface layer rating.  Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
  Where the soil property unified_soil_classification equals GM or SM in the thickest layer between 25 and 150 cm from the soil surface, the evaluation returns a value of 1.  The "multiply" factor will be used to assign a value of 0.9.

This evaluation is crisp and checks for UNIFIED equal to "MH" or "CH".

Where unified_soil_classification equals "MH" or "CH" the evaluation is absolutely true and EXCESS HUMUS is a restrictive feature.
    AND
Where unified_soil_classification does not equal "MH" or"CH" the evaluation is absolutely false and EXCESS HUMUS is not a restrictive feature.

 Ames prior to 1996

                                                |                           LIMITS                                       |  RESTRICTIVE
     PROPERTY     |  SLIGHT  | MODERATE |  SEVERE  |  FEATURE
 8. UNIFIED (10-60")                         MH, CH    HARD TO PACK            
 
 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________
 
 The unified values given on the Soils-5 are examined for the layers within 10-60 inches.  If surface layers are included in these depths, each is rated separately.  Then each sublayer is rated to determine the worst sublayer rating.  The rating algorithm used on each layer is as follows:
 
 If MH or CH is listed as Unified, then a SEVERE rating is given.
 Otherwise a SLIGHT rating is given.
 
 If surface layers are not involved, then this property is rated the same as the worst sublayer rating.
 
 If surface layers are involved, then the following applies.  If the worst sublayer rating is SEVERE, then this property is rated SEVERE and no phasing will be done, regardless of the surface layer ratings.
 
 
 If the worst sublayer rating is SLIGHT, then this property is rated SLIGHT if there is any SLIGHT surface layer rating, and it is rated SEVERE if there is any SEVERE surface layer rating.  Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
  Where the soil property unified_soil_classification equals "SP", "SW", "SP-SM", "SW-SM", "GP". "GW", "GP-GM", or "GW-GM" in the thickest layer between 25 and 150 cm from the soil surface, the evaluation returns a value of 1.

Description of Calculation:

 The layer with the most inches between 10 and 60 inches is determined.  This could be a surface layer or a sublayer.  The unified values given on the Soils-5 are examined for the appropriate layer(s).

 Otherwise a GOOD rating is given.

 If the thickest layer is a surface layer, then this property is rated GOOD if there is any GOOD surface layer rating, and it is rated POOR if there is any POOR surface layer rating.  If minerology on the Soils-5 equals '28' (Kaolinitic), then a POOR rating is upgraded to FAIR.  Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.

This evaluation check percolation capacity of the soil.  The high, low, and representative values for sat_hydraulic_conductivity are selected for each horizon to a depth of 60 inches. 

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
  Where the soil horizon property sat_hydraulic_conductivity <= 0.4 micrometers/second (0.06 inches/hour)the evaluation is absolutely true and the restrictive feature is slow percolation.
        AND
  Where the soil horizon property sat_hydraulic_conductivity => 4.0 micrometers/second (0.60 inches/hour) the evaluation is absolutely false and the restrictive feature is not slow percolation.

If no data is entered, thn an artificial default value(s) is used. 

Ames Description Prior to 1996:

                                                           |                            LIMITS                             |  RESTRICTIVE
     PROPERTY                              |  SLIGHT  | MODERATE |  SEVERE  |  FEATURE
 7. 27/PERMEABILITY                    >0.6              0.06-0.6           <0.06          PERCS SLOWLY
    (IN/HR) (0-40")  

 27/Soils in UST, TOR, ARID, BOR, or XER suborders, great groups, or subgroups, rate one class better.

 Description of Calculation:

 The values given on the Soils-5 for permeability are examined and a low value for each layer is determined.  The low value used for comparison depends on which of the following conditions is met first.

 If no data is entered, then an artificial value of 100 is used.

evalname: WLF - USDA Texture Class, in lieu of, Surface: FB, HM, MPT
evaldesc:
This evaluation is crisp and checks for the presences of Excess Humus in the soil profile.   The terms_terms_used_in-lieu_of_texture are examined for the surface layer. 

Where terms_used_in_lieu_of_texture equals fb, hm, or mpt for the surface layer the evaluation is absolutely true and the restrictive feature is excess humus.
    AND
Where terms_used_in_lieu_of_texture does not equal fb, hm, or mpt, or is NULL for the surface layer the evaluation is absolutely false and the restrictive feature is not excess humus.

evaldesc:
This evaluation checks the clay activity of the soil's upper 50 cm (20 inches).  The component horizon  cation_exch_capcty_nh4oacph7 is divided by clay_total_separate and the result is check and evaluated.

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
 
  Where the result of the soil component horizon property cation_exch_capcty_nh4oacph7 divided by clay_total_separate between 0 and 50 cm (20 in) is less than 0.05 the evaluation is absolutely true and "LOW ADSORPTION" is a restrictive feature.
     AND
  Where the result of the soil component horizon property cation_exch_capcty_nh4oacph7 divided by clay_total_separate between 0 and 50 cm (20 in) is greater than 0.15 the evaluation is absolutely false and "LOW ADSORPTION" is not a restrictive feature.

Ames Description prior to  1996:
___________________________________________________________________
                       |             LIMITS             |RESTRICTIVE
+                       ________________________________
     PROPERTY          |  SLIGHT  | MODERATE |  SEVERE  |  FEATURE
                       |          |          |          |
+___________________________________________________________________
 
 11. CLAY ACTIVITY         >.15     .05-.15      <.05    LOW
     (CEC/CLAY, WEIGHTED                                 ADSORPTION
     AVERAGE TO 20")
 
 
 
 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________
 
 The values given on the Soils-5 for clay and CEC are examined and an
 average of the low and high values is found for both.
 
 Clay:
+_____
 
 If no data is entered, then the layer is skipped.
 
 If the entry is a single number, then the single value entered is used as the average.
 
 If the entry is of the form '<xx', then the average is taken using
 
 
 If the entry is of the form '>xx', then the average is taken using xx and 99.
 
 CEC:
+____
 
 If no data is entered, then the layer is skipped.
 
 If the entry is a single number, then the single value entered is used as the average.
 
 If the entry is of the form '<xxx', then the average is taken using 0 and xxx.
 
 If the entry is of the form '>xxx', then the average is taken using xxx and 200.
 
 
 After each average is found for a layer, the clay activity is calculated.  Clay Activity = CEC ave. / Clay ave.
 
 A separate weighted average to 20 inches is calculated for each surface layer using the values for clay activity.
 
     A weighted average < .05 gets a SEVERE rating.
     A weighted average >= .05 and <= .15 gets a MODERATE rating.
     A weighted average > .15 gets a SLIGHT rating.
 
 Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.

 NOTE:  If all layers on the Soils-5 are missing CEC entries, the component is flagged in the final output table.

If the soil's surface bulk density is high then surface condition for plant growth is not optimum.

The fuzzy space is defined as:

If the soil's bulk density is < 1.2 then the root zone is optimum for plant growth and the evaluation is absolutely true and "ROOT EXTENSION" is not a restrictive feature.

If the soil's bulk density is => 2.0 then the root zone is not optimum for plant growth and the evaluation is absolutely false and "ROOT EXTENSION" is a restrictive feature.

If the soil is not ponded, then the asumption is that ponding_duration_class is NULL.

The evaluation checks surface horizon coarse fragments greater then 2mm and indexes the degree to which coarse fragments resist rutting.  Where the soil property "FRAGMENTS > 2mm SURFACE LAYER (TX)" is:

	 => 65 the soil is optimum and suitability is expressed as the number 1.0.
	  > 5 and < 65 the soil is less then optimum and suitability is expressed as a number between 0 and 1.0.
	 =< 5 the soil is not optimum and suitability is expressed as the number 0.

This evaluation checks the percent by weight > 2mm for the surface layer.

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:

  When the surface weight % > 2mm is between 25 and 50%, the evaluation returns a value between 0 and 1.
 
  Where the wght % > 2mm is more than 50% the evaluation returns a value of 1, the rule is absolutely true, and TOO GRAVELLY, TOO COBBLY, OR TOO STONY is a restrictive feature.
   OR
  Where the wght % > 2mm is less than 25 the evaluation returns a value of 0, the rule is absolutely false, TOO GRAVELLY, etc. is not a restrictive feature.

The evaluation checks surface horizon coarse fragments greater then 2mm and indexes the degree to which coarse fragments are limiting.  Where the soil property "FRAGMENTS > 2mm SURFACE LAYER (TX)" is:

	 => 100 the soil is limited and the degree of limitation is expressed as the number 1.0.
	  > 50 and < 100 the soil is somewhat limited and the degree of limitation is expressed as a number between 0 and 1.0.
	 =< 50 the soil is not limited and the degree of limitation is expressed as the number 0.

The evaluation checks surface horizon coarse fragments greater then 2mm and indexes the degree to which coarse fragments are limiting.  Where the soil property "FRAGMENTS > 2mm SURFACE LAYER (TX)" is:

	 => 50 the soil is limited and the degree of limitation is expressed as the number 1.0.
	  > 25 and < 50 the soil is somewhat limited and the degree of limitation is expressed as a number between 0 and 1.0.
	 =< 25 the soil is not limited and the degree of limitation is expressed as the number 0.

The evaluation checks surface horizon coarse fragments greater then 2mm and indexes the degree to which coarse fragments are limiting.  Where the soil property "FRAGMENTS > 2mm SURFACE LAYER (TX)" is:

	 => 75 the soil is limited and the degree of limitation is expressed as the number 1.0.
	  > 50 and < 75 the soil is somewhat limited and the degree of limitation is expressed as a number between 0 and 1.0.
	 =< 75 the soil is not limited and the degree of limitation is expressed as the number 0.

The evaluation checks surface horizon coarse fragments greater then 2mm and indexes the degree to which coarse fragments restist wind erosion.  Where the soil property "FRAGMENTS > 2mm SURFACE LAYER (TX)" is:

This evaluation checks percolation capacity of the soil.  The high, low, and representative values for the maximum  sat_hydraulic_conductivity are selected for each horizon to a depth of 62 inches (155 cm) or to the first restrictive layer above a depth of 62 inches. 

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
  Where the soil horizon property sat_hydraulic_conductivity <= 4 micrometers/second (0.6 inches/hour), the evaluation is absolutely true, returns a value of 1, and the restrictive feature is too slow percolation.
        OR
  Where the soil horizon property sat_hydraulic_conductivity >= 42 micrometers/second (6.0 inches/hour), the evaluation is absolutely true, returns a value of 1, and the restrictive feature is too rapid percolation.

If the soil horizon property sat_hydraulic_conductivity is >4 or <42, the conditions for plant growth are optimum, and the soil is not limited with too slow or too fast percolation and the evaluation returns a value between 1 and 0.

If no data is entered, then an artificial default value(s) is used.
