 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________
 
 The values given on the Soils-5 for permeability are examined and a low value for each layer is determined.  The low value used for low value for each layer is determined.  The low value used for first.
 
 If no data is entered, then an artificial value of 100 is used.
 
 If the entry is of the form '<xx', then an artificial value of 0 is used.
 
 Otherwise the low value is used.
 
 The layers within the given depths are examined.  The surface layers are each rated separately.  The lowest value found from all the sublayers is rated.  The rating algorithm used is as follows:
 
           A value < 2.0 gets a SEVERE rating.
           A value >= 2.0 and < 6.0 gets a MODERATE rating.
           A value >= 6.0 gets a SLIGHT rating.
 
 If the sublayer rating is SEVERE, then this property is rated SEVERE and no phasing will be done, regardless of the surface layer ratings.
 
 If the sublayer rating is MODERATE, then this property is rated MODERATE if there is any SLIGHT or MODERATE surface layer rating, and it is rated SEVERE if there is any SEVERE surface layer rating.  Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.
 
 If the sublayer rating is SLIGHT, then this property is rated SLIGHT if there is any SLIGHT surface layer rating, MODERATE if there is any MODERATE surface layer rating, and SEVERE if there is any SEVERE surface layer rating.  Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.

evaldesc:
This evaluation is crisp and checks the texture_class for all layers above any restrictive layer. 
 
Where texture_class equals SIC, C, SICL, CL, or SC for any layer above a restrictive layer the evaluation is absolutely true and the restrictive feature is TOO CLAYEY.
    AND
Where texture_class does not equal SICL, CL,  SC, or IS NULL for any layer above a restrictive layer the evaluation is absolutely false and the restrictive feature is not TOO CLAYEY.

 Ames Description prior to 1996: 
                                        |                      LIMITS                                |    RESTRICTIVE
     PROPERTY           |   GOOD   |         FAIR       |     POOR     |    FEATURE

    TEXTURE                                             SC

 4/Disregard (1) in all Aridisols except Salorthids and Aquic subgroups, (2) all Aridic subgroups, and (3) all Torri great groups of Entisols except Aquic subgroups.

 5/If in Kaolinitic family, rate one class better if experience confirms.

 6/Thickest layer between 0 and 30 inches.

 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________

 If not disregarded, the layer with the most inches between 10 and 60 inches is determined.  This could be a surface layer or a sublayer. The textures given on the Soils-5 are examined for the appropriate layer(s).

 The layer(s) being examined are rated according to the following algorithm:

 If SIC or C is listed as a texture, then a POOR rating is given. If CL, SICL, or SC is listed as a texture, then a FAIR rating is  given. Otherwise a GOOD rating is given.

 If the thickest layer is a sublayer, then this property is rated the same as this sublayer's rating.  If minerology on the Soils-5 equals '28' (Kaolinitic), then a FAIR rating is upgraded to GOOD, and a POOR rating is upgraded to FAIR.

 If the thickest layer is a surface layer, then this property is rated GOOD if there is any GOOD surface layer rating, FAIR if there is any FAIR surface layer rating, and POOR if there is any POOR surface layer rating.  If minerology on the Soils-5 equals '28' (Kaolinitic), then a FAIR rating is upgraded to GOOD, and a POOR rating is upgraded to FAIR.  Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.

evalname: WLF - Bulk Density Depth to >1.8 g/cc, 50-25cm (20-10")
evaldesc:
The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:

  Where the depth to the first horizon where the bulk density is
> 1.8 G/CC is less than 20" (50cm) and greater than 10" (25cm), the evaluation returns a value between 0 and 1.

    When the depth is < 10" (25cm), the evaluation returns a value of 1, the rule is absolutely true, and DENSE LAYER is a restrictive feature.

   When the depth is > 20" (50cm), the evaluation returns a value of 0, the rule is absolutely false, and DENSE LAYER is not a restrictive feature.

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:

When the frag3to10 in the thickest layer in 0-30" (0-75cm) is less than 25% but greater than 10%, the evaluation returns a value between 0 and 1.
   
If the frag3to 10 in the thickest layer between 0 and 75 cm is >25 the evaluation returns 1, the rule is absolutely true, and ROCK FRAGMENTS is a restrictive feature.

If the frag3to10 value in the thickest layer in 0-75cm is <10%, then the evaluation returns 0, the rule is absolutely false, and ROCK FRAGMENTS is not a restrictive feature.

The criteria at Ames is as follows:

 ___________________________________________________________________
                       |             LIMITS             |RESTRICTIVE
                        ________________________________
     PROPERTY          |   GOOD   |   FAIR   |   POOR   |  FEATURE
                       |          |          |          |
 ___________________________________________________________________

   6/PERCENT BY WEIGHT    <10        10-25        >25     ROCK
     >3"(THICKEST LAYER                                   FRAGMENTS
     LAYER, 0-30")                               
                                                
 6/Thickest layer between 0 and 30 inches.

evalname: WLF - Unified: OH/PT 0-100cm for excess humus
evaldesc:
The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
  Where the soil property unified_soil_classification equals "OH" or "PT" in a layer between 0 and 100 cm (40") from the soil surface, the evaluation returns a value of 1.

The evaluation as written in Ames is as follows:
 ___________________________________________________________________
                       |             LIMITS             |RESTRICTIVE
                        ________________________________
     PROPERTY          |   GOOD   |   FAIR   |   POOR   |  FEATURE
                       |          |          |          |
 ___________________________________________________________________

       UNIFIED             ---        ---       OH,PT    EXCESS
                                                         HUMUS




 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________

 The layer with the most inches between 10 and 60 inches is
 determined.  This could be a surface layer or a sublayer.  The
 unified values given on the Soils-5 are examined for the appropriate
 layer(s).

 The layer(s) being examined are rated according to the following
 algorithm:

 If OH or PT is listed as a unified entry, then a POOR rating is given.
 Otherwise a GOOD rating is given.

 If the thickest layer is a sublayer, then this property is rated the
 same as this sublayer's rating.

 If the thickest layer is a surface layer, then this property is
 rated GOOD if there is any GOOD surface layer rating, and it is
 rated POOR if there is any POOR surface layer rating.  Phasing will
 be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.

This evaluation checks the filtering capacity of the soil.  The high, low, and representative values for the minimum permeability are selected for each horizon between depths of 50 to 150 cm. 

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:

  Where the minimum permeability is > 1.4 micrometers/second (.20 inches/hr), the evaluation is absolutely true and the restrictive feature is seepage.

  Where the permeability is < .42 micrometers/sec (0.06"/hr), the evaluation is absolutely false and SEEPAGE is not a restrictive feature.
 
If no data is entered, then an artificial default value(s) is used.

Ames Description Prior to 1996
 ___________________________________________________________________
                       |             LIMITS             |RESTRICTIVE
                        ________________________________
     PROPERTY          |  SLIGHT  | MODERATE |  SEVERE  |  FEATURE
                       |          |          |          |
 _________________________________________________________________

 5. 4/PERMEABILITY        >0.2      0.2-0.06    <0.06     PERCS
      (IN/HR) (10-40")                                    SLOWLY

 4/Disregard (1) in all Aridisols except Salorthids and Aquic  subgroups, (2) all Aridic subgroups, and (3) all Torri great   groups of Entisols except Aquic subgroups.

 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________

 If not disregarded, the values given on the Soils-5 for permeability are examined and a high value for each layer is determined.  The high value used for comparison depends on which of the following conditions is met first.

 If no data is entered, then an artificial value of 0 is used.
 If the entry is a single number or is of the form '<xx', then the  single value entered is used.

 If the entry is of the form '>xx', then an artificial value of 100  is used.

 Otherwise the high value is used.

 The layers within the given depths are examined.  If surface layers are included in these depths, each is rated separately.  Then each sublayer is rated to determine the worst sublayer rating.  The rating algorithm used on each layer is as follows:

           A value <0.06 gets a POORLY SUITED rating.
           A value 0.2-0.06 gets a SUITED rating.
           A value > 0.2 gets a WELL SUITED rating.

 If surface layers are not involved, then this property is rated the same as the worst sublayer rating.

 If surface layers are involved, then the following applies.  If the worst sublayer rating is SEVERE, then this property is rated SEVERE and no phasing will be done, regardless of the surface layer ratings.

This evaluation checks for the presence of salt in the soil's 0-100cm depth.  The component horizon electrical_conductivity data are checked and evaluated.

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
 
  Where the maximum soil component horizon property electrical_conductivity in 0-100cm is greater than 8mmhos/cm then the evaluation is absolutely true and "EXCESS SALT" is a restrictive feature.
     AND
  Where the maximum soil component horizon property electrical_conductivity in 0-100cm is less than 4mmhos/cm then the evaluation is absolutely false and "EXCESS SALT" is not a restrictive feature.


Ames Description prior to  1996:
 ___________________________________________________________________
                       |             LIMITS             |RESTRICTIVE
+                       ________________________________
     PROPERTY          |  SLIGHT  | MODERATE |  SEVERE  |  FEATURE

+___________________________________________________________________
 
 13. SALINITY (MMHOS/CM)    <4        4-8        >8     EXCESS SALT
     (0-100cm)
 
 
 
 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________
 
 The values given on the Soils-5 for salinity are examined for each surface layer.  A high value is determined for each surface layer depending on which of the following conditions is met first.
 
 If the entry is a normal range, then the high value is used.
 
 If the entry is of the form '>xx', then an artificial value of 99 is used.
 
 Otherwise an artificial value of 0 is used.
 
 The maximum value over all surface layers is determined.
 
        A maximum value > 8 gets a SEVERE rating.
        A maximum value > 4 and <= 8 gets a MODERATE rating.
        A maximum value <= 4 gets a SLIGHT rating.

This evaluation checks the greater than 3 inch fraction of the soil.  The weighted average of the component horizon rock_frag_3_to_10_in and rock_frag_greater_than_10_in is calculated for the 0 to 180 cm (72in) depth of the soil and the result is checked and evaluated.

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
 
  Where the total of each layers weighted average of the soil component horizon properties rock_frag_3_to_10_in and rock_frag_greater_than_10_in from 0 to a depth of 150cm (60in) is greater than 50% the evaluation is absolutely true and "LARGE STONES" is a restrictive feature.
     AND
  Where the total of each layers weighted average of the soil component horizon properties rock_frag_3_to_10_in and rock_frag_greater_than_10_in from 0 to a depth of 150cm (60in) less than 25% the evaluation is absolutely false and "LARGE STONES" is not a restrictive feature.

If no data is entered, then a default value of 0 is used.

This evaluation checks for the weighted average of rock size fragments between 0 and 180cm.

A soil can be a complete or partial member of the set of soils that are limited by the presence of rock sized fragments and CONTENT OF LARGE STONES is the set's restrictive feature.  If the content of rock size fragments is greater than 50%, then the soil is a complete member of the set.  If the content of rock size fragments is greater then 25% and less then 50% then the soil is a partial member of the set.  A soil that has content of rock size fragments less then 25%  is not a member of the set.

This evaluation checks for the weighted average of gravel size particles between 0 and 150cm.

A soil can be a complete or partial member of the set of soils that are limited by the presence of gravel sized particles and GRAVEL CONTENT is the set's restrictive feature.  If the content of gravel size particles is greater than 50%, then the soil is a complete member of the set.  If the content of gravel size particles is greater then 25% and less then 50% then the soil is a partial member of the set.  A soil that has content of gravel size particles less then 25%  is not a member of the set.

This evaluation checks the weighted average of the greater than 2mm and less than 75mm fraction of the soil. 

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
 
  Where the weighted average of the soil component coarse fragment property between 2 and 75mm is greater than 50% the evaluation is absolutely true and "SMALL STONES" is a restrictive feature.
     AND
  Where the weighted average of the soil component coarse fragment property between 2 and 75mm is less than 25% the evaluation is absolutely false and "SMALL STONES" is not a restrictive feature.

Fuzzy zone: 25-50% by weight

This evaluation checks for the presence of bedrock within a specified depth.  The component data are check for restriction_kind = "bedrock (lithic)" or "bedrock (paralithic)" and restriction_depth_to_top is evaluated.

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
  Where the soil component property restriction_kind = "bedrock (lithic)" or "bedrock (paralithic)" and the restriction_depth_to_top is less then 50 cm (20 inches) then the evaluation is absolutely true and depth to bedrock is a restrictive feature.
     AND
  Where the soil component property restriction_kind = "bedrock (lithic)" or "bedrock (paralithic)" and the restriction_depth_to_top is greater then 76 cm (30 inches) then the evaluation is absolutely false and depth to bedrock is not a restrictive feature.

 If the entry is '>60', then an artificial value of 100 is used.
 
 If the low value is valid, then the low value is used.
 
 Otherwise an artificial value of 100 is used.
 
           A value < 20 gets a SEVERE rating.
           A value >= 20 and < 30 gets a MODERATE rating.
           A value >= 30 gets a SLIGHT rating.

This evaluation checks the available water of the soil.  The weighted average of the component horizon available_water_capacity is calculated for the soil and the result is checked and evaluated.

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
 
  Where the total of each layers weighted average of the soil component horizon property available_water_capacity to a depth of 100cm (40in) is less than 10.0cm (4in) the evaluation is absolutely true and "DROUGHTY" is a restrictive feature, the evaluation returns a value of 1.
     AND
  Where the total of each layers weighted average of the soil component horizon property available_water_capacity to a depth of 100cm (40in) is greater than 15cm (6in) the evaluation is absolutely false and "DROUGHTY" is not a restrictive feature, and the evaluation returns a value of 0.  If the available_water_capacity is equal to or greater than 10cm and equal to or less than 15cm, the evaluation returns a value greater than 0 and less than 1.

 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________
 
 The values given for available water are examined and a low value for each layer is determined.  The low value for each layer is used in a weighted average calculation to 40 inches.  Each low value used in the calculation depends on which of the following conditions is met first.
 
 If no data is entered, then the layer is skipped.
 
 If the entry is of the form '<xx', then an artificial value of 0 is  used.
 
 Otherwise the low value is used.
 
 A separate weighted average to 40 inches is calculated for each surface layer and then rated.  If for some reason the total thickness used in the weighted average calculation is 0, then it is assumed that a weighted average of 1 was calculated.  If a weighted average could not be calculated due to missing data, then it is assumed that a weighted average of 100 was calculated.

evalname: Available Water Capacity 0 to 50 cm (0 to 20in)
evaldesc:
This evaluation checks the available water of the soil.  The weight average of the component horizon available_water_capacity is calculated for the soil and the result is check and evaluated.

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
 
  Where the total of each layers weighted average of the soil component horizon property available_water_capacity to a depth of 50cm (20in) is less than 5.0cm (2in) the evaluation is absolutely true and "DROUGHTY" is a restrictive feature.
     AND
  Where the total of each layers weighted average of the soil component horizon property available_water_capacity to a depth of 50cm (20in) is greater than 7.6cm (3in) the evaluation is absolutely false and "DROUGHTY" is not a restrictive feature.

Ames Description prior to  1996:
 1___________________________________________________________________
 
+                       ________________________________
     PROPERTY          |  SLIGHT  | MODERATE |  SEVERE  |  FEATURE
                       |          |          |          |
+___________________________________________________________________
 
 9. 1/AVAILABLE WATER                                    DROUGHTY
      CAPACITY (IN/IN)    >.10      .05-.10      <.05
 
 1/Weighted average to 40 inches.
  
 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________
 
 The values given on the Soils-5 for available water are examined and a low value for each layer is determined.  The low value for each layer is used in a weighted average calculation to 40 inches.  Each low value used in the calculation depends on which of the following conditions is met first.
 
 If no data is entered, then the layer is skipped.
 
 If the entry is of the form '<xx', then an artificial value of 0 is  used.
 
 Otherwise the low value is used.
 
 A separate weighted average to 40 inches is calculated for each surface layer and then rated.  If for some reason the total thickness used in the weighted average calculation is 0, then it is assumed that a weighted average of 1 was calculated.  If a weighted average could not be calculated due to missing data, then it is assumed that a weighted average of 100 was calculated.
 
      A weighted average < .05 gets a SEVERE rating.
      A weighted average >= .05 and < .10 gets a MODERATE rating.
      A weighted average >= .10 gets a SLIGHT rating.

 If there is a weighted average rating of SEVERE, then this property is rated SEVERE.  If there is a weighted average rating of MODERATE, then this property is rated MODERATE.  If there is a weighted average rating of SLIGHT, then this property is rated SLIGHT.  Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.

evaldesc:
This crisp evaluation checks if the K-factor for the Surface Layer is > 0.35.  It returns a value of 1 if so.  Otherwise, it returns 0.

Ames Description Prior to 1996:

                                                           |                           LIMITS                              |  RESTRICTIVE
     PROPERTY                              |  SLIGHT  | MODERATE |  SEVERE  |  FEATURE
 8. EROSION FACTOR (K)            ---                 ---                31/ >.35      ERODES EASILY
    (SURFACE LAYER)

 31/Disregard on slopes of 8% or less.

 Description of Calculation:

 First, a check is made for footnote 31 on whether or not to disregard this property.  The slope range given on the Soils-5 is examined.  If the high slope <= 8, then this property is disregarded.  Otherwise the following calculations occur.

 The values given on the Soils-5 for K erosion factor are examined for each surface layer.  A value is determined for each surface layer depending on which of the following conditions is met first.

 If valid data is entered, then that value is used.

 If no data is entered, then an artificial value of 0 is used.

 The surface layers are each rated separately using the following algorithm:
           A value > .35 gets a SEVERE rating.
           A value <= .35 gets a SLIGHT rating.

 If there is a surface layer with a SEVERE rating, then this property
 is rated SEVERE.  If there is a surface layer with a SLIGHT rating,
 then this property is rated SLIGHT.  Phasing will be done using
 texture terms if more than one rating is given.
propname: EROSION FACTOR FIRST LAYER NOT ORGANIC

Evaluates surface pH for hard clams.

Soil Reaction Class (pH)
Calabrese (1972) observed that hard clams require that the pH of estuarine waters not fall below pH 7.0; that there was no significant decrease in clams within the pH range of 7.0 to 8.75; but that numbers of clams dropped significantly at pH 9.0. Normal growth for hard clams was seen at pH 6.8 to 8.5. Still (2017) identified shellfish shell dissolution stress at a soil pH as high as 7.6.

Soil Reaction Class: pH 
(surface layer)	
highly suitable
pH 7.5 to pH 8.5	
suitable
pH 6.8 to 7.4
pH 8.6 to 8.8
not suitable
< pH 6.8; > pH 8.8	 

References: Still, 2017; Calabrese, 1972

evaldesc:
This evaluation is crisp and checks the texture_modifier for the surface layer. 
 
Where texture_modifier equals VERY or EXTREMELY Gravelly for the surface layer the evaluation is absolutely true,
    AND
Where texture_modifier does not equal VERY or EXTREMELY Gravelly, or is NULL for the surface layer the evaluation is absolutely false.

This evaluation is crisp and checks the texture_modifier for the surface layer. 
 
Where texture_modifier equals VERY bouldery, cobbly, channery, flaggy, or stony for either para or lithic rocks for the surface layer the evaluation is absolutely true and the restrictive feature is EXCESS ROCKS.
    AND
Where texture_modifier does not equal  VERY bouldery, cobbly, channery, flaggy,  or stony, or is NULL for the surface layer the evaluation is absolutely false and the restrictive feature is not EXCESS STONES.

evalname: Shrink-swell of Thickest Layer in 25-150cm or Bedrock
evaldesc:
This evaluation evaluates the product of the shrink-swell value of the thickest horizon in the 25 to 150cm range.

If the shrink-swell value for the thickest layer between 25-150cm is between 3 and 6, the evaluation returns a value between 0 and 1.

When the shrink-swell value for the thickest layer between 25 to 150cm is > 6 (HIGH or VERY HIGH) the evaluation is absolutely true and the restrictive feature is SHRINK-SWELL.
	AND
When the shrink-swell value for the thickest layer between 25 to 150cm is <3 (LOW), the evaluation is absolutely false and the restrictive feature is not SHRINK-SWELL.


Ames Description Prior to 1996:
                                                      |                            LIMITS                                       |  RESTRICTIVE
     PROPERTY                         |  SLIGHT  | MODERATE |  SEVERE            |  FEATURE
 
 9. 9/SHRINK-SWELL         LOW             MODERATE      HIGH,                  SHRINK-
                                                                                                              VERY HIGH       SWELL
 
 9/Thickest layer between 10 and 60 inches.
 
 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________
 
 The layer with the most inches between 10 and 60 inches is determined.  This could be a surface layer or a sublayer.  The shrink-swell values given on the Soils-5 are examined for the appropriate layer(s).
 
 The layer(s) being examined are rated according to the following algorithm:
 
 If the shrink-swell value equals '1' (HIGH) or '5' (VERY HIGH), then a SEVERE rating is given.  If the shrink-swell value equals '3' (MODERATE), then a MODERATE rating is given. Otherwise a SLIGHT rating is given.
 
 If the thickest layer is a sublayer, then this property is rated the same as this sublayer's rating.
 
 If the thickest layer is a surface layer, then this property is rated SLIGHT if there is any SLIGHT surface layer rating, MODERATE if there is any MODERATE surface layer rating, and SEVERE if there is any SEVERE surface layer rating.  Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.
propname: SHRINK-SWELL THICKEST LAYER  25-150cm OR ABOVE ROCK

  Where the result of the soil component surface horizon property rock_frag_3_to_10_in is greater than 35 percent by weight the evaluation is absolutely true and "TOO COBBLY" is a restrictive feature.
     AND
  Where the result of the soil component surface horizon property rock_frag_3_to_10_in is less than 15 percent by weight the evaluation is absolutely false and "TOO COBBLY" is not a restrictive feature.

___________________________________________________________________
                       |             LIMITS             |RESTRICTIVE
+                       ________________________________
     PROPERTY          |  SLIGHT  | MODERATE |  SEVERE  |  FEATURE
                       |          |          |          |
+___________________________________________________________________
 
 13a. WEIGHT PERCENT 3-10" <15       15-35       >35     TOO COBBLY
 
 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________
 
 The values given on the Soils-5 for fraction 3-10 inches are examined and a high value for each layer is determined.  The high value used in the calculation depends on which of the following conditions is met first.
 
 If a single value of '99' is entered, then an artificial value of  100 is used.
 
 If a single value not equal to '99' is entered, then an artificial  value of 0 is used.
 
 Otherwise the high value is used.
 
 A separate weighted average is calculated for each surface layer.
 
       A weighted average > 35 gets a SEVERE rating.
       A weighted average > 15 and <= 35 gets a MODERATE rating.
       A weighted average <= 15 gets a SLIGHT rating.
 
 Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.

This evaluation checks the available water of the soil.  The weight average of the component horizon available_water_capacity is calculated for the soil and the result is check and evaluated.

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
 
  Where the total of each layers weighted average of the soil component horizon property available_water_capacity to a depth of 150cm (60in) is less than 7.5 cm (3 in) the evaluation is absolutely true and "DROUGHTY" is a restrictive feature.
     AND
  Where the total of each layers weighted average of the soil component horizon property available_water_capacity to a depth of 150cm (60in) is greater than 15 cm (6 in) the evaluation is absolutely false and "DROUGHTY" is not a restrictive feature.

     (WEIGHT AVE, 0 TO 60")
  
 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________
 
 The values given on the Soils-5 for available water are examined and
 
 If no data is entered, then the layer is skipped.
 
 If the entry is a single number, then the single value entered is used as the average.
 
 If the entry is of the form '<xxxx', then the average is taken using 0 and xxxx.
 
 Otherwise the low value is used.
 
 
 A separate total is calculated for each surface layer and then rated.  The total is the sum of each layer's average value times the number of inches in the layer for layers up to 60".

    AND

This evaluation calculates the thickest layer from the surface to 150cm or a restrictive layer.

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
     Where the thickness of the thickest layer  is greater  than 150cm (60 in) the evaluation is absolutely true and "THIN LAYER" is not a restrictive feature.
    AND
    Where the thickness of the thickest layer  is less than 75cm (30 in) the evaluation is absolutely false and "THIN LAYER" is a restrictive feature.

Current version contains major  revisions to the Ames 1996 version.

Ames prior to 1996

1___________________________________________________________________
                                                       |             LIMITS                                                   |RESTRICTIVE
+                                                    ________________________________
     PROPERTY                          |   GOOD   |   FAIR     |   POOR                         |  FEATURE
 +___________________________________________________________________

 6. LAYER THICKNESS        >60               30-60          <30                                THIN LAYER
    (IN)

 These calculations are done only if the thickest layer ratings for Property Nos. 4 and 5 were chosen (see previous page).

 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________

 If any one of Property Nos. 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 or 7 in this guide are given a POOR rating, then this property is rated GOOD and nothing more is done.  Otherwise the following calculations occur.

 The layer with the most inches between 10 and 60 inches is determined.  Call this THICKEST_LAYER.  The layers above and below the THICKEST_LAYER are checked separately to find all the adjacent layers with GOOD or FAIR material.

 Each layer is rated according to Property No. 4, SHRINK-SWELL, and Property No. 5, AASHTO GROUP INDEX NUMBER, given elsewhere in this guide.  The algorithms are the same except that the rating is made for the given layer only.  If either of these ratings are POOR, then the layer is "flagged".

 The total layer thickness of THICKEST_LAYER plus all adjacent, non-flagged layers is found.  Call this TOTAL_THICKNESS.  (If surface layers are involved, the surface thickness is only added in once.)

 The value of TOTAL_THICKNESS is used to make the final rating for this property.  However, if the bottom-most adjacent, non-flagged layer is the actual bottom layer, TOTAL_THICKNESS is set to 100.

   If TOTAL_THICKNESS < 30, then a POOR rating is given.
   If TOTAL_THICKNESS >= 30 and < 60, then a FAIR rating is given.
   If TOTAL_THICKNESS >= 60, then a GOOD rating is given.

This evaluation calculates the thickest layer from the surface to 150cm or a restrictive layer.

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
 

     Where the thickness of the thickest layer  is greater than 100cm (40 in) the evaluation is absolutely true and "THIN LAYER" is not a restrictive feature.
    AND
    Where the thickness of the thickest layer  is less than 30cm (12 in) the evaluation is absolutely false and "THIN LAYER" is a restrictive feature.

Current version contains major  revisions to the Ames 1996 version.

Ames prior to 1996

The layer with the most inches between 10 and 60 inches is determined.  This could be a surface layer or a sublayer.  The unified values given on the Soils-5 are examined for the appropriate layer(s).

 The layer(s) being examined are rated according to the following algorithm:

 If GW, GP, GW-GM, or GP-GM is listed as a unified entry, or if SW, SP, SW-SM or SP-SM is listed as a unified entry and footnote 15 applies (see following description of footnote 15), then a PROBABLE rating is given.

 Otherwise an IMPROBABLE rating is given.

 If the thickest layer is a sublayer, then this property is rated the same as this sublayer's rating.

 If the thickest layer is a surface layer, then this property is rated PROBABLE if there is any PROBABLE surface layer rating.  If there is none, then it is rated IMPROBABLE.

 Restrictive feature terms are assigned appropriately.



 Description of Calculation for Bottom Layer:
+____________________________________________

 If the bottom layer has no data, then this calculation is skipped and the ratings for the thickest layer are chosen.

 Otherwise, this calculation is the same as that for the thickest layer, except it is done for the bottom layer.  The bottom layer, like the thickest layer, may be a surface layer or a sublayer.

 Description of Calculation for Thickest Layer:
+______________________________________________

 The layer with the most inches between 10 and 60 inches is determined.  This could be a surface layer or a sublayer.  The unified values given on the Soils-5 are examined for the appropriate layer(s).

 The layer(s) being examined are rated according to the following algorithm:

 If GW, GP, GW-GM, or GP-GM is listed as a unified entry, or if SW, SP, SW-SM or SP-SM is listed as a unified entry and footnote 15 applies (see following description of footnote 15), then a PROBABLE rating is given.

 Otherwise an IMPROBABLE rating is given.

 If the thickest layer is a sublayer, then this property is rated the same as this sublayer's rating.

 If the thickest layer is a surface layer, then this property is rated PROBABLE if there is any PROBABLE surface layer rating.  If there is none, then it is rated IMPROBABLE.

 Restrictive feature terms are assigned appropriately.



 Description of Calculation for Bottom Layer:
+____________________________________________

 If a single value, say x, is entered, then No_4_Lo = x and  No_4_Hi = x.

 If the entry is a normal range, say x-y, then No_4_Lo = x and  No_4_Hi = y.

 100 - No_4_Lo = Lo

 4. 6/FRACTION >3            <50                         >50                          LARGE
    IN (WT PCT)                                                                                      STONES

 6/Thickest layer between 10 and 60 inches.



 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________

 NOTE:  THE CURRENT CALCULATION FOR THIS PROPERTY IS ACTUALLY A WEIGHTED AVERAGE FROM 10 TO 60 INCHES.

 The values given on the Soils-5 for fraction 3-10 inches are examined and a high value for each layer within 10 to 60 inches is
 determined.  The given depths may or may not include surface layers.   The high value used in the calculation depends on which of the following conditions is met first.

 If a single value of '99' is entered, then an artificial value of 100 is used.

 If a single value not equal to '99' is entered, then an artificial  value of 0 is used.

 Otherwise the high value is used.

 If surface layers are not included, then a weighted average from 10 to 60 inches is calculated and rated.  No phasing is done.

 If surface layers are included, then a separate weighted average from 10 to 60 inches is calculated and rated for each surface
 layer.  Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.

 The rating algorithm is as follows:

    A weighted average > 50 gets an IMPROBABLE rating.
    A weighted average <= 50 gets a PROBABLE rating.

This evaluation checks for coarse fragments greater than 10 inches in the thickest layer.  The rock_frag_10_in is checked and evaluated.

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
 
Where the result of the soil horizon property rock_frag_10_in is greater than 35 percent by weight the evaluation is absolutely true and "PERCENT ROCK FRAGMENTS" is a restrictive feature.
     AND
Where the result of the soil horizon property rock_frag_10_in is less than 5 percent by weight the evaluation is absolutely false and "PERCENT ROCK FRAGMENTS" is not a restrictive feature.

Current version contains major  revisions to the Ames 1996 version.

Ames Description prior to  1996:

1___________________________________________________________________
                                       |             LIMITS                                        |RESTRICTIVE
+                                    ________________________________
     PROPERTY          |    PROBABLE   |   IMPROBABLE   |  FEATURE
                                      |     SOURCE         |             SOURCE     |
+___________________________________________________________________

 4. 6/FRACTION >3            <50                         >50                          LARGE
    IN (WT PCT)                                                                                      STONES

 6/Thickest layer between 10 and 60 inches.



 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________

 NOTE:  THE CURRENT CALCULATION FOR THIS PROPERTY IS ACTUALLY A WEIGHTED AVERAGE FROM 10 TO 60 INCHES.

 The values given on the Soils-5 for fraction 3-10 inches are examined and a high value for each layer within 10 to 60 inches is
 determined.  The given depths may or may not include surface layers.   The high value used in the calculation depends on which of the following conditions is met first.

 If a single value of '99' is entered, then an artificial value of 100 is used.

 If a single value not equal to '99' is entered, then an artificial  value of 0 is used.

 Otherwise the high value is used.

 If surface layers are not included, then a weighted average from 10 to 60 inches is calculated and rated.  No phasing is done.

 If surface layers are included, then a separate weighted average from 10 to 60 inches is calculated and rated for each surface
 layer.  Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.

 The rating algorithm is as follows:

    A weighted average > 50 gets an IMPROBABLE rating.
    A weighted average <= 50 gets a PROBABLE rating.

evaldesc:
NOTE: This evaluation has been modified to reflect conditions in CT as noted below.  Check the NSSC version for a comparison.

This evaluation tests for percent of gravel in the bottom layer.

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
 
Where the result of the soil horizon property sieveno4 is less than 50 percent by weight the evaluation is absolutely true and "EXCESS FINES" is not a restrictive feature.
     AND
Where the result of the soil horizon property sieveno4 is greater than 85 percent by weight the evaluation is absolutely false and "EXCESS FINES" is a restrictive feature.

Current version contains major  revisions to the Ames 1996 version.

Ames prior to 1996

 1___________________________________________________________________
                                                                               LIMITS                                    |RESTRICTIVE
+                       ________________________________
     PROPERTY             |    PROBABLE                 |   IMPROBABLE      |  FEATURE
                                         |     SOURCE                       |     SOURCE                |
+___________________________________________________________________

 2. 12/UNIFIED          GW, GP, GW-GM,
                                        GP-GM

                                       15/SW, 15/SP,
                                      15/SW-SM,
                                      15/SP-SM

                                                                                              16/SW, 16/SP,              TOO
                                                                                             16/SW-SM,                   SANDY
                                                                                             16/SP-SM 

                                                                                                PT                                  EXCESS  HUMUS

                                                                                         ALL OTHER                    EXCESS  FINES

 12/Evaluate the thickest layer between 10 and 60 inches and also the  bottom layer.  Choose the best rating.  When rating is based on  bottom layer, verify thickness.
 15/100 minus % passing No. 4 sieve > 25.
 16/100 minus % passing No. 4 sieve < 25.



 According to footnote 12, calculations are done for both the thickest layer and the bottom layer.

 Description of Calculation for Thickest Layer:
+______________________________________________

 The layer with the most inches between 10 and 60 inches is determined.  This could be a surface layer or a sublayer.  The unified values given on the Soils-5 are examined for the appropriate layer(s).

 The layer(s) being examined are rated according to the following algorithm:

 If GW, GP, GW-GM, or GP-GM is listed as a unified entry, or if SW, SP, SW-SM or SP-SM is listed as a unified entry and footnote 15 applies (see following description of footnote 15), then a PROBABLE rating is given.

 Otherwise an IMPROBABLE rating is given.

 If the thickest layer is a sublayer, then this property is rated the same as this sublayer's rating.

 If the thickest layer is a surface layer, then this property is rated PROBABLE if there is any PROBABLE surface layer rating.  If there is none, then it is rated IMPROBABLE.

 Restrictive feature terms are assigned appropriately.



 Description of Calculation for Bottom Layer:
+____________________________________________

 If the bottom layer has no data, then this calculation is skipped and the ratings for the thickest layer are chosen.

 Otherwise, this calculation is the same as that for the thickest layer, except it is done for the bottom layer.  The bottom layer,
 like the thickest layer, may be a surface layer or a sublayer.

 Calculations for Footnotes 15 and 16
+____________________________________

 To do the calculations for these footnotes, the values given on the Soils-5 for % passing No. 4 sieve are examined.

 % passing No. 4 sieve
+_____________________

 Assign values to No_4_Lo and No_4_Hi.

 If no data is entered, then No_4_Lo = 0 and No_4_Hi = 0.

 If a single value, say x, is entered, then No_4_Lo = x and  No_4_Hi = x.

 If the entry is a normal range, say x-y, then No_4_Lo = x and  No_4_Hi = y.

 Once these values have been assigned, the following calculations take place.

 100 - No_4_Lo = Lo
 100 - No_4_Hi = Hi

 maximum(Lo,Hi) = max

 If max > 25 then footnote 15 applies.
 If max <= 25 then footnote 16 applies.

 For Property No. 2, UNIFIED, the best ratings must be chosen between those calculated for the thickest layer and the bottom layer.

+_______________________________________________

 The values for % passing No. 10 sieve and fraction 3-10 inches given on the Soils-5 are examined.  These values are used in the calculations of weighted averages from 0-40 inches.

 % passing No. 10 sieve
+______________________

 The low value is examined for each layer within the given depths. The value used for each layer in the calculation depends on which of the following conditions is met first.

 If a single value of '99' is entered, then an artificial value of  100 is used.

 If a single value not equal to '99' is entered, then an artificial  value of 0 is used.

 Otherwise the high value is used.

 A separate weighted average is calculated for each surface layer for both % passing No. 10 sieve and fraction 3-10 inches.  For each surface layer, the two weighted averages are added together (call this SUM) and rated.

 To determine the dominant condition, a new weighted average from 0-40 inches is calculated for both % passing No. 10 sieve and fraction 3-10 inches.  The surface layer value used in each calculation is the maximum value over all surface layers.  If the weighted average for fraction 3-10 inches is >= the weighted average for % passing No. 10, then the restrictive term used is LARGE STONES.  Otherwise it is SMALL STONES.

           A SUM > 25 gets a POOR rating.
           A SUM > 5 and <= 25 gets a FAIR rating.
           A SUM <= 5 gets a GOOD rating.

 Description of Calculation for lines 8b and 9b:
+_______________________________________________

 This calculation is similar to that above, except we will assume that no surface layers are involved.

 A separate weighted average from 40-60 inches is calculated for both % passing No. 10 sieve and fraction 3-10 inches.  The two weighted averages are added together (call this SUM).

 If the weighted average for fraction 3-10 inches is >= the weighted average for % passing No. 10 sieve, then the following ratings apply:

           A SUM > 30 gets a POOR rating.
           A SUM > 15 and <= 30 gets a FAIR rating.
           A SUM <= 15 gets a GOOD rating.
 Otherwise the following ratings apply:
           A SUM > 50 gets a POOR rating.
           A SUM > 25 and <= 50 gets a FAIR rating.
           A SUM <= 25 gets a GOOD rating.
                     ---------------
 It is possible that Property No. 4, DEPTH TO BULK DENSITY, Property No. 8b, FRACTION >3 IN (40-60") and Property No. 9b, COARSE FRAGMENTS (40-60") may all have the same restrictive term, AREA RECLAIM.  At this point, a check must be made to ensure that this term will only appear in the final output at most once.

 If No. 4 is marked POOR, then No. 8b and No. 9b are cancelled out. Else if No. 8b is marked POOR, then No. 9b is cancelled out.  The same procedure is repeated for FAIR.

 6. 17/USDA TEXTURE              ---           18/SCL,            SIC, C, SC        TOO CLAYEY

 17/Thickest layer between 0 and 40 inches.

 18/If soil contains >3% organic matter and has less than 35% clay,  rate GOOD.

 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________

 The layer with the most inches between 0 and 40 inches is determined.  This could be a surface layer or a sublayer.  The textures given on the Soils-5 are examined for the appropriate layer(s).

 The layer(s) being examined are rated according to the following algorithm:

 If SIC, C or SC is listed as a texture, then a POOR rating is    given.
 If 18/SCL, 18/CL or 18/SICL is listed as a texture, then a FAIR rating is given.  (See the next page for a description of the    calculation for footnote 18.)
 Otherwise a GOOD rating is given.

 If the thickest layer is a sublayer, then this property is rated the same as this sublayer's rating.

 If the thickest layer is a surface layer, then this property is rated GOOD if there is any GOOD surface layer rating, FAIR if there is any FAIR surface layer rating, and POOR if there is any POOR surface layer rating.  Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.

1

 Calculation of Footnote 18:
+___________________________

 To calculate footnote 18, an organic matter percentage and a clay percentage must be determined for each layer being rated.  The values given on the Soils-5 for organic matter and clay are examined.

 Organic matter
+______________
 Assign a value to OrgMat_Pct.

 For a surface layer, the OrgMat_Pct is the lower value in the range of values for organic matter for this layer.  If this value is blank, then OrgMat_Pct = 0.

 For a sublayer, the OrgMat_Pct is the minimum over all surface layers of the lower value in the range of values for organic matter.  If these values are all blank, then OrgMat_Pct = 0.

 Clay
+____
 Assign a value to Clay_Pct.
 If no data is entered, then Clay_Pct = 100.
 If the entry is a single number, say x, then Clay_Pct = x.
 If the entry is a normal range, say x-y, then Clay_Pct = y.
                     ---------------
 If OrgMat_Pct >= 3 and Clay_Pct <= 35, then rate GOOD.
 Otherwise rate FAIR.

evaldesc:
jmoore copy

This evaluation checks for soil shrink-swell potential from the weighted average LEP within a depth of 250 to 150cm (60 inches) or to bedrock.  The weighted average LEP (linear_extensibility_percent) is examined and evalutated for the depth conditions.

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
  Where the weight average linear_extensibility_percent is less than  3 the evaluation is absolutely true and SHRINK-SWELL is not a restrictive feature.
   OR
  Where the weight average  linear_extensibility_percent  is greater than 9 the evaluation is absolutely false and SHRINK-SWELL is a restrictive feature.

If the weight average  linear_extensibility_percent is NULL then the weight average  LEP is assumed to be less than 3.

Ames Description Prior to 1996:
 
 1___________________________________________________________________
                                                         |             LIMITS                                                                    |RESTRICTIVE
+                                                      ________________________________
     PROPERTY                            |   GOOD   |   FAIR            |           POOR                           |  FEATURE
 +___________________________________________________________________

 4. 12/SHRINK-SWELL        LOW          MODERATE    HIGH, VERY HIGH           SHRINK -SWELL
                                                          (LE <3)        (LE 3-6)                   ( LE>6)

 12/Evaluate the thickest layer between 10 and 60 inches and also the bottom layer.  Choose the best rating.  When rating is based on bottom layer, verify thickness.



 According to footnote 12, calculations are done for both the thickest layer and the bottom layer.  Further description follows Property No. 5.

 Description of Calculation for Thickest Layer:
+______________________________________________

 The layer with the most inches between 10 and 60 inches is determined.  This could be a surface layer or a sublayer.  The shrink-swell values given on the Soils-5 are examined for the appropriate layer(s).

 The layer(s) being examined are rated according to the following algorithm:

 If the shrink-swell value equals '1' (HIGH) or '5' (VERY HIGH), then a POOR rating is given.
 If the shrink-swell value equals '3' (MODERATE), then a FAIR rating is given.
 Otherwise a GOOD rating is given.

 If the thickest layer is a sublayer, then this property is rated the same as this sublayer's rating.

 If the thickest layer is a surface layer, then this property is rated GOOD if there is any GOOD surface layer rating, FAIR if there is any FAIR surface layer rating, and POOR if there is any POOR surface layer rating.  Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.



 Description of Calculation for Bottom Layer:
+____________________________________________

 If the bottom layer has no data, then this calculation is skipped and the ratings for the thickest layer are chosen.

 Otherwise, this calculation is the same as above, except it is done for the bottom layer.  The bottom layer, like the thickest layer, may be a surface layer or a sublayer.
propname: SHRINK-SWELL 25-150cm OR ABOVE Restrictive Layer Wt_Ave.

This evaluation checks for the absence of permafrost within a specified depth.  The component data are check for restriction_kind = "permafrost" and restriction_depth_to_top is evaluated.

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
  Where the soil component property restriction_kind = "permafrost" and the restriction_depth_to_top is less then 50 cm (20 inches) then the evaluation is absolutely false and permafrost is not absent within the specified depth.
     AND
  Where the soil component property restriction_kind = "permafrost" and the restriction_depth_to_top is greater then 100 cm (40 inches) then the evaluation is absolutely true and permafrost is absent within the specified depth.

This evaluation is crisp and checks USDA texture class of the thickest horizon and above any restrictive layer.

The soil is a member of the set of soils that are considered moderately sandy if the udsa texture of the thickest horizon matches LCOS, LS, LFS, or VFS.
propname: USDA TEXTURE THICKEST LAYER IN DEPTH 25-180cm

evalname: AGR-Sandy USDA Textures - thickest layer in 25-180cm
evaldesc:
This evaluation is crisp and checks the texture_class for all layers above any restrictive layer. 
 
Where texture_class equals LCOS, LS,SFS or LVFS for any layer above a restrictive layer the evaluation is absolutely true and the restrictive feature is TOO SANDY.
    AND
Where texture_class does not equal LCOS, LS, LFS, or LVFS or IS NULL for any layer above a restrictive layer the evaluation is absolutely false and the restrictive feature is not TOO SANDY.

 Ames Description prior to 1996:
                                                  |                             LIMITS                            |        RESTRICTIVE
     PROPERTY                     |  SLIGHT  | MODERATE |  SEVERE  |       FEATURE
 9. 6/USDA TEXTURE          ---            LCOS, LS,           COS, S,          TOO SANDY
                                                                            LFS, VFS          FS, SG

 6/Thickest layer between 10 and 60 inches.

 Description of Calculation:

 The layer with the most inches between 10 and 60 inches is determined.  This could be a surface layer or a sublayer.  The textures given on the Soils-5 are examined for the appropriate layer(s).

 The layer(s) being examined are rated according to the following algorithm:

 If COS, S, FS, VFS, or SG is listed as a texture, then a SEVERE    rating is given.
 If LCOS, LS, LFS, LVFS is listed as a texture, then a MODERATE    rating is given.
 Otherwise a SLIGHT rating is given.

 If the thickest layer is a sublayer, then this property is rated the same as this sublayer's rating.

 If the thickest layer is a surface layer, then this property is rated SLIGHT if there is any SLIGHT surface layer rating, MODERATE if there is any MODERATE surface layer rating, and SEVERE if there is any SEVERE surface layer rating.  Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.
propname: USDA TEXTURE THICKEST LAYER IN DEPTH 25-180cm

evalname: Steel Corrosion Sands and Sandy Gravels 25-180cm
evaldesc:
This evaluation is crisp and checks the texture_modifier_and_class for all layers. 
 
Where texture_class equals coarse sands, fine sands, very fine sands or sandy gravel for any layer the evaluation is absolutely true and the restrictive feature is CUTBANKS CAVE.
    AND
Where texture_class does not equal coarse sands, fine sands, very fine sands or sandy gravel or is NULL for all layers the evaluation is absolutely false and the restrictive feature is not CUTBANKS CAVE.
 
 
 Ames Description prior to 1996: 
1___________________________________________________________________
                       |             LIMITS             |RESTRICTIVE
+                       ________________________________
     PROPERTY          |  SLIGHT  | MODERATE |  SEVERE  |  FEATURE
                       |          |          |          |
+___________________________________________________________________
 
 4. USDA TEXTURE           ---                COS, S,    CUTBANKS
    (20-60")                                  FS, VFS,   CAVE
                                              LCOS, LS,
                                              LFS, LVFS,
                                              G, SG
 
 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________
 
The textures given on the Soils-5 are examined for the layers within 20-60 inches.  If surface layers are included in these depths, each is rated separately.  Then each sublayer is rated to determine the worst sublayer rating.  The rating algorithm used on each layer is as follows:
 
If COS, S, FS, VFS, LCOS, LS, LFS, LVFS, G, or SG is listed as a texture, then a SEVERE rating is given.

Otherwise a SLIGHT rating is given.
 
If surface layers are not involved, then this property is rated the same as the worst sublayer rating.
 
If surface layers are involved, then the following applies.  If the worst sublayer rating is SEVERE, then this property is rated SEVERE and no phasing will be done, regardless of the surface layer ratings.
 
If the worst sublayer rating is MODERATE, then this property is rated MODERATE if there is any SLIGHT or MODERATE surface layer rating, and it is rated SEVERE if there is any SEVERE surface layer
 rating.  Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.
 
If the worst sublayer rating is SLIGHT, then this property is rated SLIGHT if there is any SLIGHT surface layer rating, MODERATE if there is any MODERATE surface layer rating, and SEVERE if there is any SEVERE surface layer rating.  Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given. rating, and it is rated SEVERE if there is any SEVERE surface layer rating.  Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.

 4/Disregard (1) in all Aridisols except Salorthids and Aquic subgroups, (2) all Aridic subgroups, and (3) all Torri great

 6/Thickest layer between 10 and 60 inches.

 If the thickest layer is a sublayer, then this property is rated the same as this sublayer's rating.  If minerology on the Soils-5 equals '28' (Kaolinitic), then a MODERATE rating is upgraded to SLIGHT, and a SEVERE rating is upgraded to MODERATE.

 If the thickest layer is a surface layer, then this property is rated SLIGHT if there is any SLIGHT surface layer rating, MODERATE if there is any MODERATE surface layer rating, and SEVERE if there is any SEVERE surface layer rating.  Description of Calculation:
+___________________________
 
The textures given on the Soils-5 are examined for the layers within 20-60 inches.  If surface layers are included in these depths, each is rated separately.  Then each sublayer is rated to determine the worst sublayer rating.  The rating algorithm used on each layer is as follows:
 
If COS, S, FS, VFS, LCOS, LS, LFS, LVFS, G, or SG is listed as a texture, then a SEVERE rating is given.

Otherwise a SLIGHT rating is given.
 
If surface layers are not involved, then this property is rated the same as the worst sublayer rating.
 
If surface layers are involved, then the following applies.  If the worst sublayer rating is SEVERE, then this property is rated SEVERE and no phasing will be done, regardless of the surface layer ratings.
 
If the worst sublayer rating is MODERATE, then this property is rated MODERATE if there is any SLIGHT or MODERATE surface layer rating, and it is rated SEVERE if there is any SEVERE surface layer
 rating.  Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.
 
If the worst sublayer rating is SLIGHT, then this property is rated SLIGHT if there is any SLIGHT surface layer rating, MODERATE if there is any MODERATE surface layer rating, and SEVERE if there is any SEVERE surface layer rating.  Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given. rating, and it is rated SEVERE if there is any SEVERE surface layer rating.  If the thickest layer is a surface layer, then this property is rated SLIGHT if there is any SLIGHT surface layer rating, MODERATE if there is any MODERATE surface layer rating, and SEVERE if there is any SEVERE surface layer rating.  If minerology on the Soils-5 equals '28' (Kaolinitic), then a MODERATE rating is upgraded to SLIGHT, and a SEVERE rating is upgraded to MODERATE. evalname: Maximum Percolation of Layers Within the Water Table
evaldesc:
If the maximum hydraulic conductivity rate of the layer contained by the water table is low than Slow Refill is a restrictive feature.

If the maximum hydraulic conductivity rate is less than 4 mico-meters per second than the evaluation is absolutely true and Slow Refill is a restrictive feature.

If the maximum hydraulic conductivity rate is greater than 14 mico-meters per second than the evaluation is absolutely false and Slow Refill is not a restrictive feature.

If no data is entered, thn an artificial default value(s) is used. 

Ames Description Prior to 1996:

1___________________________________________________________________
                       |             LIMITS             |RESTRICTIVE
+                       ________________________________
     PROPERTY          |  SLIGHT  | MODERATE |  SEVERE  |  FEATURE
                       |          |          |          |
+___________________________________________________________________

 3. PERMEABILITY (IN/HR)   >2.0      0.6-2.0     <0.6    SLOW REFILL
    (BELOW 10")



 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________

 The values given on the Soils-5 for permeability are examined and a
 low value for each layer below 10 inches is determined.  The low
 value used for comparison depends on which of the following
 conditions is met first.

 If no data is entered, then an artificial value of 100 is used.

 If the entry is of the form '<xx', then an artificial value of 0 is
  used.

 Otherwise the low value is used.

 The layers below 10 inches are examined.  If surface layers
 are included in these depths, each is rated separately.  Then each
 sublayer is rated to determine the worst sublayer rating.  The
 rating algorithm used on each layer is as follows:

           A value < 0.6 gets a SEVERE rating.
           A value >= 0.6 and < 2.0 gets a MODERATE rating.
           A value >= 2.0 gets a SLIGHT rating.

 If surface layers are not involved, then this property is rated the
 same as the worst sublayer rating.

 If surface layers are involved, then the following applies.  If the
 worst sublayer rating is SEVERE, then this property is rated SEVERE
 and no phasing will be done, regardless of the surface layer
 ratings.

 If the worst sublayer rating is MODERATE, then this property is
 rated MODERATE if there is any SLIGHT or MODERATE surface layer
 rating, and it is rated SEVERE if there is any SEVERE surface layer
 rating.  Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one
 rating is given.

 If the worst sublayer rating is SLIGHT, then this property is rated
 SLIGHT if there is any SLIGHT surface layer rating, MODERATE if
 there is any MODERATE surface layer rating, and SEVERE if there is
 any SEVERE surface layer rating.  Phasing will be done using texture
 terms if more than one rating is given.

This evaluation check percolation capacity of the soil.  The high, low, and representative values for sat_hydraulic_conductivity are selected for the bottom horizon.

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
  Where the soil horizon property sat_hydraulic_conductivity > 14 micrometers/second (2.0 inches/hour)the evaluation is absolutely true and the restrictive feature is seepage.
        AND
  Where the soil horizon property sat_hydraulic_conductivity =< 14.0 micrometers/second (2.00 inches/hour) the evaluation is absolutely false and the restrictive feature is not seepage.

If no data is entered, then an artificial default value(s) is used. 

Ames Description Prior to 1996:
                                                      |                           LIMITS                              |   RESTRICTIVE
     PROPERTY                         |  SLIGHT  | MODERATE |  SEVERE  |  FEATURE
 5. 4/PERMEABILITY                 ---                ---                    >2.0         SEEPAGE
      (IN/HR) (BOTTOM LAYER)
 
 4/Disregard (1) in all Aridisols except Salorthids and Aquic  subgroups, (2) all Aridic subgroups, and (3) all Torri great groups of Entisols except Aquic subgroups.
 
 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________
 
 If not disregarded, the bottom-most layer with a valid permeability entry is found.  This could be a surface layer or a sublayer.  For example, if there are no sublayers, or all the sublayers are missing permeability entries, then the surface layers will be examined. Otherwise, just the bottom single sublayer will be examined.
 
 The values given on the Soils-5 for permeability are examined and a high value determined for the appropriate layer(s).  The high value used for comparison depends on which of the following conditions is
 met first.
 
 If no data is entered, then an artificial value of 0 is used. 
 If the entry is a single number or is of the form '<xx', then the  single value entered is used.
 
 If the entry is of the form '>xx', then an artificial value of 100 
 
 Otherwise the high value is used.
 
 The layer(s) being examined are rated according to the following algorithm: 
           A value > 2.0 gets a SEVERE rating.
           A value <= 2.0 gets a SLIGHT rating.
 
 If the bottom layer is a sublayer, then this property is rated the same as this sublayer's rating.
 
 If the bottom layer is a surface layer, then this property is rated SLIGHT if there is any SLIGHT surface layer rating, and it is rated SEVERE if there is any SEVERE surface layer rating.  Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.

dmoore 4/3/00 had to split the moderately too sandy evaluations.  When all the various options were on just one evaluations we got a progam error and nasis would just shut down.

dmoore 3/28/00  major twicking to try and match legacy.  Tested against Matsu (some "slight" ratings will change to "very limited" where stratified soils with sandy textures occure), North Star, Gerstle, Copper River, Upper Tanana, and Yentna.  With mostly good results, except where noted in Matsu and where legacy ratings for stratified textures, i.e., SR-S-SIL were inconsistent.  Some times legacy would rate these textures "severe" other times too sandy rating was not addressed.

Phone call with Bob Neilsen on 3/29/00 on this matter.  At this time Bob could not give a reason for legacy inconsistenties with rating stratified soils with sandy layers.  He hopes to have an answer sometime in the future.

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:

evalname: AK3:Shrink-Swell Thickest Layer Above Bedrock or to 40"
evaldesc:
dmoore 2/11/00 try to fix LEI ratings.3/7/00 never made edits use for coping purposes

This evaluation checks for soil shrink-swell potential for the thickest layer within 0 to 100cm (40 inches) or the soil surface to bedrock.  The linear_extensibility_percent for the thickest layer is examined and evalutated for depth conditions.

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
  Where linear_extensibility_percent of the thickest layer is greater than 6 the evaluation is absolutely true.
   OR
  Where linear_extensibility_percent of the thickest layer is less than 3 the evaluation is absolutely false.

If the linear_extensibility_percent of the thickest layer is NULL then LE is assumed to be less than 3.

Ames Description Prior to 1996:
                                                      |                            LIMITS                                       |  RESTRICTIVE
     PROPERTY                         |  SLIGHT  | MODERATE |  SEVERE            |  FEATURE
 
 5. 9/SHRINK-SWELL         LOW             MODERATE      HIGH,                  SHRINK-
                                                                                                              VERY HIGH       SWELL
 
 9/Thickest layer between 10 and 40 inches.
 
 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________
 
 The layer with the most inches between 10 and 40 inches is determined.  This could be a surface layer or a sublayer.  The shrink-swell values given on the Soils-5 are examined for the appropriate layer(s).
 
 The layer(s) being examined are rated according to the following algorithm:
 
 If the shrink-swell value equals '1' (HIGH) or '5' (VERY HIGH), then a SEVERE rating is given.  If the shrink-swell value equals '3' (MODERATE), then a MODERATE rating is given. Otherwise a SLIGHT rating is given.
 
 If the thickest layer is a sublayer, then this property is rated the same as this sublayer's rating.
 
 If the thickest layer is a surface layer, then this property is rated SLIGHT if there is any SLIGHT surface layer rating, MODERATE if there is any MODERATE surface layer rating, and SEVERE if there is any SEVERE surface layer rating.  Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.

dmoore 2/1/00 changed bulk density so rv >1.699 is moderate to match matsu survey area, confirmed this with MHC.   Checked against Matsu, North Star, Upper Tana, Gerstle, Yetna, and Copper River with good results.

This evaluation is crisp and checks the bulk_density_one_third_bar  for all layers within a depth of 50 to 150 cm (20 to 60 inches).
 
Where bulk_density_one_third_bar is greater then 1.8 for any layer within a depth of 50 to 150 cm (20 to 60 inches) the evaluation is true and the restrictive feature is DENSE LAYER.  However, this restriction has only a moderate inpact on the interpretation.
    AND
Where bulk_density_one_third_bar is less than 1.8 or is NULL for all layers within a depth of 50 to 150 cm (20 to 60 inches) the evaluation is absolutely false and the restrictive feature is not DENSE LAYER.
 
 
 Ames Description prior to 1996: 
1___________________________________________________________________
                                                                |                           LIMITS                               | RESTRICTIVE
     PROPERTY     		|  SLIGHT  | MODERATE |  SEVERE  |  FEATURE
 
 7. BULK DENSITY (G/CC)    	     ---                  >1.8                   ---            DENSE LAYER
    (20-60")

 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________
 
 The values given on the Soils-5 for bulk density are examined.  A high value is determined for each layer within 20-60 inches depending on which of the following conditions is met first.
 
 If the entry is a normal range, then the high value is used.
 
 If the entry is of the form '>xx', then an artificial value of 99.99 is used.
 
 If the entry is a single number or is of the form '<xx', then the single value entered is used.
 
 Otherwise an artificial value of 0 is used.
 
 If any of the determined values is > 1.8, then this property is rated SEVERE.  Otherwise it is rated SLIGHT.

dmoore 3/28/00  major twicking to try and match legacy.  Tested against Matsu (some "slight" ratings will change to "very limited" where stratified soils with sandy textures occure), North Star, Gerstle, Copper River, Upper Tanana, and Yentna.  With mostly good results, except where noted in Matsu and where legacy ratings for stratified textures, i.e., SR-S-SIL were inconsistent.  Some times legacy would rate these textures "severe" other times too sandy rating was not addressed.

Phone call with Bob Neilsen on 3/29/00 on this matter.  At this time Bob could not give a reason for legacy inconsistenties with rating stratified soils with sandy layers.  He hopes to have an answer sometime in the future.

Changed rule rating name from Too sandy to Too sandy, caving.  Phone call with Bob Neilsen on this matter.  Bob could not give reason why to have too sandy rating unless it was for cutbanks caving or trench wall strenght.  He hopes to have an answer sometime in the future.  Made rule name rating change to keep orginal too sandy criteria as opposed to replacing it with the cutbank caving in shallow excavations.

evalname: AK jpm ENG-Unified (sand/gravel in the thickest layer)
evaldesc:
Test modification of national evaluation by jmoore on 12/20/99.  Attempt to determine gravel suitability based on Unified.


This evaluation is crisp and checks for Unified equal to "GW", "GP", "GW-GM", or "GP-GM" in the bottom layer.

Where unified_soil_classification equals "GW", "GP", "GW-GM", or "GP-GM" the evaluation is absolutely false, a value of 0 is returned, and the restrictive feature is not EXCESS FINES.
    AND
Where unified_soil_classification does not equal "GW", "GP", "GW-GM", or "GP-GM" the evaluation is absolutely TRUE, a value of 1 is returned, and EXCESS FINES may be a restrictive feature.

1___________________________________________________________________
                       |             LIMITS             |RESTRICTIVE
+                       ________________________________
     PROPERTY          |   Well   | Moderately |  Poorly  |  FEATURE
                       |  Suited  | Well Suited|   Suited |
+___________________________________________________________________
 USDA Soil Texture         ---		---	ANY OTHER     EXCESS
    (BOTTOM LAYER)	   		        THAN GW,      FINES
    						GP, GW-GM,
 						GP-GM
 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________
 
The unified values given on the Soils-5 are examined for the bottom layer.  The bottom layer may be a surface layer or a sublayer.
 
The bottom layer is rated according to the following algorithm:
 
If SW, SP, SW-SM, or SP-SM is listed as a unified entry, then a POORLY SUITED rating is given.  Otherwise a WELL SUITED rating is given.
 
If the bottom layer is a sublayer, then this property is rated the same as this sublayer's rating.
 
If the bottom layer is a surface layer, then this property is rated POORLY SUITED if there is any POORLY SUITED surface layer rating, and it is rated WELL SUITED if there is any WELL SUITED surface layer rating.  Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.

evalname: AK: Percolation (1.39 to 14 um/sec) 122 to 180cm (48 to 72")
evaldesc:
AK: This evaluation check percolation capacity of the soil.  The high, low, and representative values for sat_hydraulic_conductivity are selected for each horizon between 48 to 72 inches and permeability is <1.39um/sec). dmoore3/6/00

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
  Where the soil horizon property sat_hydraulic_conductivity < 2.0 micrometers/second (0.60 inches/hour)the evaluation is absolutely true and the restrictive feature is slow percolation.
        AND
  Where the soil horizon property sat_hydraulic_conductivity => 14.0 micrometers/second (2.00 inches/hour) the evaluation is absolutely false and the restrictive feature is not slow percolation.

If no data is entered, then an artificial default value(s) is used. 

Ames Description Prior to 1996:
                                                   |                           LIMITS                              |   RESTRICTIVE
     PROPERTY                      |  SLIGHT  | MODERATE |  SEVERE  |  FEATURE
 7. PERMEABILITY              2.0-6.0          I/0.6-2.0               <0.6         PERCS SLOWLY
    (IN/HR):    (24-60")            

    I/Recheck to see if rating should be SLIGHT.

 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________
 
 This property is calculated as if it were two separate properties.
 The calculation for the first line (PERCS SLOWLY) is:
 
 The values given on the Soils-5 for permeability are examined and a
 low value for each layer is determined.  The low value used for
 comparison depends on which of the following conditions is met
 first.
 
 If no data is entered, then an artificial value of 100 is used.
 
 If the entry is of the form '<xx', then an artificial value of 0 is
  used.
 
 Otherwise the low value is used.
 
 The layers within the given depths are examined.  If surface layers
 are included in these depths, each is rated separately.  Then each
 sublayer is rated to determine the worst sublayer rating.  The
 rating algorithm used on each layer is as follows:

           A value < 0.6 gets a SEVERE rating
           A value >= 0.6 and < 2.0 gets a MODERATE rating.
           A value >= 2.0 gets a SLIGHT rating.
 
 If surface layers are not involved, then this property is rated the
 same as the worst sublayer rating.
 
 If surface layers are involved, then the following applies.  If the
 worst sublayer rating is SEVERE, then this property is rated SEVERE
 and no phasing will be done, regardless of the surface layer
 ratings.
 
 If the worst sublayer rating is MODERATE, then this property is
 rated MODERATE if there is any SLIGHT or MODERATE surface layer
 rating, and it is rated SEVERE if there is any SEVERE surface layer
 rating.  Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one
 rating is given.
 
 If the worst sublayer rating is SLIGHT, then this property is rated
 SLIGHT if there is any SLIGHT surface layer rating, MODERATE if
 there is any MODERATE surface layer rating, and SEVERE if there is
 any SEVERE surface layer rating.  Phasing will be done using texture
 terms if more than one rating is given.
