evalname: AK jpm: Coarse Frags 75 to 250mm (3 to 10 in) (Bottom Laye
evaldesc:
jmoore copy

This evaluation checks for coarse fragments between 3 and 10 inches in the bottom layer.  The rock_frag_3_to_10_in is checked and evaluated.

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
 
Where the result of the soil horizon property rock_frag_3_to_10_in is greater than 35 percent by weight the evaluation is absolutely true and "PERCENT COARSE FRAGMENTS" is a restrictive feature.
     AND
Where the result of the soil horizon property rock_frag_3_to_10_in is less than 0 percent by weight the evaluation is absolutely false and "PERCENT COARSE FRAGMENTS" is not a restrictive feature.

Current version contains major  revisions to the Ames 1996 version.

Ames Description prior to  1996:

1___________________________________________________________________
                                       |             LIMITS                                        |RESTRICTIVE
+                                    ________________________________
     PROPERTY          |    PROBABLE   |   IMPROBABLE   |  FEATURE
                                      |     SOURCE         |             SOURCE     |
+___________________________________________________________________

 4. 6/FRACTION >3            <50                         >50                          LARGE
    IN (WT PCT)                                                                                      STONES

 6/Thickest layer between 10 and 60 inches.



 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________

 NOTE:  THE CURRENT CALCULATION FOR THIS PROPERTY IS ACTUALLY A WEIGHTED AVERAGE FROM 10 TO 60 INCHES.

 The values given on the Soils-5 for fraction 3-10 inches are examined and a high value for each layer within 10 to 60 inches is
 determined.  The given depths may or may not include surface layers.   The high value used in the calculation depends on which of the following conditions is met first.

 If a single value of '99' is entered, then an artificial value of 100 is used.

 If a single value not equal to '99' is entered, then an artificial  value of 0 is used.

 Otherwise the high value is used.

 If surface layers are not included, then a weighted average from 10 to 60 inches is calculated and rated.  No phasing is done.

 If surface layers are included, then a separate weighted average from 10 to 60 inches is calculated and rated for each surface
 layer.  Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.

 The rating algorithm is as follows:

    A weighted average > 50 gets an IMPROBABLE rating.
    A weighted average <= 50 gets a PROBABLE rating.

evalname: AK jpm Sand in the Thickest Layer to 100cm
evaldesc:
jmoore copy

This evaluation tests for percent of sand in the thickest layer within 40 inches of the surface.

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
 
Where the result of the calculation sieveno200 -  sieveno4 is less than 75 percent by weight the evaluation is absolutely true and "TOO SANDY" is not a restrictive features.
     AND
Where the result of the calculation sieveno200 -  sieveno4 is greater than 85 percent by weight the evaluation is absolutely false and "TOO SANDY" is a restrictive features.

Current version contains major  revisions to the Ames 1996 version.

Ames prior to 1996

 
 1___________________________________________________________________
                                                                 |             LIMITS                                                  |RESTRICTIVE
+                       ________________________________
     PROPERTY                         |   GOOD   |   FAIR                   |   POOR                    |  FEATURE
+___________________________________________________________________
 5. 17/USDA TEXTURE         ---             LCOS, LS,             COS, S,                  TOO SANDY
                                                                              LFS, LVFS             FS, VFS
 17/Thickest layer between 0 and 40 inches.

 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________

 The layer with the most inches between 0 and 40 inches is determined.  This could be a surface layer or a sublayer.  The textures given on the Soils-5 are examined for the appropriate layer(s).

 The layer(s) being examined are rated according to the following algorithm:

 If COS, S, FS or VFS is listed as a texture, then a POOR rating is  given.
If LCOS, LS, LFS or LVFS is listed as a texture, then a FAIR rating is given.
Otherwise a GOOD rating is given.

 If the thickest layer is a sublayer, then this property is rated the same as this sublayer's rating.

 If the thickest layer is a surface layer, then this property is rated GOOD if there is any GOOD surface layer rating, FAIR if there is any FAIR surface layer rating, and POOR if there is any POOR surface layer rating.  Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.

evalname: ron Wet, Ground Water Near Surface (20 - 100cm)
evaldesc:
This evaluation checks for a saturated or wet condition within a depth of 90 cm (40 inch) of the soil surface.  The water moisture status for all layers are examined and those saturated or wet layers are evalutated for depth.  If a saturated condition occurs within 20 cm (8 inches) of the soil surface than wetness is a limitation.

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
  Where soil_moisture_status is wet and the depth to soil_moist_depth_to_top is greater than 100 cm (3 foot) the evaluation is absolutely true.
   OR
  Where soil_moisture_status is wet and the depth to  soil_moist_depth_to_top  is less than 20 cm (8 inches) the evaluation is absolutely false.

If the soil_moisture_status is not wet or null, then the property asumption is that soil_moist_depth_to_top is NULL and no water table is present.

The low value in the range of values given on the Soils-5 for depth to high water table is examined.  The value used for comparison depends on which of the following conditions are met first.

This evaluation checks the percolation rate of the soil.  The high, low, and representative values for sat_hydraulic_conductivity are selected for each horizon between 24 to 60 inches. 

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:

Ames Description Prior to 1996

 1___________________________________________________________________
                       |             LIMITS             |RESTRICTIVE
+                       ________________________________
     PROPERTY          |  SLIGHT  | MODERATE |  SEVERE  |  FEATURE
                       |          |          |          |

 7. PERMEABILITY
    (IN/HR):
    (24-40")              <0.6      0.6-2.0       >2.0     SEEPAGE
 
  
 
 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________
   
 The values given on the Soils-5 for permeability are examined and a
 high value for each layer is determined.  The high value used for
 comparison depends on which of the following conditions is met
 first.
 
 If no data is entered, then an artificial value of 0 is used.
 
 If the entry is a single number or is of the form '<xx', then the
  single value entered is used.
 
 If the entry is of the form '>xx', then an artificial value of 100
  is used.
 
 Otherwise the high value is used.
 
 The layers within the given depths are examined.  If surface layers are included in these depths, each is rated separately.  Then each sublayer is rated to determine the worst sublayer rating.  The rating algorithm used on each layer is as follows:
 
           A value > 2.0 gets a SEVERE rating.
           A value <= 0.6 gets a SLIGHT rating.
 
 If surface layers are not involved, then this property is rated the
 same as the worst sublayer rating.
 
 If surface layers are involved, then the following applies.  If the
 worst sublayer rating is SEVERE, then this property is rated SEVERE
 and no phasing will be done, regardless of the surface layer
 ratings.
 
 If the worst sublayer rating is SLIGHT, then this property is rated
 SLIGHT if there is any SLIGHT surface layer rating, and it is rated
 SEVERE if there is any SEVERE surface layer rating.  Phasing will be
 done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.

evaldesc:
This evaluation checks for a saturated or wet condition within a depth of 100 cm (3.3 feet) of the soil surface.  The water moisture status for all layers are examined and those saturated or wet layers are evalutated for depth.

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
  Where soil_moisture_status is saturated or wet and the depth to soil_moist_depth_to_top is less than 100 cm (3.3 feet) the evaluation is absolutely true.
   OR
  Where soil_moisture_status is saturated or wet and the depth to  soil_moist_depth_to_top  is greater than >= 100 cm (3.3 feet) the evaluation is absolutely false.

If the soil_moisture_status is not saturated or wet, then the property asumption is that soil_moist_depth_to_top is NULL and no water table is present.
propname: CT-DEPTH TO LEAF OFF WATER TABLE MINIMUM

evaldesc:

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
  Where soil_moisture_status is wet and the depth to soil_moist_depth_to_top is less than 120 cm (4 feet) the evaluation is absolutely true.
   OR

If the soil_moisture_status is not wet or null, then the property asumption is that soil_moist_depth_to_top is NULL and no water table is present.

 ___________________________________________________________________
                       |             LIMITS             |RESTRICTIVE
+                       ________________________________
     PROPERTY          |  SLIGHT  | MODERATE |  SEVERE  |  FEATURE
                       |          |          |          |
+___________________________________________________________________
 
 3b:  WATER TABLE (FT)       >6         4-6       <4      WETNESS

 If no data is entered, then an artificial value of 99.9 is used.

+______________________________________________

 The layer with the most inches between 10 and 60 inches is determined.  This could be a surface layer or a sublayer.  The unified values given on the Soils-5 are examined for the appropriate layer(s).

 The layer(s) being examined are rated according to the following algorithm:

 If GW, GP, GW-GM, or GP-GM is listed as a unified entry, or if SW, SP, SW-SM or SP-SM is listed as a unified entry and footnote 15 applies (see following description of footnote 15), then a PROBABLE rating is given.

 Restrictive feature terms are assigned appropriately.



 Description of Calculation for Bottom Layer:
+____________________________________________

 If the bottom layer has no data, then this calculation is skipped and the ratings for the thickest layer are chosen.

 % passing No. 4 sieve

 If a single value, say x, is entered, then No_4_Lo = x and  No_4_Hi = x.

 If the entry is a normal range, say x-y, then No_4_Lo = x and  No_4_Hi = y.

 100 - No_4_Lo = Lo
 100 - No_4_Hi = Hi

     PROPERTY                   |  SLIGHT  | MODERATE |  SEVERE  |  FEATURE
 8. UNIFIED (10-40")         ---                ---               OL, OH, PT   EXCESS HUMUS
 
 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________
 
 The unified values given on the Soils-5 are examined for the layers within 10-40 inches.  If surface layers are included in these depths, each is rated separately.  Then each sublayer is rated to determine the worst sublayer rating.  The rating algorithm used on each layer is as follows:
 
 If OL, OH, or PT is listed as a texture, then a SEVERE rating is given.
 Otherwise a SLIGHT rating is given.
 
 If surface layers are not involved, then this property is rated the same as the worst sublayer rating.
 
 If surface layers are involved, then the following applies.  If the worst sublayer rating is SEVERE, then this property is rated SEVERE and no phasing will be done, regardless of the surface layer ratings.
 
 
 If the worst sublayer rating is SLIGHT, then this property is rated SLIGHT if there is any SLIGHT surface layer rating, and it is rated SEVERE if there is any SEVERE surface layer rating.  Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.
Where the soil property unified_soil_classification equals = "ol", "oh", "pt" in any layer >=10cm thick within 15cm of the soil surface, the evaluation returns a value of 1.

evaldesc:

evaldesc:

taxonomic_temp_regime		growing season months
---------------------		---------------------
cryic, isofrigid, or pergelic	July and August

frigid or mesic			May, June, July, 
				August, and September

thermic 			March, April, May, 
         			June, July, August,
				September, and October

isothermic,			February, March, April,
isohyperthermic,		May, June, July, August,
isomesic, hyperthermic		September, October, and
				November

If the climate is dry and the water table is not near the surface of the soil during the regions growing season then the condition is optimum for the soil rating for plant growth.

The fuzzy space is defined as the codition where:
Soil moisture regime is xeric or aridic and 
the growing season is defined as:

July to August for temperature regimes cryic and pergilic;
May to September for temperature regimes mesic and frigid;
February to November for temperature regimes thermic and hyperthermic;
January to December for temperature regimes isomesic, isofrigid,
   isohyperthermic, and isothermic.


If the depth to the high water table under these conditions is > 45 cm then the depth to high water table is optimum for the soil rating for plant growth and the evaluation is absolutely true.

If the depth to the high water table under these conditions is 0 cm then the depth to high water table less than optimum for the soil rating for plant growth and the evaluation is somewhat false.

This evaluation is based on Mean Annual Precipitation MAP effect on the growth of winter wheat in Kansas.  The fuzzy space is defined as beginning at .7 for 400mm of MAP and 1.0 for 1100mm of MAP.  The greater the MAP the less impact on SRPG.

This evaluation checks the greater than 3 inch fraction of the soil.  The component horizon rock_frag_3_to_10_in and rock_frag_greater_than_10_in is calculated for the surface layer of the soil and the result is checked and evaluated.

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
 
  Where the total of the soil component surface horizon properties rock_frag_3_to_10_in and rock_frag_greater_than_10_in is greater than 30% the evaluation is absolutely true and "LARGE STONES" is a restrictive feature.
     AND
  Where the total of the soil component surface horizon properties rock_frag_3_to_10_in and rock_frag_greater_than_10_in is less than 5% the evaluation is absolutely false and "LARGE STONES" is not a restrictive feature.

Ames Description prior to  1996:

                                                  |                             LIMIT                               |  RESTRICTIVE
     PROPERTY                     |  SLIGHT  | MODERATE |  SEVERE  |  FEATURE
 7. FRACTION >3 IN                  <5                 5-30                >30            LARGE STONES
    (WT PCT) (SURFACE 
    LAYER)
 
 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________
 
 The values given on the Soils-5 for fraction 3-10 inches are examined and a high value for each layer is determined.  The high value used in the calculation depends on which of the following conditions is met first.
 
 If a single value of '99' is entered, then an artificial value of 100 is used. 
 If a single value not equal to '99' is entered, then an artificial value of 0 is used. 
 Otherwise the high value is used.
 
 A separate weighted average is calculated for each surface layer. 
       A weighted average > 30 gets a SEVERE rating.
       A weighted average > 5 and <= 30 gets a MODERATE rating.
       A weighted average <= 5 gets a SLIGHT rating.
 
 Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.

This evaluation checks the values of greater than  3" (75mm) fraction for the surface horizon. 

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
 
  Where the total of the soil component horizon coarse fragment property > 75mm is greater than 25% the evaluation is absolutely true and "LARGE STONES" is a restrictive feature.
     AND
  Where the total of the soil component horizon coarse fragment property > 75mm is less than 5% the evaluation is absolutely false and "LARGE STONES" is not a restrictive feature.

The coarse fragments greater then 3 inches in the soil surface are evaluated and indexes the degree to which LARGE STONES are limiting.  Where the soil property "MO16-FRAGMENTS > 75mm SURFACE LAYER" is:
	 
	  > 75 the soil is limited and the degree of limitation is expressed as the number 1.0.
	 => 25 and =< 75 the soil is somewhat limited and the degree of limitation is expressed as a number between 0 and 1.0.
	  < 25 the soil is not limited and the degree of limitation is expressed as the number.

This evaluation checks the values of greater than  3" (75mm) fraction for the surface horizon. 

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
 
  Where the total of the soil component horizon coarse fragment property > 75mm is greater than 50% the evaluation is absolutely true and "LARGE STONES" is a restrictive feature.
     AND
  Where the total of the soil component horizon coarse fragment property > 75mm is less than 15% the evaluation is absolutely false and "LARGE STONES" is not a restrictive feature.

Fuzzy zone: 15-50% by weight (5-35% by volume)

The fuzzy space is defined as ( 25-75% by weight) 15-60% coarse fragments >75mm.  If the percent of coarse fragments >75mm is more than 60 percent, then the rule is true (not suited).  If the percent is less than 15 percent, then the rule is false (well suited).

An evaluation of the impact of surface fragments >75mm.

The fuzzy space is defined as ( 25-75% by weight) 15-60% coarse fragments >75mm.  If the percent of coarse fragments >75mm is more than 60 percent, then the rule is true (not suited).  If the percent is less than 15 percent, then the rule is false (well suited).

The fuzzy space is defined as ( 25-75% by weight) 15-60% coarse fragments >75mm.  If the percent of coarse fragments >75mm is more than 60 percent, then the rule is true (not suited).  If the percent is less than 15 percent, then the rule is false (well suited).

The fuzzy range is 6-20 in/hr (41-141 micrometers/sec).  If permeability is >20 in/hr, then the rule is false (not suited).  If permeability is <6 in/hr, then the rule is false (well suited).

evaldesc:
This evaluation checks aashto_group_index.  The component data are check for aashto_group_index index number.

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
  Where the soil component property aashto_group_index is greaer then 8 then the evaluation is absolutely true and LOW STRENGTH is a restrictive feature.
     AND
  Where the soil component property aashto_group_index is less then 5 then the evaluation is absolutely false and LOW STRENGTH is not a restrictive feature.


Ames Description prior to  1996:
____________________________________________________________________
                                                             |             LIMITS                                              |RESTRICTIVE
+                                                         ________________________________
     PROPERTY                              |  SLIGHT  | MODERATE |  SEVERE     |  FEATURE
 +___________________________________________________________________
 
 6. 5/, 9/, 10/AASHTO                     <5                    5-8                        >8               LOW  STRENGTH
    GROUP INDEX NUMBER                                   
    
 5/If in Kaolinitic family, rate one class better if experience confirms.
 9/Thickest layer between 10 and 40 inches.
 10/GIN=(F-35)[.2+.005(LL-40)]+.01(F-15)(PI-10) where F=% passing No. 200 sieve.  If F<=35 and PI>=11, use only part 2 of equation.  Use median values.
 
 
 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________
 
 The layer with the most inches between 10 and 40 inches is determined.  This could be a surface layer or a sublayer.  The GIN is calculated for the appropriate layer(s) according to the given algorithm.
 
 To calculate the GIN, median values are needed for the following: percent passing No. 200 sieve (F), liquid limit (LL), and plasticity index (PI).  A median is calculated by adding the low and high values, then dividing by 2, unless special conditions exist.  The median calculation is given below for each of these three variables.
 
 Percent passing No. 200 sieve:
+______________________________
 
 If no valid data is entered, then an artificial value of 0 is used as the median.
 
 If a single value is entered, then this value is used as the median.
 
 Otherwise the median is calculated using the low and high values.
 

 
 Liquid limit:
+_____________
 
 If the entry is of the form '<xxx', then a median is calculated using 0 and xxx. 
 If the entry is of the form '>xxx', then a median is calculated using xxx and 100.
  If no valid data is entered, then an artificial value of 0 is used as the median. 
 If a single value is entered, then this value is used as the median. 
 Otherwise the median is calculated using the low and high values.
 
 Plasticity index:
+_________________
 
 If the entry is of the form '<xxx', then a median is calculated using 0 and xxx. 
 If the entry is of the form '>xxx', then a median is calculated using xxx and 100. 
 If the entry is of the form 'NP', then an artificial value of 0 is used as the median. 
 
 If the entry is of the form 'NP-xxx', then a median is calculated using 0 and xxx. 
 If no valid data is entered, then an artificial value of 0 is used as the median. 
 If a single value is entered, then this value is used as the median. 
 Otherwise the median is calculated using the low and high values. 
 After the GIN is calculated, the layer(s) being examined are rated according to the following algorithm: 
    If GIN > 8, then a SEVERE rating is given.
    If GIN > 5 and <= 8, then a MODERATE rating is given.
    If GIN <= 5, then a SLIGHT rating is given.
 
 If the thickest layer is a sublayer, then this property is rated the same as this sublayer's rating.  If minerology on the Soils-5 equals '28' (Kaolinitic), then a MODERATE rating is upgraded to SLIGHT, and a SEVERE rating is upgraded to MODERATE.
 
 If the thickest layer is a surface layer, then this property is rated SLIGHT if there is any SLIGHT surface layer rating, MODERATE if there is any MODERATE surface layer rating, and SEVERE if there is any SEVERE surface layer rating.  If minerology on the Soils-5 equals '28' (Kaolinitic), then a MODERATE rating is upgraded to SLIGHT, and a SEVERE rating is upgraded to MODERATE.  Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.
propname: RTF-AASHTO GROUP INDEX No. THICKEST LAYER (10-60")

evaldesc:

Ames prior to 1996:

     PROPERTY                    |   GOOD   |   FAIR   |   POOR   |  FEATURE
 7. 5/,6/UNIFIED                       ---         ---       OL, OH,       HARD TO
                                             	                          CH, MH        PACK

   confirms.

Description of Calculation:

 The layer with the most inches between 10 and 60 inches is determined.  This could be a surface layer or a sublayer.  The unified values given on the Soils-5 are examined for the appropriate layer(s).

 The layer(s) being examined are rated according to the following algorithm:

 If OL, OH, CH, or MH is listed as a unified entry, then a POOR  rating is given.
 Otherwise a GOOD rating is given.

 If the thickest layer is a sublayer, then this property is rated the same as this sublayer's rating.  If minerology on the Soils-5 equals '28' (Kaolinitic), then a POOR rating is upgraded to FAIR.

 If the thickest layer is a surface layer, then this property is rated GOOD if there is any GOOD surface layer rating, and it is rated POOR if there is any POOR surface layer rating.  If minerology on the Soils-5 equals '28' (Kaolinitic), then a POOR rating is upgraded to FAIR.  Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.

evaldesc:
This evaluation checks the available water of the soil.  The weight average of the component horizon available_water_capacity is calculated for the soil and the result is check and evaluated.

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
 
  Where the total of each layers weighted average of the soil component horizon property available_water_capacity to a depth of 50cm (20in) is less than 2.5cm (1in) the evaluation is absolutely true and "DROUGHTY" is a restrictive feature.
     AND
  Where the total of each layers weighted average of the soil component horizon property available_water_capacity to a depth of 50cm (20in) is greater than 5cm (2.5in) the evaluation is absolutely false and "DROUGHTY" is not a restrictive feature.

Fuzzy zone: 2.5-5.0 cm (1-2 in) within 50 cm (20 in)

This evaluation tests for percent of clay in the thickest layer to a depth of 72 inches or above a restrictive layer.

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
 
27-60% clay

The weighted average of the component horizon rock_frag_3_to_10_in and rock_frag_greater_than_10_in to a depth of 180cm (72") indexes the degree to which LARGE STONES are limiting.  Where the soil property "RTF- FRAGMENTS > 75MM WEIGHTED AVE. IN DEPTH 0-180CM" is:
	 => 50 the soil is limited and the degree of limitation is expressed as the number 1.0.
	  > 15 and < 50 the soil is somewhat limited and the degree of limitation is expressed as a number between 0 and 1.0.
	 =< 15 the soil is not limited and the degree of limitation is expressed as the number 0.
propname: RTF- FRAGMENTS > 75MM WEIGHTED AVE. IN DEPTH 0-180CM

This evaluation looks at the condition: 
  Where the maximum value of the soil property soil_moisture_depth_to_top is >=30 and <=75cm AND the soil property soil_moisture_status is "wet" for any month corresponding to a "growing season month" as determined by the soil property taxonomic_temp_regime, the evaluation returns a value of 1.

Growing season months are derived from the temperature regime of the soil component as follows:

taxonomic_temp_regime	growing season months
---------------------	---------------------
cryic or pergelic	July and August

frigid or mesic		May, June, July, 
			August, and September

thermic or		March, April, May, 
hyperthermic		June, July, August,
			September, and October

isothermic,		February, March, April,
isohyperthermic,	May, June, July, August,
or isomesic		September, October, and
			November

  Where the maximum value of the soil property soil_moisture_depth_to_top is >=15 and <=60cm AND the soil property soil_moisture_status is "wet" for any month corresponding to a "growing season month" as determined by the soil property taxonomic_temp_regime, the evaluation returns a value of 1.

Growing season months are derived from the temperature regime of the soil component as follows:

taxonomic_temp_regime	growing season months
---------------------	---------------------
cryic or pergelic	July and August

frigid or mesic		May, June, July, 
			August, and September

thermic or		March, April, May, 
hyperthermic		June, July, August,
			September, and October

isothermic,		February, March, April,
isohyperthermic,	May, June, July, August,
or isomesic		September, October, and
			November

evalname: VA VIN - Depth  to Restrictive Layer
evaldesc:
This evaluation tests the depth to a restrictive layer where the following is true.
As the depth to a  restrictive layer decreases then the soil hydrologic group approaches group "D".  At depths > than 20 inches (50cm) the hydrologic groups B and C are possible.  Hydrologic group A is possible at depths > 40 inches (100cm). 

The fuzzy space is defined as depth to restrictive layer < 50cm and > 100cm (< 20 inches and > 40 inches).
propname: VA - DEPTH TO FIRST RESTRICTIVE LAYER

evalname: JTH-USDA Texture Class, Surface - COS, S, FS
evaldesc:
This evaluation is crisp and checks the texture_class for surface layer. 
                                     
Where texture_class equals cos, fs, or s for the surface layer the evaluation is absolutely true and the restrictive feature is TOO SANDY.
    AND
Where texture_class does not equal cos, fs, or s, or is NULL for the surface layer the evaluation is absolutely false and the restrictive feature is not TOO SANDY.
 
 
 Ames Description prior to 1996:
                                                    |                            LIMITS                             |   RESTRICTIVE
      PROPERTY                      |  SLIGHT  | MODERATE |  SEVERE  |  FEATURE
 14. USDA TEXTURE             ---                   ---                COS           TOO SANDY
     (SURFACE LAYER) 
 
 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________
 
The textures given on the Soils-5 for each surface layer are examined.
 
The surface layers are each rated separately using the following algorithm: 
     If COS is listed as a texture, then a SEVERE rating is
     given.
     Otherwise a SLIGHT rating is given.
 
If there is a surface layer with a SEVERE rating, then this property is rated SEVERE.  If there is a surface layer with a SLIGHT rating, then this property is rated SLIGHT.  Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.

 These textures and considered (moderately limiting) and will assigned a fuzzy value of 0.5.
If cover type is rangeland, tundra then the evaluation is true and "SENATIVE VEGETATION" is a restrictive feature.

evaldesc:
This evaluation is crisp and checks the texture_modifier_and_class for all layers. 
 
Where texture_class equals coarse sands, fine sands, very fine sands or sandy gravel for any layer the evaluation is absolutely true and the restrictive feature is CUTBANKS CAVE.
    AND
Where texture_class does not equal coarse sands, fine sands, very fine sands or sandy gravel or is NULL for all layers the evaluation is absolutely false and the restrictive feature is not CUTBANKS CAVE.
 
 
 Ames Description prior to 1996: 

                                   	    |             LIMITS      		               |RESTRICTIVE
     PROPERTY       	    |  SLIGHT  | MODERATE |  SEVERE  |  FEATURE
 4. USDA TEXTURE       	              ---                COS, S,     CUTBANKS
    (20-60")                                  		                 FS, VFS,    CAVE
                                             		                 LCOS, LS,
			                                       LFS, LVFS,
			                                       G, SG
 
 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________
 
The textures given on the Soils-5 are examined for the layers within 20-60 inches.  If surface layers are included in these depths, each is rated separately.  Then each sublayer is rated to determine the worst sublayer rating.  The rating algorithm used on each layer is as follows:
 
If COS, S, FS, VFS, LCOS, LS, LFS, LVFS, G, or SG is listed as a texture, then a SEVERE rating is given.

Otherwise a SLIGHT rating is given.
 
If surface layers are not involved, then this property is rated the same as the worst sublayer rating.
 
If surface layers are involved, then the following applies.  If the worst sublayer rating is SEVERE, then this property is rated SEVERE and no phasing will be done, regardless of the surface layer ratings.
 
If the worst sublayer rating is MODERATE, then this property is rated MODERATE if there is any SLIGHT or MODERATE surface layer rating, and it is rated SEVERE if there is any SEVERE surface layer
 rating.  Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.
 
If the worst sublayer rating is SLIGHT, then this property is rated SLIGHT if there is any SLIGHT surface layer rating, MODERATE if there is any MODERATE surface layer rating, and SEVERE if there is any SEVERE surface layer rating.  Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given. rating, and it is rated SEVERE if there is any SEVERE surface layer rating.  Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.

evaldesc:
This evaluation checks the available water of the soil.  The total avialable water is calculated for the soil and the result is check and evaluated.

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
 
  Where the total available water to a depth of 150cm (60in) is less than 7.5 cm (3 in) the evaluation is absolutely true and "DROUGHTY" is a restrictive feature.
     AND
  Where the total avaiilable water to a depth of 150cm (60in) is greater than 15 cm (6 in) the evaluation is absolutely false and "DROUGHTY" is not a restrictive feature.

Ames Description prior to  1996:
 ___________________________________________________________________
                       |             LIMITS             |RESTRICTIVE
+                       ________________________________
     PROPERTY          |  SLIGHT  | MODERATE |  SEVERE  |  FEATURE
                       |          |          |          |
+___________________________________________________________________
 
 14. AVAILABLE WATER        >6        3-6         <3     DROUGHTY
     (WEIGHT AVE, 0 TO 60")
  
 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________
 
 The values given on the Soils-5 for available water are examined and
 
 If no data is entered, then the layer is skipped.
 
 If the entry is a single number, then the single value entered is used as the average.
 
 If the entry is of the form '<xxxx', then the average is taken using 0 and xxxx.
 
 Otherwise the low value is used.
 
 
 A separate total is calculated for each surface layer and then rated.  The total is the sum of each layer's average value times the number of inches in the layer for layers up to 60".
 
           A value < 3 gets a SEVERE rating.
           A value >= 3 and < 6 gets a MODERATE rating.
           A value >= 6 gets a SLIGHT rating.
 
 If there is a value rated SEVERE, then this property is rated SEVERE.  If there is a value rated MODERATE, then this property is rated MODERATE.  If there is a value rated SLIGHT, then this property is rated SLIGHT.  Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.

 8/Sum (100-% passing No. 10 sieve) and fraction >3 in.  Use   dominant condition for restrictive feature.

 Lines 8a and 9a are calculated together, and lines 8b and 9b are calculated together.

 Description of Calculation for lines 8a and 9a:
+_______________________________________________

 The values for % passing No. 10 sieve and fraction 3-10 inches given on the Soils-5 are examined.  These values are used in the calculations of weighted averages from 0-40 inches.

 % passing No. 10 sieve
+______________________

 The low value is examined for each layer within the given depths. The value used for each layer in the calculation depends on which of the following conditions is met first.

 If the low value is valid, then (100 - low value) is used.

 Otherwise an artificial value of 0 is used.

 Fraction 3-10 inches
+____________________

 The values are examined for each layer within the given depths and a high value is determined.  The high value used for each layer in the calculation depends on which of the following conditions is met first.

 If a single value of '99' is entered, then an artificial value of  100 is used.

 If a single value not equal to '99' is entered, then an artificial  value of 0 is used.

 Otherwise the high value is used.

 A separate weighted average is calculated for each surface layer for both % passing No. 10 sieve and fraction 3-10 inches.  For each surface layer, the two weighted averages are added together (call this SUM) and rated.

 To determine the dominant condition, a new weighted average from 0-40 inches is calculated for both % passing No. 10 sieve and fraction 3-10 inches.  The surface layer value used in each calculation is the maximum value over all surface layers.  If the weighted average for fraction 3-10 inches is >= the weighted average for % passing No. 10, then the restrictive term used is LARGE STONES.  Otherwise it is SMALL STONES.

           A SUM > 25 gets a POOR rating.
           A SUM > 5 and <= 25 gets a FAIR rating.
           A SUM <= 5 gets a GOOD rating.

 Description of Calculation for lines 8b and 9b:
+_______________________________________________

 This calculation is similar to that above, except we will assume that no surface layers are involved.

 A separate weighted average from 40-60 inches is calculated for both % passing No. 10 sieve and fraction 3-10 inches.  The two weighted averages are added together (call this SUM).

 If the weighted average for fraction 3-10 inches is >= the weighted average for % passing No. 10 sieve, then the following ratings apply:

           A SUM > 30 gets a POOR rating.
           A SUM > 15 and <= 30 gets a FAIR rating.
           A SUM <= 15 gets a GOOD rating.
 Otherwise the following ratings apply:
           A SUM > 50 gets a POOR rating.
           A SUM > 25 and <= 50 gets a FAIR rating.
           A SUM <= 25 gets a GOOD rating.
                     ---------------
 It is possible that Property No. 4, DEPTH TO BULK DENSITY, Property No. 8b, FRACTION >3 IN (40-60") and Property No. 9b, COARSE FRAGMENTS (40-60") may all have the same restrictive term, AREA RECLAIM.  At this point, a check must be made to ensure that this term will only appear in the final output at most once.

 If No. 4 is marked POOR, then No. 8b and No. 9b are cancelled out. Else if No. 8b is marked POOR, then No. 9b is cancelled out.  The same procedure is repeated for FAIR.

evaldesc:
This evaluation check percolation capacity of the soil.  The high, low, and representative values for sat_hydraulic_conductivity are selected for each horizon between 24 to 80 inches. This is chnage from the criteria listed below.

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
  Where the soil horizon property sat_hydraulic_conductivity < 4.0 micrometers/second (0.60 inches/hour)the evaluation is absolutely true and the restrictive feature is slow percolation.
        AND
  Where the soil horizon property sat_hydraulic_conductivity => 14.0 micrometers/second (2.00 inches/hour) the evaluation is absolutely false and the restrictive feature is not slow percolation.

If no data is entered, then an artificial default value(s) is used. 

Ames Description Prior to 1996:
                                                   |                           LIMITS                              |   RESTRICTIVE
     PROPERTY                      |  SLIGHT  | MODERATE |  SEVERE  |  FEATURE
 7. PERMEABILITY              2.0-6.0          I/0.6-2.0               <0.6         PERCS SLOWLY
    (IN/HR):    (24-60")            

    I/Recheck to see if rating should be SLIGHT.

 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________
 
 This property is calculated as if it were two separate properties.
 The calculation for the first line (PERCS SLOWLY) is:
 
 The values given on the Soils-5 for permeability are examined and a
 low value for each layer is determined.  The low value used for
 comparison depends on which of the following conditions is met
 first.
 
 If no data is entered, then an artificial value of 100 is used.
 
 If the entry is of the form '<xx', then an artificial value of 0 is
  used.
 
 Otherwise the low value is used.
 
 The layers within the given depths are examined.  If surface layers
 are included in these depths, each is rated separately.  Then each
 sublayer is rated to determine the worst sublayer rating.  The
 rating algorithm used on each layer is as follows:

           A value < 0.6 gets a SEVERE rating
           A value >= 0.6 and < 2.0 gets a MODERATE rating.
           A value >= 2.0 gets a SLIGHT rating.
 
 If surface layers are not involved, then this property is rated the
 same as the worst sublayer rating.
 
 If surface layers are involved, then the following applies.  If the
 worst sublayer rating is SEVERE, then this property is rated SEVERE
 and no phasing will be done, regardless of the surface layer
 ratings.
 
 If the worst sublayer rating is MODERATE, then this property is
 rated MODERATE if there is any SLIGHT or MODERATE surface layer
 rating, and it is rated SEVERE if there is any SEVERE surface layer
 rating.  Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one
 rating is given.
 
 If the worst sublayer rating is SLIGHT, then this property is rated
 SLIGHT if there is any SLIGHT surface layer rating, MODERATE if
 there is any MODERATE surface layer rating, and SEVERE if there is
 any SEVERE surface layer rating.  Phasing will be done using texture
 terms if more than one rating is given.

Ames Description prior to  1996:
____________________________________________________________________
                                                             |             LIMITS                                              |RESTRICTIVE
+                                                         ________________________________
     PROPERTY                              |  SLIGHT  | MODERATE |  SEVERE     |  FEATURE
 +___________________________________________________________________
 
 6. 5/, 9/, 10/AASHTO                     <5                    5-8                        >8               LOW  STRENGTH
    GROUP INDEX NUMBER                                   
    
 5/If in Kaolinitic family, rate one class better if experience confirms.
 9/Thickest layer between 10 and 40 inches.
 10/GIN=(F-35)[.2+.005(LL-40)]+.01(F-15)(PI-10) where F=% passing No. 200 sieve.  If F<=35 and PI>=11, use only part 2 of equation.  Use median values.
 
 
 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________
 
 The layer with the most inches between 10 and 40 inches is determined.  This could be a surface layer or a sublayer.  The GIN is calculated for the appropriate layer(s) according to the given algorithm.
 
 To calculate the GIN, median values are needed for the following: percent passing No. 200 sieve (F), liquid limit (LL), and plasticity index (PI).  A median is calculated by adding the low and high values, then dividing by 2, unless special conditions exist.  The median calculation is given below for each of these three variables.
 
 Percent passing No. 200 sieve:
+______________________________
 
 If no valid data is entered, then an artificial value of 0 is used as the median.
 
 If a single value is entered, then this value is used as the median.
 
 Otherwise the median is calculated using the low and high values.
 

 
 Liquid limit:
+_____________
 
 If the entry is of the form '<xxx', then a median is calculated using 0 and xxx. 
 If the entry is of the form '>xxx', then a median is calculated using xxx and 100.
  If no valid data is entered, then an artificial value of 0 is used as the median. 
 If a single value is entered, then this value is used as the median. 
 Otherwise the median is calculated using the low and high values.
 
 Plasticity index:
+_________________
 
 If the entry is of the form '<xxx', then a median is calculated using 0 and xxx. 
 If the entry is of the form '>xxx', then a median is calculated using xxx and 100. 
 If the entry is of the form 'NP', then an artificial value of 0 is used as the median. 
 
 If the entry is of the form 'NP-xxx', then a median is calculated using 0 and xxx. 
 If no valid data is entered, then an artificial value of 0 is used as the median. 
 If a single value is entered, then this value is used as the median. 
 Otherwise the median is calculated using the low and high values. 
 After the GIN is calculated, the layer(s) being examined are rated according to the following algorithm: 
    If GIN > 8, then a SEVERE rating is given.
    If GIN > 5 and <= 8, then a MODERATE rating is given.
    If GIN <= 5, then a SLIGHT rating is given.
 
 If the thickest layer is a sublayer, then this property is rated the same as this sublayer's rating.  If minerology on the Soils-5 equals '28' (Kaolinitic), then a MODERATE rating is upgraded to SLIGHT, and a SEVERE rating is upgraded to MODERATE.
 
 If the thickest layer is a surface layer, then this property is rated SLIGHT if there is any SLIGHT surface layer rating, MODERATE if there is any MODERATE surface layer rating, and SEVERE if there is any SEVERE surface layer rating.  If minerology on the Soils-5 equals '28' (Kaolinitic), then a MODERATE rating is upgraded to SLIGHT, and a SEVERE rating is upgraded to MODERATE.  Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.

evaldesc:
This evaluation checks the maximum values of greater than 2mm and less than 3" (75mm) fraction for the 0-30" (0-75cm) depth of soil. 

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
 
  Where the total of the soil component horizon coarse fragment property between 2 and 75mm is greater than 75% the evaluation is absolutely true and "TOO GRAVELLY" is a restrictive feature.
     AND
  Where the total of the soil component horizon coarse fragment property between 2 and 75mm is less than 50% the evaluation is absolutely false and "TOO GRAVELLY" is not a restrictive feature.

Ames Description prior to  1996:
1___________________________________________________________________
                       |             LIMITS             |RESTRICTIVE
+                       ________________________________
     PROPERTY          |  SLIGHT  | MODERATE |  SEVERE  |  FEATURE
                       |          |          |          |
+___________________________________________________________________
 
 6. % BY WEIGHT 2MM-3"    <50       50-75       >75      TOO GRAVELLY
    (0-30")                                               
  
 
 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________
 
 Each surface layer is rated separately according to the following algorithm: 
     A value > 75 gets a SEVERE rating.
     A value > 50 and <= 75 gets a MODERATE rating.
     A value <= 50 gets a SLIGHT rating.
 
 Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.

taxonomic_temp_regime	growing season months
---------------------	---------------------
cryic or pergelic	July and August

frigid or mesic		May, June, July, 
			August, and September

thermic or		March, April, May, 
hyperthermic		June, July, August,
			September, and October

isothermic,		February, March, April,
isohyperthermic,	May, June, July, August,

			November

evaldesc:
This evaluation checks for a saturated or wet condition within a depth of 90 cm (3 feet) of the soil surface.  The water moisture status for all layers are examined and those saturated or wet layers are evalutated for depth.  If a saturated condition occurs within 30 cm (1 foot) of the soil surface than wetness is a limitation.

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
  Where soil_moisture_status is wet and the depth to soil_moist_depth_to_top is greater than 90 cm (3 foot) the evaluation is absolutely true.
   OR
  Where soil_moisture_status is wet and the depth to  soil_moist_depth_to_top  is less than 30 cm (1 feet) the evaluation is absolutely false.

If the soil_moisture_status is not wet or null, then the property asumption is that soil_moist_depth_to_top is NULL and no water table is present.

Ames Description Prior to 1996:

                                                     |                                 LIMITS                            |RESTRICTIVE
+                                                   ________________________________
     PROPERTY                        |   GOOD   |   FAIR   |   POOR   |                        FEATURE
 +___________________________________________________________________

 8. DEPTH TO HIGH WATER
    WATER TABLE (FT)           >3             1-3             <1                                   WETNESS

 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________

 The low value in the range of values given on the Soils-5 for depth to high water table is examined.  The value used for comparison depends on which of the following conditions is met first.

 If no data is entered, then an artificial value of 99.9 is used.

 Otherwise the low value is used.

           A value >= 1 and < 3 gets a FAIR rating.

This evaluation checks for the presence of permafrost and if present evaluates permafrost depth.  The component data are check for restriction_kind = "permafrost" and restriction_depth_to_top is evaluated.

A soil can be a complete or partial member of the set of soils that are limited by the depth to permafrost and PERMAFROST is the set's restrictive feature.  If the depth to permafrost is less than 50 cm (20 inches), then the soil is a complete member of the set.  If the depth to permafrost is greater than 50 cm (20 inches) and less than 100 cm (40 inches) then the soil is a partial member of the set.  A soil that has permafrost at a depth of more than 100 cm (40 inches) is not a member of the set.

evalname: AK3:Depth to Hard Bedrock 100 to 150cm (40 to 60")
evaldesc:
This evaluation checks for the presence of bedrock within a specified depth.  The component data are check for restriction_kind = "bedrock (lithic)" and restriction_depth_to_top is evaluated.

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
  Where the soil component property restriction_kind = "bedrock (lithic)" and the restriction_depth_to_top is less then 100 cm (40 inches) then the evaluation is absolutely true and depth to hard bedrock is a restrictive feature.
     AND
  Where the soil component property restriction_kind = "bedrock (lithic)" and the restriction_depth_to_top is greater then 150 cm (60 inches) then the evaluation is absolutely false and depth to hard bedrock is not a restrictive feature.

                       |             LIMITS             |RESTRICTIVE
+                       ________________________________
     PROPERTY          |  SLIGHT  | MODERATE |  SEVERE  |  FEATURE
                       |          |          |          |
+___________________________________________________________________

    (IN):                                                ROCK
    HARD                   >60       40-60       <40 
 
 The bedrock hardness and the values given on the Soils-5 for depth to rock are examined and the low value determined.  The low value used for comparison depends on which of the following conditions is met first.
 
 If the entry is '>60', then an artificial value of 100 is used.
 
 If the low value is valid, then the low value is used.
 
 Otherwise an artificial value of 100 is used.
 
 If the bedrock hardness equals (hard), then the following
 ratings apply:
 

           A value < 40 gets a SEVERE rating.
           A value >= 40 and < 60 gets a MODERATE rating.
           A value >= 60 gets a SLIGHT rating.

evaldesc:
This evaluation checks slope.

A soil can be a complete or partial member of the set of soils that are too steep and SLOPE is the set's restrictive feature.  If the slope is greater than 15 percent, then the soil is a complete member of the set.  If slope is greater than 8 percent and less than 15 percent then the soil is a partial member of the set.  A soil that has slope less than 8 percent is not a member of the set.

This evaluation checks for a moderately sloping condition.  The high, low, and representative values for Slope are selected.

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
  Where the soil property slope_gradient > 8 the evaluation is absolutely true and the restrictive feature is slope.
     OR
  Where the soil property slope_gradient < 4 the evaluation is absolutely false and the restrictive feature is not slope.

If no data is entered then the property is NULL and the default condition is used.

Ames Description Prior to 1996:
 ___________________________________________________________________
                       |             LIMITS             |RESTRICTIVE
                        ________________________________
     PROPERTY          |  SLIGHT  | MODERATE |  SEVERE  |  FEATURE 
+___________________________________________________________________
 
 4. SLOPE                  <4          4-8        >8     SLOPE
    (SURFACE, PCT)
  
 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________
 
 The low and high values in the slope range given on the Soils-5 are examined.
 
    A high slope > 8 gets a SEVERE rating.
    A low slope < 8 and a high slope > 4 gets a MODERATE rating.
    A low slope < 4 gets a SLIGHT rating.
 
 Phasing will be done using slope terms if more than one rating is given.

    AND

 subsidence is examined.  The low value used for comparison depends
 on which of the following conditions is met first.

This evaluation is crisp and checks for UNIFIED equal to "OL", "OH", or "PT".

Where unified_soil_classification equals "OL", "OH", or "PT" the evaluation is absolutely true and LOW STRENGTH is a restrictive feature.
    AND
Where unified_soil_classification does not equal "OL", "OH", or "PT" the evaluation is absolutely false and LOW STRENGTH is not a restrictive feature.

 Ames prior to 1996

                                                |                           LIMITS                              |  RESTRICTIVE
     PROPERTY                   |  SLIGHT  | MODERATE |  SEVERE  |  FEATURE
 8. UNIFIED (10-40")         ---                ---               OL, OH, PT   EXCESS HUMUS
 
 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________
 
 The unified values given on the Soils-5 are examined for the layers within 10-40 inches.  If surface layers are included in these depths, each is rated separately.  Then each sublayer is rated to determine the worst sublayer rating.  The rating algorithm used on each layer is as follows:
 
 If OL, OH, or PT is listed as a texture, then a SEVERE rating is given.
 Otherwise a SLIGHT rating is given.
 
 If surface layers are not involved, then this property is rated the same as the worst sublayer rating.
 
 If surface layers are involved, then the following applies.  If the worst sublayer rating is SEVERE, then this property is rated SEVERE and no phasing will be done, regardless of the surface layer ratings.
 
 
 If the worst sublayer rating is SLIGHT, then this property is rated SLIGHT if there is any SLIGHT surface layer rating, and it is rated SEVERE if there is any SEVERE surface layer rating.  Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.

evaldesc:
This evaluation checks the greater than 3 inch fraction of the soil.  The weighted average of the component horizon rock_frag_3_to_10_in and rock_frag_greater_than_10_in is calculated for the 0 to 100 cm (40in) depth of the soil and the result is checked and evaluated.

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
 
  Where the total of each layers weighted average of the soil component horizon properties rock_frag_3_to_10_in and rock_frag_greater_than_10_in from 0 to a depth of 100cm (40in) is greater than 50% the evaluation is absolutely true and "LARGE STONES" is a restrictive feature.
     AND
  Where the total of each layers weighted average of the soil component horizon properties rock_frag_3_to_10_in and rock_frag_greater_than_10_in from 0 to a depth of 100cm (40in) less than 25% the evaluation is absolutely false and "LARGE STONES" is not a restrictive feature.

If no data is entered, then a default value of 0 is used.

Ames Description prior to  1996:

                                                  |                             LIMITS                            |  RESTRICTIVE
     PROPERTY                     |  SLIGHT  | MODERATE |  SEVERE  |  FEATURE
 9. 1/FRACTION >3 IN       <25                25-50                    >50            LARGE STONES
      (WT PCT)        
 
 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________
 
 The values given on the Soils-5 for fraction 3-10 inches are examined and a high value for each layer is determined.  The high value used in the calculation depends on which of the following conditions is met first.
 
 If a single value of '99' is entered, then an artificial value of 100 is used.
 
 If a single value not equal to '99' is entered, then an artificial value of 0 is used.
 
 Otherwise the high value is used.
 
 A separate weighted average to 40 inches is calculated for each surface layer.
 
           A weighted average > 50 gets a SEVERE rating.
           A weighted average > 25 and <= 50 gets a MODERATE rating.
           A weighted average <= 25 gets a SLIGHT rating.
 
 Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.

evalname: AK3:Shrink-swell of Thickest Layer in 25-150cm or Bedrock
evaldesc:
This evaluation evaluates the product of the shrink-swell value of the thickest horizon in the 25 to 150cm range.

If the shrink-swell value for the thickest layer between 25-150cm is between 3 and 6, the evaluation returns a value between 0 and 1.

When the shrink-swell value for the thickest layer between 25 to 150cm is > 6 (HIGH or VERY HIGH) the evaluation is absolutely true and the restrictive feature is SHRINK-SWELL.
	AND
When the shrink-swell value for the thickest layer between 25 to 150cm is <3 (LOW), the evaluation is absolutely false and the restrictive feature is not SHRINK-SWELL.


Ames Description Prior to 1996:
                                                      |                            LIMITS                                       |  RESTRICTIVE
     PROPERTY                         |  SLIGHT  | MODERATE |  SEVERE            |  FEATURE
 
 9. 9/SHRINK-SWELL         LOW             MODERATE      HIGH,                  SHRINK-
                                                                                                              VERY HIGH       SWELL
 
 9/Thickest layer between 10 and 60 inches.
 
 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________
 
 The layer with the most inches between 10 and 60 inches is determined.  This could be a surface layer or a sublayer.  The shrink-swell values given on the Soils-5 are examined for the appropriate layer(s).
 
 The layer(s) being examined are rated according to the following algorithm:
 
 If the shrink-swell value equals '1' (HIGH) or '5' (VERY HIGH), then a SEVERE rating is given.  If the shrink-swell value equals '3' (MODERATE), then a MODERATE rating is given. Otherwise a SLIGHT rating is given.
 
 If the thickest layer is a sublayer, then this property is rated the same as this sublayer's rating.
 
 If the thickest layer is a surface layer, then this property is rated SLIGHT if there is any SLIGHT surface layer rating, MODERATE if there is any MODERATE surface layer rating, and SEVERE if there is any SEVERE surface layer rating.  Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.
propname: AK3:SHRINK-SWELL THICKEST LAYER  25-180cm OR ABOVE ROCK

evaldesc:
This evaluation is crisp and checks for UNIFIED equal to "OL", "OH", or "PT".

Where unified_soil_classification equals "OL", "OH", or "PT" the evaluation is absolutely true and LOW STRENGTH is a restrictive feature.
    AND
Where unified_soil_classification does not equal "OL", "OH", or "PT" the evaluation is absolutely false and LOW STRENGTH is not a restrictive feature.

 Ames prior to 1996

                                                |                           LIMITS                              |  RESTRICTIVE
     PROPERTY                   |  SLIGHT  | MODERATE |  SEVERE  |  FEATURE
 9. UNIFIED                             ---                  ---           OL, OH, PT     LOW
     (BOTTOM LAYER)                                                                                   STRENGTH
 
 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________
 
The unified values given on the Soils-5 are examined for the bottom layer.  The bottom layer may be a surface layer or a sublayer.
 
The bottom layer is rated according to the following algorithm:
 
If OL, OH, or PT is listed as a unified entry, then a SEVERE rating is given.

Otherwise a SLIGHT rating is given.
 
If the bottom layer is a sublayer, then this property is rated the same as this sublayer's rating.
 
If the bottom layer is a surface layer, then this property is rated SLIGHT if there is any SLIGHT surface layer rating, and it is rated SEVERE if there is any SEVERE surface layer rating.  Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.

This evaluation checks aashto_group_index.  The component data are check for aashto_group_index index number.

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
  Where the soil component property aashto_group_index is greaer then 8 then the evaluation is absolutely true and LOW STRENGTH is a restrictive feature.
     AND
  Where the soil component property aashto_group_index is less then 5 then the evaluation is absolutely false and LOW STRENGTH is not a restrictive feature.


Ames Description prior to  1996:
____________________________________________________________________
                                                             |             LIMITS                                              |RESTRICTIVE
+                                                         ________________________________
     PROPERTY                              |  SLIGHT  | MODERATE |  SEVERE     |  FEATURE
 +___________________________________________________________________
 
 6. 5/, 9/, 10/AASHTO                     <5                    5-8                        >8               LOW  STRENGTH
    GROUP INDEX NUMBER                                   
    
 5/If in Kaolinitic family, rate one class better if experience confirms.
 9/Thickest layer between 10 and 40 inches.
 10/GIN=(F-35)[.2+.005(LL-40)]+.01(F-15)(PI-10) where F=% passing No. 200 sieve.  If F<=35 and PI>=11, use only part 2 of equation.  Use median values.
 
 
 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________
 
 The layer with the most inches between 10 and 40 inches is determined.  This could be a surface layer or a sublayer.  The GIN is calculated for the appropriate layer(s) according to the given algorithm.
 
 To calculate the GIN, median values are needed for the following: percent passing No. 200 sieve (F), liquid limit (LL), and plasticity index (PI).  A median is calculated by adding the low and high values, then dividing by 2, unless special conditions exist.  The median calculation is given below for each of these three variables.
 
 Percent passing No. 200 sieve:
+______________________________
 
 If no valid data is entered, then an artificial value of 0 is used as the median.
 
 If a single value is entered, then this value is used as the median.
 
 Otherwise the median is calculated using the low and high values.
 

 
 Liquid limit:
+_____________
 
 If the entry is of the form '<xxx', then a median is calculated using 0 and xxx. 
 If the entry is of the form '>xxx', then a median is calculated using xxx and 100.
  If no valid data is entered, then an artificial value of 0 is used as the median. 
 If a single value is entered, then this value is used as the median. 
 Otherwise the median is calculated using the low and high values.
 
 Plasticity index:
+_________________
 
 If the entry is of the form '<xxx', then a median is calculated using 0 and xxx. 
 If the entry is of the form '>xxx', then a median is calculated using xxx and 100. 
 If the entry is of the form 'NP', then an artificial value of 0 is used as the median. 
 
 If the entry is of the form 'NP-xxx', then a median is calculated using 0 and xxx. 
 If no valid data is entered, then an artificial value of 0 is used as the median. 
 If a single value is entered, then this value is used as the median. 
 Otherwise the median is calculated using the low and high values. 
 After the GIN is calculated, the layer(s) being examined are rated according to the following algorithm: 
    If GIN > 8, then a SEVERE rating is given.
    If GIN > 5 and <= 8, then a MODERATE rating is given.
    If GIN <= 5, then a SLIGHT rating is given.
 
 If the thickest layer is a sublayer, then this property is rated the same as this sublayer's rating.  If minerology on the Soils-5 equals '28' (Kaolinitic), then a MODERATE rating is upgraded to SLIGHT, and a SEVERE rating is upgraded to MODERATE.
 
 If the thickest layer is a surface layer, then this property is rated SLIGHT if there is any SLIGHT surface layer rating, MODERATE if there is any MODERATE surface layer rating, and SEVERE if there is any SEVERE surface layer rating.  If minerology on the Soils-5 equals '28' (Kaolinitic), then a MODERATE rating is upgraded to SLIGHT, and a SEVERE rating is upgraded to MODERATE.  Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.
propname: AASHTO GROUP INDEX NUMBER THICKEST LAYER IN DEPTH 10-40 in.

evaldesc:
This evaluation checks the maximum clay content for all layers within a depth of 50 to 150 cm (20 to 60 inches). 
                                     
Where the maximum clay content is greater than 60% within a depth of 50 to 150 cm (20 to 60 inches) the evaluation is absolutely true and the restrictive feature is TOO CLAYEY. 
    AND
Where the maximum clay content is less than 40% within a depth of 50 to 150 cm (20 to 60 inches) the evaluation is absolutely false and the restrictive feature is not TOO CLAYEY. 
 
 Ames Description prior to 1996:
 
 
                                                  |                           LIMITS                              | RESTRICTIVE 
     PROPERTY                     |  SLIGHT  | MODERATE |  SEVERE  |  FEATURE 
 5. USDA TEXTURE           ---                 C, SIC                  ---           TOO CLAYEY 
    (20-60") 
 
  Description of Calculation: 
+___________________________ 
 
 The textures given on the Soils-5 are examined for the layers within 20-60 inches.  If surface layers are included in these depths, each is rated separately.  Then each sublayer is rated to determine the worst sublayer rating.  The rating algorithm used on each layer is as follows: 
 
If C or SIC is listed as a texture, then a MODERATE rating is given.  Otherwise a SLIGHT rating is given. 
 
If surface layers are not involved, then this property is rated the same as the worst sublayer rating. 
 
If surface layers are involved, then the following applies.  If the worst sublayer rating is MODERATE, then this property is rated  MODERATE. 
 
If the worst sublayer rating is SLIGHT, then this property is rated  SLIGHT if there is any SLIGHT surface layer rating, and it is rated MODERATE if there is any MODERATE surface layer rating.  Phasing  will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.

This evaluation is crisp and checks for the soil order Vertisols.
 
Where taxonomic_order equals vertisols the evaluation is absolutely true and the restrictive feature is CUTBANKS CAVE.
    AND
Where taxonomic_order does not equal vertisols or is NULL the evaluation is absolutely false and the restrictive feature is not CUTBANKS CAVE.
 
 
 
Ames Description prior to 1996: 

 	                      |             LIMITS      		            	 |RESTRICTIVE
     PROPERTY               |  SLIGHT  | MODERATE |  SEVERE 	 |  FEATURE
 6. SOIL ORDER             ---	        --- 	             VERTISOLS    	   CUTBANKS   CAVE
 
 The great group given on the Soils-5 is examined.
 
 If the first character of the great group equals 'V' (Vertisols),
 then this property is rated SEVERE.
 
 Otherwise this property is rated SLIGHT.
 
                     ---------------
 
 If Property No. 4, USDA TEXTURE, produced a SEVERE rating, then a
 SEVERE rating here will be cancelled out to prevent the same two
 restrictive terms, CUTBANKS CAVE, from appearing in the final
 output.

This evaluation is crisp and checks the texture_class for all layers. 
 
Where texture_class equals SIL for any layer the evaluation is absolutely true and the restrictive feature is CUTBANKS CAVE.
    AND
Where texture_class does not equal SIL or is NULL for all layers the evaluation is absolutely false and the restrictive feature is not CUTBANKS CAVE.

    (20-60")                                                                                                      CAVE
                                             
 VII/If loess, rating should be SLIGHT.
 
 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________
 
The textures given on the Soils-5 are examined for the layers within 20-60 inches.  If surface layers are included in these depths, each is rated separately.  Then each sublayer is rated to determine the worst sublayer rating.  The rating algorithm used on each layer is as follows:
 
If SI is listed as a texture, then a MODERATE rating is given.

Otherwise a SLIGHT rating is given.
 
If surface layers are not involved, then this property is rated the same as the worst sublayer rating.
 
If surface layers are involved, then the following applies.  If the worst sublayer rating is SEVERE, then this property is rated SEVERE and no phasing will be done, regardless of the surface layer ratings.
 
If the worst sublayer rating is MODERATE, then this property is rated MODERATE if there is any SLIGHT or MODERATE surface layer rating.  Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.
 
If the worst sublayer rating is SLIGHT, then this property is rated SLIGHT if there is any SLIGHT surface layer rating, and MODERATE if there is any MODERATE surface layer rating. The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:

 Description of Calculation for Thickest Layer:
+______________________________________________

 The layer with the most inches between 10 and 60 inches is determined.  This could be a surface layer or a sublayer.  The unified values given on the Soils-5 are examined for the appropriate layer(s).

 The layer(s) being examined are rated according to the following algorithm:

 If SW, SP, SW-SM, or SP-SM is listed as a unified entry, or if GW, GP, GW-GM or GP-GM is listed as a unified entry and footnote 13 applies (see following description of footnote 13), then a PROBABLE rating is given.

 Otherwise an IMPROBABLE rating is given.

 If the thickest layer is a sublayer, then this property is rated the same as this sublayer's rating.

 If the thickest layer is a surface layer, then this property is rated PROBABLE if there is any PROBABLE surface layer rating.  If there is none, then it is rated IMPROBABLE.

 Restrictive feature terms are assigned appropriately.



 Description of Calculation for Bottom Layer:
+____________________________________________

 If the bottom layer has no data, then this calculation is skipped and the ratings for the thickest layer are chosen.

 Otherwise, this calculation is the same as that for the thickest layer, except it is done for the bottom layer.  The bottom layer, like the thickest layer, may be a surface layer or a sublayer.

1

 Calculations for Footnotes 13 and 14
+____________________________________

 To do the calculations for these footnotes, the values given on the Soils-5 for % passing No. 4 sieve and % passing No. 200 sieve are examined.

 % passing No. 4 sieve
+_____________________

 Assign values to No_4_Lo and No_4_Hi.

 If no data is entered, then No_4_Lo = 100 and No_4_Hi = 100.

 If a single value, say x, is entered, then No_4_Lo = x and No_4_Hi = x.

 If the entry is a normal range, say x-y, then No_4_Lo = x and No_4_Hi = y.

 % passing No. 200 sieve
+_______________________

 Assign values to No_200_Lo and No_200_Hi.

 If no data is entered, then No_200_Lo = 0 and No_200_Hi = 0.

 If a single value, say x, is entered, then No_200_Lo = x and No_200_Hi = x.

 If the entry is a normal range, say x-y, then No_200_Lo = x and  No_200_Hi = y.


 Once these values have been assigned, the following calculations take place.

 No_4_Lo - No_200_Lo = Lo
 No_4_Hi - No_200_Hi = Hi

 maximum(Lo,Hi) = max

 If max > 25 then footnote 13 applies.
 If max <= 25 then footnote 14 applies.

For Property No. 2, UNIFIED, the best ratings must be chosen between those calculated for the thickest layer and the bottom layer.

 If both the thickest and bottom layers are rated PROBABLE, then the bottom layer is chosen.

 If the thickest layer is rated PROBABLE and the bottom layer is rated IMPROBABLE, then the thickest layer is chosen.

 If the bottom layer is rated PROBABLE and the thickest layer is rated IMPROBABLE, then the bottom layer is chosen.

 If neither the thickest or bottom layer is rated PROBABLE, then they must both be rated IMPROBABLE and the bottom layer is chosen.

 If the ratings for the thickest layer were chosen, then the calculations on the following page for Property No. 3, LAYER THICKNESS, are done.

 No_4_Hi - No_200_Hi = Hi

 maximum(Lo,Hi) = max

 If max > 25 then footnote 13 applies.
 If max <= 25 then footnote 14 applies.

For Property No. 2, UNIFIED, the best ratings must be chosen between those calculated for the thickest layer and the bottom layer.

 If both the thickest and bottom layers are rated PROBABLE, then the bottom layer is chosen.

 If the thickest layer is rated PROBABLE and the bottom layer is rated IMPROBABLE, then the thickest layer is chosen.

 If the bottom layer is rated PROBABLE and the thickest layer is rated IMPROBABLE, then the bottom layer is chosen.

 If neither the thickest or bottom layer is rated PROBABLE, then they must both be rated IMPROBABLE and the bottom layer is chosen.

 If the ratings for the thickest layer were chosen, then the calculations on the following page for Property No. 3, LAYER THICKNESS, are done.

evalname: IA - Wet, Ground Water Near Surface (60 - 120cm)
evaldesc:
This evaluation checks for a saturated or wet condition within a depth of 120 cm (4 feet) of the soil surface.  The water moisture status for all layers are examined and those saturated or wet layers are evalutated for depth.  If a saturated condition occurs within 60 cm (2 feet) of the soil surface than wetness is a limitation.

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
  Where soil_moisture_status is wet and the depth to soil_moist_depth_to_top is less than 60 cm (2 feet) the evaluation is absolutely true.
   OR
  Where soil_moisture_status is wet and the depth to  soil_moist_depth_to_top  is greater than 120 cm (4 feet) the evaluation is absolutely false.

If the soil_moisture_status is not wet or null, then the property asumption is that soil_moist_depth_to_top is NULL and no water table is present.

Ames Description Prior to 1996:

 ___________________________________________________________________
                       |             LIMITS             |RESTRICTIVE
+                       ________________________________
     PROPERTY          |  SLIGHT  | MODERATE |  SEVERE  |  FEATURE
                       |          |          |          |
+___________________________________________________________________
 
 3b:  WATER TABLE (FT)       >4         2-4        <2      WETNESS
 
The low value in the range of values given on the Soils-5 for depth to high water table is examined.  The value used for comparison depends on which of the following conditions are met first.
 
 If no data is entered, then an artificial value of 99.9 is used.
 
 Otherwise the low value is used.
 
           A value < 2 gets a SEVERE rating.
           A value >= 2 and < 4 gets a MODERATE rating.
           A value >= 4 gets a SLIGHT rating.

This evaluation is crisp and checks the texture_modifier_and_class for all layers. 
 
Where texture_class equals coarse sands, fine sands, very fine sands or sandy gravel for any layer the evaluation is absolutely true and the restrictive feature is CUTBANKS CAVE.
    AND
Where texture_class does not equal coarse sands, fine sands, very fine sands or sandy gravel or is NULL for all layers the evaluation is absolutely false and the restrictive feature is not CUTBANKS CAVE.
 
 
 Ames Description prior to 1996: 

                                   	    |             LIMITS      		               |RESTRICTIVE

 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________
 
The textures given on the Soils-5 are examined for the layers within 20-60 inches.  If surface layers are included in these depths, each is rated separately.  Then each sublayer is rated to determine the worst sublayer rating.  The rating algorithm used on each layer is as follows:
 
If COS, S, FS, VFS, LCOS, LS, LFS, LVFS, G, or SG is listed as a texture, then a SEVERE rating is given.

Otherwise a SLIGHT rating is given.
 
If surface layers are not involved, then this property is rated the same as the worst sublayer rating.
 
If surface layers are involved, then the following applies.  If the worst sublayer rating is SEVERE, then this property is rated SEVERE and no phasing will be done, regardless of the surface layer ratings.
 
If the worst sublayer rating is MODERATE, then this property is rated MODERATE if there is any SLIGHT or MODERATE surface layer rating, and it is rated SEVERE if there is any SEVERE surface layer
 rating.  Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.
 
If the worst sublayer rating is SLIGHT, then this property is rated SLIGHT if there is any SLIGHT surface layer rating, MODERATE if there is any MODERATE surface layer rating, and SEVERE if there is any SEVERE surface layer rating.  Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given. rating, and it is rated SEVERE if there is any SEVERE surface layer rating.
