evaldesc:
This evaluation was edited to call a property script for Delmarva which looks for third bar bulk densities greater than 1.9 g/cc rather than 1.8 g/cc as was written in the Ames 1996 criteria.  This revision was made to avoid "hard to reclaim" ratings for the sandy layers found in the Delmarva soils that have relatively high bulk densities without being compacted or fragic. CMB

_______________________________________________________________________________________

This evaluation is checks the depth of  the first layer that has bulk density greater than 1.8.
 
Where the depth to the first layer with a bulk_density_one_third_bar greater then 1.8 is greater than 100cm (40in) the evaluation is absolutely true and  HIGH BULK DENSITY is not a restrictive feature. 
    AND
Where the depth to the first layer with a bulk_density_one_third_bar greater then 1.8 is less than 50cm (20in) the evaluation is absolutely false and HIGH BULK DENSITY is a restrictive feature.  
 
Ames prior to 1996:
1___________________________________________________________________
                                                 |                     LIMITS                            |RESTRICTIVE
+                                              ________________________________
     PROPERTY                   |   GOOD   |   FAIR   |   POOR   |         FEATURE
+___________________________________________________________________

 4. DEPTH TO BULK          >40            20-40       <20    	        AREA RECLAIM
    DENSITY > 1.8                                        
    (G/CC) (IN)

 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________

 The values given on the Soils-5 for bulk density and the upper depth of each layer are examined.  A value for bulk density is determined for each layer depending on which of the following conditions is met first.

 If no data is entered, then an artificial value of 0 is used.

 If the entry is a single number or is of the form '<xx', then the  single value entered is used.

 If the entry is of the form '>xx', then an artificial value of 99.99  is used.

 If the entry is a normal range, then the high value is used.

    If any layer has a value > 1.8 and an upper layer depth < 20,  then a POOR rating is given.
    If any layer has a value > 1.8 and an upper layer depth >= 20  and < 40, then a FAIR rating is given.
    Otherwise a GOOD rating is given.

 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________
 
 The values given on the Soils-5 for fraction 3-10 inches are examined and a high value for each layer is determined.  The high value used in the calculation depends on which of the following conditions is met first.
 
 If a single value of '99' is entered, then an artificial value of 100 is used.

evaldesc:
This evaluation checks for a perched saturated or wet condition within a depth of 120 cm (4 feet) of the soil surface.  The water moisture status for all layers are examined and those saturated or wet layers are evalutated for depth.

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
  Where soil_moisture_status is wet, has a dry layer below the wet layer, and the depth to soil_moist_depth_to_top is less than 60 cm (2 feet) the evaluation is absolutely true and WETNESS is a restrictive feature.
   OR
  Where soil_moisture_status is wet, has a dry layer below the wet layer, and the depth to  soil_moist_depth_to_top  is greater than >= 120 cm (4 feet) the evaluation is absolutely false and WETNESS is not a restrictive feature.

If the soil_moisture_status is not wet or null, then the property asumption is that soil_moist_depth_to_top is NULL and no water table is present.

Ames Description Prior to 1996:
                                                     |                            LIMITS                             |   RESTRICTIVE
     PROPERTY                        |  SLIGHT  | MODERATE |  SEVERE  |  FEATURE
 6. DEPTH TO HIGH                     >4                   2-4                   <2              WETNESS
    WATER TABLE (FT)
         PERCHED 

 Description of Calculation:
 
 The water table kind and the low value in the range of values given on the Soils-5 for depth to high water table are examined.  If a '+'  occurs in the low value, then there is ponding and a SEVERE rating is given.  Otherwise the value used for comparison depends on which of the following conditions is met first.
 
 If no data is entered, then an artificial value of 99.9 is used. 
 Otherwise the low value is used.
  
 If the water table kind is perched, then the following ratings apply: 
           A value < 2 gets a SEVERE rating.
           A value >= 2 and < 4 gets a MODERATE rating.
           A value >= 4 gets a SLIGHT rating.

This evaluation checks the available water of the soil.  The weight average of the component horizon available_water_capacity is calculated for the soil and the result is check and evaluated.

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
 
  Where the total of each layers weighted average of the soil component horizon property available_water_capacity to a depth of 100cm (40in) is less than 5.0cm (2in) the evaluation is absolutely true and "DROUGHTY" is a restrictive feature.
     AND

Ames Description prior to  1996:

 9. 1/AVAILABLE WATER             >.10               .05-.10              <.05            DROUGHTY
      CAPACITY (IN/IN)                    
 
 1/Weighted average to 40 inches.
  
 Description of Calculation:
 
 The values given on the Soils-5 for available water are examined and a low value for each layer is determined.  The low value for each layer is used in a weighted average calculation to 40 inches.  Each low value used in the calculation depends on which of the following conditions is met first.
 
 If no data is entered, then the layer is skipped. 
 If the entry is of the form '<xx', then an artificial value of 0 is  used.
 
 Otherwise the low value is used.
 
 A separate weighted average to 40 inches is calculated for each surface layer and then rated.  If for some reason the total thickness used in the weighted average calculation is 0, then it is assumed that a weighted average of 1 was calculated.  If a weighted average could not be calculated due to missing data, then it is assumed that a weighted average of 100 was calculated.
 
      A weighted average < .05 gets a SEVERE rating.
      A weighted average >= .05 and < .10 gets a MODERATE rating.
      A weighted average >= .10 gets a SLIGHT rating.

 If there is a weighted average rating of SEVERE, then this property is rated SEVERE.  If there is a weighted average rating of MODERATE, then this property is rated MODERATE.  If there is a weighted average rating of SLIGHT, then this property is rated SLIGHT.  Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.

evaldesc:
This evaluation checks the soil surface reaction (pH).  The surface horizon ph_1_1_water check and evaluated.  Modified 7/98 to reflect the criteria in the Ag Waste Mang. Handbook

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
 
  Where the surface soil component horizon property ph_1_1_water is less than 3.5 the evaluation is absolutely true and "TOO ACID" is a restrictive feature.
     AND
  Where the surface soil component horizon property ph_1_1_water is greater than 6.5 the evaluation is absolutely false and "TOO ACID" is not a restrictive feature.

Ames Description prior to  1996:
 ___________________________________________________________________
                       |             LIMITS             |RESTRICTIVE
                       ________________________________
     PROPERTY          |  SLIGHT  | MODERATE |  SEVERE  |  FEATURE
                       |          |          |          |
+___________________________________________________________________
 
 15. SOIL REACTION (pH)    >6.0      5.0-6.0    <5.0     TOO ACID

 
 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________
 
 The values given on the Soils-5 for soil reaction are examined for each surface layer.  A low value is determined for each surface layer depending on which of the following conditions is met first.
 
 If the entry is of the form '<xx', then an artificial value of 0 is  used.
 
 If the entry is a normal range, then the low value is used.
 
 If the entry is a single number or is of the form '>xx', then the  single value entered is used.
 
 Otherwise an artificial value of 10 is used.
 
 The minimum value over all surface layers is determined.
 
      A minimum value < 5.0 gets a SEVERE rating.
      A minimum value >= 5.0 and < 6.0 gets a MODERATE rating.
      A minimum value >= 6.0 gets a SLIGHT rating.

Missouri separated the rating of the topsoil and subsoil for this property. The national rule we started with gave higher ratings for surface soils with free carbonates that would render phosphorus insoluble. We used the logic that it is better to have the phosphorus stored in the subsoil and not have a high concentration at the surface where it is available for transport by runoff to the streams and lakes.

Soils with free carbonates at some depth below the surface layer will tie up the phosphorus. Missouri has some karst landscapes with skeletal soils.  It also has loosing streams and shallow depth to bedrock soils. It is favorable to have free carbonates in the subsoil tie up the phosphorus before it leaches down into the cave systems and cave streams. These caves and streams eventually supply surface water to our lakes and streams.
(Null)

Deeper soils have more ability to store water, air and nutrients. Soils with restrictive layers many times increase runoff because of low permeability or ksat, have less volume to sore nutrients, may have fractured bedrock that allows leaching into cave systems and ground water, and are less productive for removal of phosphorus by crops.

Fragipans do restrict downward movement of water and air and also restrict rooting depth. Since the slow permeability of fragipans greatly increases runoff, the restrictive layer has already provided a large reduction in rating value. We should consider not reducing the rating by depth to restrictive layer of fragipans because of the heavy reduction due to component runoff values. The runoff ratings provide a large portion of the ratings.

evalname: NY Coarse Fragments 75 to 250mm(3 to 10 in)(Thickest Layer)
evaldesc:
This evaluation checks for coarse fragments between 3 and 10 inches in the thickest layer.  The rock_frag_3_to_10_in is checked and evaluated.

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
 
Where the result of the soil horizon property rock_frag_3_to_10_in is greater than 15 percent by weight the evaluation is absolutely true and "PERCENT COARSE FRAGMENTS" is a restrictive feature.
     AND
Where the result of the soil horizon property rock_frag_3_to_10_in is less than 0 percent by weight the evaluation is absolutely false and "PERCENT COARSE FRAGMENTS" is not a restrictive feature.

Current version contains major  revisions to the Ames 1996 version.

Ames Description prior to  1996:

1___________________________________________________________________
                                       |             LIMITS                                        |RESTRICTIVE
+                                    ________________________________
     PROPERTY          |    PROBABLE   |   IMPROBABLE   |  FEATURE
                                      |     SOURCE         |             SOURCE     |
+___________________________________________________________________

 4. 6/FRACTION >3            <50                         >50                          LARGE
    IN (WT PCT)                                                                                      STONES

 6/Thickest layer between 10 and 60 inches.



 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________

 NOTE:  THE CURRENT CALCULATION FOR THIS PROPERTY IS ACTUALLY A WEIGHTED AVERAGE FROM 10 TO 60 INCHES.

 The values given on the Soils-5 for fraction 3-10 inches are examined and a high value for each layer within 10 to 60 inches is
 determined.  The given depths may or may not include surface layers.   The high value used in the calculation depends on which of the following conditions is met first.

 If a single value of '99' is entered, then an artificial value of 100 is used.

 If a single value not equal to '99' is entered, then an artificial  value of 0 is used.

 Otherwise the high value is used.

 If surface layers are not included, then a weighted average from 10 to 60 inches is calculated and rated.  No phasing is done.

 If surface layers are included, then a separate weighted average from 10 to 60 inches is calculated and rated for each surface
 layer.  Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.

 The rating algorithm is as follows:

    A weighted average > 50 gets an IMPROBABLE rating.
    A weighted average <= 50 gets a PROBABLE rating.

evaldesc:
This evaluation calculates the thickest layer from the surface to 150cm or a restrictive layer.

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
 

     Where the thickness of the thickest layer  is greater than 100cm (40 in) the evaluation is absolutely true and "THIN LAYER" is not a restrictive feature.
    AND
    Where the thickness of the thickest layer  is less than 30cm (12 in) the evaluation is absolutely false and "THIN LAYER" is a restrictive feature.

Current version contains major  revisions to the Ames 1996 version.

Ames prior to 1996

The layer with the most inches between 10 and 60 inches is determined.  This could be a surface layer or a sublayer.  The unified values given on the Soils-5 are examined for the appropriate layer(s).

 The layer(s) being examined are rated according to the following algorithm:

 If GW, GP, GW-GM, or GP-GM is listed as a unified entry, or if SW, SP, SW-SM or SP-SM is listed as a unified entry and footnote 15 applies (see following description of footnote 15), then a PROBABLE rating is given.

 Otherwise an IMPROBABLE rating is given.

 If the thickest layer is a sublayer, then this property is rated the same as this sublayer's rating.

 If the thickest layer is a surface layer, then this property is rated PROBABLE if there is any PROBABLE surface layer rating.  If there is none, then it is rated IMPROBABLE.

 Restrictive feature terms are assigned appropriately.



 Description of Calculation for Bottom Layer:
+____________________________________________

 If the bottom layer has no data, then this calculation is skipped and the ratings for the thickest layer are chosen.

 Otherwise, this calculation is the same as that for the thickest layer, except it is done for the bottom layer.  The bottom layer, like the thickest layer, may be a surface layer or a sublayer.

This evaluation check percolation capacity of the soil.  The high, low, and representative values for sat_hydraulic_conductivity are selected for each horizon to a depth of 60 inches. 

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
  Where the soil horizon property sat_hydraulic_conductivity <= 1.0 micrometers/second (0.20 inches/hour)the evaluation is absolutely true and the restrictive feature is slow percolation.
        AND
  Where the soil horizon property sat_hydraulic_conductivity => 4.0 micrometers/second (0.60 inches/hour) the evaluation is absolutely false and the restrictive feature is not slow percolation.

If no data is entered, thn an artificial default value(s) is used. 

Ames Description Prior to 1996:
 ___________________________________________________________________
                       |             LIMITS             |RESTRICTIVE
+                       ________________________________
     PROPERTY          |  SLIGHT  | MODERATE |  SEVERE  |  FEATURE
                       |          |          |          |
+___________________________________________________________________
 
 2a. PERMEABILITY        0.6-2.0     0.2-0.6     <0.2    PERCS
     (0-60", IN/HR)                                      SLOWLY
The values given on the Soils-5 for permeability are examined and a low value for each layer is determined.  The low value used for comparison depends on which of the following conditions is met first.  If no data is entered, then an artificial value of 100 is used.
 
If the entry is of the form '<xx', then an artificial value of 0 is used. Otherwise the low value is used.
The layers within the given depths are examined.  The surface layers are each rated separately.  The lowest value found from all the sublayers is rated.  The rating algorithm used is as follows:
 
A value < 0.2 gets a SEVERE rating.
A value >= 0.2 and < 0.6 gets a MODERATE rating.
A value >= 0.6 gets a SLIGHT rating.
 
If the sublayer rating is SEVERE, then this property is rated SEVERE and no phasing will be done, regardless of the surface layer ratings. If the sublayer rating is MODERATE, then this property is rated MODERATE if there is any SLIGHT or MODERATE surface layer rating, and it is rated SEVERE if there is any SEVERE surface layer rating. Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.
 
If the sublayer rating is SLIGHT, then this property is rated SLIGHT if there is any SLIGHT surface layer rating, MODERATE if there is any MODERATE surface layer rating, and SEVERE if there is any SEVERE surface layer rating. Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.

evalname: Shrink-swell of thick. layer rv in 25-150cm or restriction
evaldesc:
This evaluation evaluates the product of the shrink-swell value of the thickest horizon in the 25 to 150cm range.

If the shrink-swell value for the thickest layer between 25-150cm is between 3 and 6, the evaluation returns a value between 0 and 1.

When the shrink-swell value for the thickest layer between 25 to 150cm is > 6 (HIGH or VERY HIGH) the evaluation is absolutely true and the restrictive feature is SHRINK-SWELL.
	AND
When the shrink-swell value for the thickest layer between 25 to 150cm is <3 (LOW), the evaluation is absolutely false and the restrictive feature is not SHRINK-SWELL.


Ames Description Prior to 1996:
                                                      |                            LIMITS                                       |  RESTRICTIVE
     PROPERTY                         |  SLIGHT  | MODERATE |  SEVERE            |  FEATURE
 
 9. 9/SHRINK-SWELL         LOW             MODERATE      HIGH,                  SHRINK-
                                                                                                              VERY HIGH       SWELL
 
 9/Thickest layer between 10 and 60 inches.
 
 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________
 
 The layer with the most inches between 10 and 60 inches is determined.  This could be a surface layer or a sublayer.  The shrink-swell values given on the Soils-5 are examined for the appropriate layer(s).
 
 The layer(s) being examined are rated according to the following algorithm:
 
 If the shrink-swell value equals '1' (HIGH) or '5' (VERY HIGH), then a SEVERE rating is given.  If the shrink-swell value equals '3' (MODERATE), then a MODERATE rating is given. Otherwise a SLIGHT rating is given.
 
 If the thickest layer is a sublayer, then this property is rated the same as this sublayer's rating.
 
 If the thickest layer is a surface layer, then this property is rated SLIGHT if there is any SLIGHT surface layer rating, MODERATE if there is any MODERATE surface layer rating, and SEVERE if there is any SEVERE surface layer rating.  Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.

 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________
 
 This property is calculated as if it were two separate properties.

 sublayer is rated to determine the worst sublayer rating.  The
 rating algorithm used on each layer is as follows:

           A value < 0.6 gets a SEVERE rating
           A value >= 0.6 and < 2.0 gets a MODERATE rating.
           A value >= 2.0 gets a SLIGHT rating.
 
 If surface layers are not involved, then this property is rated the
 same as the worst sublayer rating.
 
 If surface layers are involved, then the following applies.  If the
 worst sublayer rating is SEVERE, then this property is rated SEVERE

 If the worst sublayer rating is MODERATE, then this property is

 rating, and it is rated SEVERE if there is any SEVERE surface layer
 rating.  Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one

 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________

 The values given on the Soils-5 for permeability are examined and a
 low value for each layer below 10 inches is determined.  The low

 If no data is entered, then an artificial value of 100 is used.

 The layers below 10 inches are examined.  If surface layers

 sublayer is rated to determine the worst sublayer rating.  The
 rating algorithm used on each layer is as follows:

           A value < 0.6 gets a SEVERE rating.

           A value >= 2.0 gets a SLIGHT rating.

 If surface layers are not involved, then this property is rated the
 same as the worst sublayer rating.

 If surface layers are involved, then the following applies.  If the
 worst sublayer rating is SEVERE, then this property is rated SEVERE

 ratings.

 If the worst sublayer rating is MODERATE, then this property is
 rated MODERATE if there is any SLIGHT or MODERATE surface layer
 rating, and it is rated SEVERE if there is any SEVERE surface layer
 rating.  Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one
 rating is given.

 If the worst sublayer rating is SLIGHT, then this property is rated
 SLIGHT if there is any SLIGHT surface layer rating, MODERATE if
 there is any MODERATE surface layer rating, and SEVERE if there is
 any SEVERE surface layer rating.  Phasing will be done using texture
 terms if more than one rating is given.

evaldesc:
This evaluation checks for soil shrink-swell potential for the thickest layer within 0 to 100cm (40 inches) or the soil surface to bedrock.  The linear_extensibility_percent for the thickest layer is examined and evalutated for depth conditions.

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
  Where linear_extensibility_percent of the thickest layer is greater than 6 the evaluation is absolutely true.
   OR
  Where linear_extensibility_percent of the thickest layer is less than 3 the evaluation is absolutely false.

If the linear_extensibility_percent of the thickest layer is NULL then LE is assumed to be less than 3.

                                                                                                              VERY HIGH       SWELL
 
 9/Thickest layer between 10 and 40 inches.
 
 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________
 
 The layer with the most inches between 10 and 40 inches is determined.  This could be a surface layer or a sublayer.  The shrink-swell values given on the Soils-5 are examined for the appropriate layer(s).
 
 The layer(s) being examined are rated according to the following algorithm:
 
 If the shrink-swell value equals '1' (HIGH) or '5' (VERY HIGH), then a SEVERE rating is given.  If the shrink-swell value equals '3' (MODERATE), then a MODERATE rating is given. Otherwise a SLIGHT rating is given.
 
 If the thickest layer is a sublayer, then this property is rated the same as this sublayer's rating.
 
 If the thickest layer is a surface layer, then this property is rated SLIGHT if there is any SLIGHT surface layer rating, MODERATE if there is any MODERATE surface layer rating, and SEVERE if there is any SEVERE surface layer rating.  Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.

evaldesc:
Vermont version uses a property that ignores duff layers, assuming that their texture is HPM, MPM, SPM.

This evaluation is crisp and checks for UNIFIED equal to  "PT".

Where unified_soil_classification equals or "PT" the evaluation is absolutely true.
    AND
Where unified_soil_classification does not equal or "PT" the evaluation is absolutely false.

 Ames prior to 1996
                                                              |             LIMITS             |RESTRICTIVE
     PROPERTY                                 |  SLIGHT  | MODERATE |  SEVERE  |  FEATURE
  7. UNIFIED (ANY DEPTH)              --             OL, OH                  PT             EXCESS HUMUS
  
 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________
 
 The unified values given on the Soils-5 are examined for each layer.
 
 The surface layers are each rated separately.  Then each sublayer is rated to determine the worst sublayer rating.  The rating algorithm used on each layer is as follows:
 
 If PT is listed as a unified entry, then a SEVERE rating is given. If OL or OH is listed as a unified entry, then a MODERATE rating is      given. Otherwise a SLIGHT rating is given.
 
 If the worst sublayer rating is SEVERE, then this property is rated SEVERE and no phasing will be done, regardless of the surface layer ratings.
 
 If the worst sublayer rating is MODERATE, then this property is rated MODERATE if there is any SLIGHT or MODERATE surface layer rating, and it is rated SEVERE if there is any SEVERE surface layer rating. Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.

This evaluation looks at the representative value for surface fragment cover. Using a sigmoid curve, this evaluation has fuzzy ratings for surface stoniness between 15 and 50. Anything less than 15 is absolutely in the class and returns a value of 0. Surface stoniness cover that is greater than 50 is absolutely out of the class and a value of 1 is returned. Fuzzy number of 0.85 is used for moderate surface stones in the rating class as the closer stoniness approaches 1 the more stones on the surface could be considered a limitation.

This evaluation tests for percent of gravel in the bottom layer.

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
 
Where the result of the soil horizon property sieveno4 is less than 40 percent by weight the evaluation is absolutely true and "EXCESS FINES" is not a restrictive feature.
     AND
Where the result of the soil horizon property sieveno4 is greater than 70 percent by weight the evaluation is absolutely false and "EXCESS FINES" is a restrictive feature.

Current version contains major  revisions to the Ames 1996 version.

Ames prior to 1996

 1___________________________________________________________________
                                                                               LIMITS                                    |RESTRICTIVE
+                       ________________________________
     PROPERTY             |    PROBABLE                 |   IMPROBABLE      |  FEATURE
                                         |     SOURCE                       |     SOURCE                |
+___________________________________________________________________

 2. 12/UNIFIED          GW, GP, GW-GM,
                                        GP-GM

                                       15/SW, 15/SP,
                                      15/SW-SM,
                                      15/SP-SM

                                                                                              16/SW, 16/SP,              TOO
                                                                                             16/SW-SM,                   SANDY
                                                                                             16/SP-SM 

                                                                                                PT                                  EXCESS  HUMUS

                                                                                         ALL OTHER                    EXCESS  FINES

 12/Evaluate the thickest layer between 10 and 60 inches and also the  bottom layer.  Choose the best rating.  When rating is based on  bottom layer, verify thickness.
 15/100 minus % passing No. 4 sieve > 25.
 16/100 minus % passing No. 4 sieve < 25.



 According to footnote 12, calculations are done for both the thickest layer and the bottom layer.

 Description of Calculation for Thickest Layer:
+______________________________________________

 The layer with the most inches between 10 and 60 inches is determined.  This could be a surface layer or a sublayer.  The unified values given on the Soils-5 are examined for the appropriate layer(s).

 The layer(s) being examined are rated according to the following algorithm:

 If GW, GP, GW-GM, or GP-GM is listed as a unified entry, or if SW, SP, SW-SM or SP-SM is listed as a unified entry and footnote 15 applies (see following description of footnote 15), then a PROBABLE rating is given.

 Otherwise an IMPROBABLE rating is given.

 If the thickest layer is a sublayer, then this property is rated the same as this sublayer's rating.

 If the thickest layer is a surface layer, then this property is rated PROBABLE if there is any PROBABLE surface layer rating.  If there is none, then it is rated IMPROBABLE.

 Restrictive feature terms are assigned appropriately.



 Description of Calculation for Bottom Layer:
+____________________________________________

 If the bottom layer has no data, then this calculation is skipped and the ratings for the thickest layer are chosen.

 Otherwise, this calculation is the same as that for the thickest layer, except it is done for the bottom layer.  The bottom layer,
 like the thickest layer, may be a surface layer or a sublayer.

 Calculations for Footnotes 15 and 16
+____________________________________

 To do the calculations for these footnotes, the values given on the Soils-5 for % passing No. 4 sieve are examined.

 % passing No. 4 sieve
+_____________________

 Assign values to No_4_Lo and No_4_Hi.

 If no data is entered, then No_4_Lo = 0 and No_4_Hi = 0.

 If a single value, say x, is entered, then No_4_Lo = x and  No_4_Hi = x.

 If the entry is a normal range, say x-y, then No_4_Lo = x and  No_4_Hi = y.

 Once these values have been assigned, the following calculations take place.

 100 - No_4_Lo = Lo
 100 - No_4_Hi = Hi

 maximum(Lo,Hi) = max

 If max > 25 then footnote 15 applies.
 If max <= 25 then footnote 16 applies.

 For Property No. 2, UNIFIED, the best ratings must be chosen between those calculated for the thickest layer and the bottom layer.

 If both the thickest and bottom layers are rated PROBABLE, then the bottom layer is chosen.

 If the thickest layer is rated PROBABLE and the bottom layer is rated IMPROBABLE, then the thickest layer is chosen.

 If the bottom layer is rated PROBABLE and the thickest layer is rated IMPROBABLE, then the bottom layer is chosen.

 If neither the thickest or bottom layer is rated PROBABLE, then they must both be rated IMPROBABLE and the bottom layer is chosen.

 If the ratings for the thickest layer were chosen, then the calculations on the following page for Property No. 3, LAYER
 THICKNESS, are done.

This evalution finds the top depth of the first layer where soil moisture layer status is wet or saturated during any month at a depth less than 122cm (48 inches).  The representative value, low and high values are returned from the Property script High Water Table Minimum.

This is a sigmoid curve where anything less than 122cm is rated as 1, meaning that water table restriction in this depth will make a septic system severely limited. Water table depths greater than 137cm are absolutely in the class and have no limitation for septic systems and are rated as 0. Fuzzy logic is applied to the partial members of the class which are between 122cm and 137cm.

This rating is based on the depth of the trench which can range from 12 to 18 inches, in which 3 feet of soil material is required to underlie. Depending on the depth at which the trench is installed will determine the critical depth to the water table. Therefore fuzzy values provide a range of limitations.

This evaluation takes the number from the property script "Flooding Rating" and evaluates it thusly:

Flooding of 0.0 to 0.1 gets a fuzzy number of 0.  This is no flooding.
Flooding of 0.1001 to 0.2000 gets a fuzzy number of 0.6.  This is very rare flooding.
Flooding of .20001 and higher gets a fuzzy number of 1.  This is all other flooding classes.

This is a crisp evaluation.

	else the soil is limited and the degree of suitability is expressed as the number 0.

evalname: USDA Texture Class & Modifiers - Sand and Sandy Gravel (TX)
evaldesc:
This evaluation checks the USDA texture group of the soil horizon between 50 and 180cm and indexes the degree to which the texture group is limiting.  Where the soil property "USDA TEXTURE GROUP IN DEPTH 50-180cm (TX)" matches:
	    
	"*S *", "*S", "GR*", or "* GR" the soil is limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as the number 1.0.
	else the soil is not limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as the number 0.
eval:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-16"?>
<EvaluationParameter xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema">
  <DomainPoints />
  <RangePoints />
  <CrispExpression>matches "*S *" or matches "*S" or matches "GR*" or matches "* GR"</CrispExpression>
</EvaluationParameter>
crispExpression: matches "*S *" or matches "*S" or matches "GR*" or matches "* GR"

evaldesc:
This evaluation checks the USDA texture of the soil horizon between 50 and 180cm and indexes the degree to which the texture is limiting.  Where the soil property "USDA TEXTURE SILT LOAM IN DEPTH 50-180cm (TX)" matches:
	    
	"si" the soil is limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as the number 1.0.
	else the soil is not limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as the number 0.

evalname: Unified; Organic Surface Layer Thicker Then 25cm (TX)
evaldesc:
This evaluation checks the Unified class of the soil surface layer with a surface layer greater then 25cm and indexes the degree to which unified class is limiting.  Where the soil property "UNIFIED IN SURFACE THICKER THEN 25CM (TX)" is:

	     = "OL", "OH", or "PT" the soil is limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as the number 1.0.
	 not = "OL", "OH", or "PT" the soil is not limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as the number 0.

This evaluation checks the Unified class of the soil between a depth of 50 to 150cm and indexes the degree to which unified class is limiting.  Where the soil property "UNIFIED IN DEPTH 50-150cm (TX)" is:

	     = "OL", "OH", or "PT" the soil is limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as the number 1.0.
	 not = "OL", "OH", or "PT" the soil is not limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as the number 0.

This evaluation checks for the presence of Permafrost.  Where the soil property "USDA TEXTURE MODIFIER (TX)" is:
	 = "pf" the soil is limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as the number 1.0.
	 not = "pf" the soil is not limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as the number 0.

This evaluation checks for the presence of marl or gypsum.  Where the soil property "USDA TEXTURE MODIFIER (TX)" is:
	     = "gyp" or "mr" the soil is limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as the number 1.0.
	 not = "gyp" or "mr" the soil is not limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as the number 0.

The evaluation checks for the presence of permafrost and if present indexes the depth.  This index expresses as the degree to which PERMAFROST is a limiting feature.  Where the soil property "DEPTH TO PERMAFROST (TX)" is:
	 =< 50cm the soil is limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as the number 1.0.
	 > 50cm and < 100cm the soil is somewhat limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as a number between 0 and 1.0.
	 => 100cm the soil is not limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as the number 0.

The evaluation checks for the presence of permafrost and if present indexes the depth.  This index expresses as the degree to which PERMAFROST is a limiting feature.  Where the soil property "DEPTH TO PERMAFROST (TX)" is:
	  > 60cm the soil is limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as the number 1.0.
	 =< 60cm the soil is not limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as the number 0.

This evaluation checks for the presence of Permafrost.  Where the soil property "USDA TEXTURE (IN-LIEU-OF) (TX)" is:
	 = "cpf" the soil is limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as the number 1.0.
	 not = "cpf" the soil is not limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as the number 0.

evalname: Sandy USDA Textures 2 - thickest layer in 25-180cm (TX)
evaldesc:
This evaluation checks the USDA texture of the thickest layer within depths 25 to 180cm and indexes the degree to which the thickest layer's texture is limiting.  Where the soil property "USDA TEXTURE THICKEST LAYER IN DEPTH 25-180cm (TX)" is:
	     = "cos" or "s" or "fs" or "vfs" or "sg" the soil is limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as the number 1.0.
	 not = "cos" or "s" or "fs" or "vfs" or "sg" the soil is not limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as the number 0.
eval:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-16"?>
<EvaluationParameter xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema">
  <DomainPoints />
  <RangePoints />
  <CrispExpression>= "cos" or "s" or "fs" or "sg" or "vfs"</CrispExpression>
</EvaluationParameter>
propname: USDA TEXTURE THICKEST LAYER IN DEPTH 25-180cm (TX)

evalname: Sandy USDA Textures - thickest layer in 25-180cm (TX)
evaldesc:
This evaluation checks the USDA texture of the thickest layer within depths 25 to 180cm and indexes the degree to which the thickest layer's texture is limiting.  Where the soil property "USDA TEXTURE THICKEST LAYER IN DEPTH 25-180cm (TX)" is:
	     = "cos" or "s" or "fs" or "sg" the soil is limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as the number 1.0.
	 not = "cos" or "s" or "fs" or "sg" the soil is not limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as the number 0.
propname: USDA TEXTURE THICKEST LAYER IN DEPTH 25-180cm (TX)

evalname: Sandy USDA Textures 3 - thickest layer in 25-180cm (TX)
evaldesc:
This evaluation checks the USDA texture of the thickest layer within depths 25 to 180cm and indexes the degree to which the thickest layer's texture is limiting.  Where the soil property "USDA TEXTURE THICKEST LAYER IN DEPTH 25-180cm (TX)" is:
	     = "lcos" or "ls" or "lfs" or "lvfs" the soil is limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as the number 1.0.
	 not = "lcos" or "ls" or "lfs" or "lvfs" the soil is not limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as the number 0.
propname: USDA TEXTURE THICKEST LAYER IN DEPTH 25-180cm (TX)

evalname: Taxonomic Great Group; ust*, *torr* or xer (TX)
evaldesc:
This evaluation checks soil's taxonomic great group classification and indexes the degree to which the soil taxonomic great group is limiting.  Where the soil property "TAXONOMIC GREAT GROUP (TX)" matches:
	 
	"ust*", "torr*", or  "xer*" the soil is limited and the degree of limitation is expressed as the number 1.0.
	else the soil is not limited and the degree of limitation is expressed as the number 0.
eval:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-16"?>
<EvaluationParameter xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema">
  <DomainPoints />
  <RangePoints />
  <CrispExpression>matches "ust*" or matches "torr*" or matches "xer*"</CrispExpression>
</EvaluationParameter>

evaldesc:
This evaluation checks soil's taxonomic great group classification and indexes the degree to which the soil taxonomic great group is limiting.  Where the soil property "TAXONOMIC GREAT GROUP (TX)" matches:
	 
	"*torr*" the soil is limited and the degree of limitation is expressed as the number 1.0.
	else the soil is not limited and the degree of limitation is expressed as the number 0.

This evaluation checks soil's taxonomic great group classification and indexes the degree to which the soil taxonomic great group is limiting.  Where the soil property "TAXONOMIC GREAT GROUP (TX)" matches:
	 
	= "vitritorrands" the soil is limited and the degree of limitation is expressed as the number 1.0.
	else the soil is not limited and the degree of limitation is expressed as the number 0.

This evaluation checks soil's taxonomic great group classification and indexes the degree to which the soil taxonomic great group is limiting.  Where the soil property "TAXONOMIC GREAT GROUP (TX)" matches:
	 
	"ust*" the soil is limited and the degree of limitation is expressed as the number 1.0.
	else the soil is not limited and the degree of limitation is expressed as the number 0.

This evaluation checks soil's taxonomic great group classification and indexes the degree to which the soil taxonomic great group is limiting.  Where the soil property "TAXONOMIC GREAT GROUP (TX)" matches:
	 
	= "fragiumbrepts" or "durochrepts" or "durandepts" or "eutrandepts" or "vitrandepts" the soil is limited and the degree of limitation is expressed as the number 1.0.
	else the soil is not limited and the degree of limitation is expressed as the number 0.
eval:

evalname: Taxonomic Great Group; calciaquerts or salaquerts (TX)
evaldesc:
This evaluation checks soil's taxonomic great group classification and indexes the degree to which the soil taxonomic great group is limiting.  Where the soil property "TAXONOMIC GREAT GROUP (TX)" matches:
	 
	= "calciaquerts" or "salaquerts" the soil is limited and the degree of limitation is expressed as the number 1.0.
	else the soil is not limited and the degree of limitation is expressed as the number 0.

This evaluation checks soil's taxonomic great group classification and indexes the degree to which it's sulfur content is limiting.  Where the soil property "TAXONOMIC GREAT GROUP (TX)" matches:
	 
	"*sulf*" the soil is limited and the degree of limitation is expressed as the number 1.0.
	else the soil is not limited and the degree of limitation is expressed as the number 0.

This evaluation checks soil's taxonomic great group classification and indexes the degree to which the soil taxonomic great group is limiting.  Where the soil property "TAXONOMIC GREAT GROUP (TX)" matches:
	 
	"xer*" the soil is limited and the degree of limitation is expressed as the number 1.0.
	else the soil is not limited and the degree of limitation is expressed as the number 0.

evalname: Taxonomic Mineralogy Family smectitic and mixed (TX)
evaldesc:
This evaluation checks the soil's taxonomic mineralogy class.  Where the soil property "TAXONOMIC MINERALOGY CLASS (TX)" is:

	     = "mixed", "smectitic" or "montmorillonitic" the soil is limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as the number 1.0.
	 not = "mixed", "smectitic" or "montmorillonitic" the soil is not limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as the number 0.

This evaluation checks the soil's taxonomic mineralogy class.  Where the soil property "TAXONOMIC MINERALOGY CLASS (TX)" is:

	     = "carbonatic" the soil is a member of the class and the index is expressed as the number 1.0.
	 not = "carbonatic" the soil is not a member of the class and the index is expressed as the number 0.

This evaluation checks the soil's taxonomic mineralogy class.  Where the soil property "TAXONOMIC MINERALOGY CLASS (TX)" is:

	     = "kaolinitic" the soil is limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as the number 1.0.
	 not = "kaolinitic" the soil is not limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as the number 0.

This evaluation checks the soil's taxonomic mineralogy class.  Where the soil property "TAXONOMIC MINERALOGY CLASS (TX)" is:

	     = "smectitic" or "montmorillonitic" the soil is limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as the number 1.0.
	 not = "smectitic" or "montmorillonitic" the soil is not limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as the number 0.

This evaluation checks the soil's minimum Ksat to a depth of 5cm and indexes the degree to which Ksat is limiting.  Where the soil property "KSAT, MINIMUM IN DEPTH 0-5CM (TX)" is:
	   < 1 micrometers/second the soil is limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as the number 1.0.
	  => 1 micrometers/second the soil is not limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as the number 0.

This evaluation checks the soil's electrical conductivity and indexes the degree to which EC is limiting.  Where the soil property "SALINITY MAXIMUM (TX)" is:
	  > 16 the soil is limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as the number 1.0.
	 =< 16 the soil is not limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as the number 0.

This evaluation checks the soil's electrical conductivity and indexes the degree to which EC is limiting.  Where the soil property "SALINITY MAXIMUM (TX)" is:
	 => 16 the soil is limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as the number 1.0.
	  > 4.0 and < 16 the soil is somewhat limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as a number between 0 and 1.0.
	 =< 4.0 the soil is not limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as the number 0.

This evaluation checks the soil's electrical conductivity and indexes the degree to which EC is limiting.  Where the soil property "SALINITY MAXIMUM (TX)" is:
	 => 8 the soil is limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as the number 1.0.
	  > 4 and < 8 the soil is somewhat limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as a number between 0 and 1.0.
	 =< 4 the soil is not limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as the number 0.

This evaluation checks the soil's electrical conductivity and indexes the degree to which EC is limiting.  Where the soil property "SALINITY MAXIMUM (TX)" is:
	  > 4 the soil is limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as the number 1.0.
	 =< 4 the soil is not limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as the number 0.

The evaluation checks for the presence of a continuously wet or saturated from the top of the first wet layer throughout the remainder of the soil and if present indexes the depth.  This index expresses the degree to which "WETNESS" is a limiting feature.  Where the soil property "DEPTH TO HIGH WATER TABLE APPARENT MINIMUM (TX)" is:
	 < 180cm the soil is limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as the number 1.0.
	  => 180cm the soil is not limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as the number 0.
propname: DEPTH TO HIGH WATER TABLE APPARENT MINIMUM (TX)

evaldesc:
The evaluation checks for the presence of a continuously  wet or saturated from the top of the first wet layer throughout the remainder of the soil and if present indexes the depth.  This index expresses the degree to which "WETNESS" is a limiting feature.  Where the soil property "DEPTH TO HIGH WATER TABLE APPARENT MINIMUM (TX)" is:
	 < 60cm the soil is limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as the number 1.0.
	  => 60cm the soil is not limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as the number 0.
propname: DEPTH TO HIGH WATER TABLE APPARENT MINIMUM (TX)

evaldesc:
The evaluation checks for the presence of a wet or saturated layer and if present indexes the depth.  This index expresses the degree to which "WETNESS" is a limiting feature.  Where the soil property "DEPTH TO HIGH WATER TABLE APPARENT MINIMUM (TX)" is:
	=< 60cm the soil is limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as the number 1.0.
	 > 60cm the soil is not limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as the number 0.
propname: DEPTH TO HIGH WATER TABLE APPARENT MINIMUM (TX)

evaldesc:
The evaluation checks for the presence of a discontinuous wet or saturated moisture status where there is one or more layers below the initial wet layer that are not wet or saturated.  If the condition is present the evaluation indexes depth.  This index expresses the degree to which "WETNESS" is a limiting feature.  Where the soil property "DEPTH TO HIGH WATER TABLE PERCHED MINIMUM (TX)" is:
	 < 60cm the soil is limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as the number 1.0.
	  => 60cm the soil is not limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as the number 0.
propname: DEPTH TO HIGH WATER TABLE PERCHED MINIMUM (TX)

evalname: Depth to Perched Water Table 60 to 120cm (TX)
evaldesc:
The evaluation checks for the presence of a discontinuous wet or saturated moisture status where there is one or more layers below the initial wet layer that are not wet or saturated.  If the condition is present the evaluation indexes depth.  This index expresses the degree to which "WETNESS" is a limiting feature.  Where the soil property "DEPTH TO HIGH WATER TABLE PERCHED MINIMUM (TX)" is:
	  =< 60cm the soil is limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as the number 1.0.
	   > 60cm and < 120cm the soil is somewhat limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as a number between 0 and 1.0.
	  => 120cm the soil is not limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as the number 0.
propname: DEPTH TO HIGH WATER TABLE PERCHED MINIMUM (TX)

evaldesc:
This evaluation checks the soil's wind erodibility group (WEG).  Where the soil property "WIND ERODIBILITY GROUP (TX)" is:
	 matches "1" or "2" the soil is limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as the number 1.0.
	 does not match "1" or "2" the soil is not limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as the number 0.

This evaluation checks the soil's wind erodibility group (WEG).  Where the soil property "WIND ERODIBILITY GROUP (TX)" is:

	 match "1" the soil is not suited and the degree of suitability index is expressed as the number 0.
	 else matches "2", "3", "4", "4L", 5, 6, or 7 the soil is suited and the degree of suitability index is expressed as the number 1.0.

This evaluation checks the soil's wind erodibility group (WEG).  Where the soil property "WIND ERODIBILITY GROUP (TX)" is:

	 matches "1" or "2" or "3" the soil is limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as the number 1.0.
	 does not match "1" or "2" or "3"  the soil is not limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as the number 0.
eval:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-16"?>
<EvaluationParameter xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema">
  <DomainPoints />
  <RangePoints />
  <CrispExpression>matches "1" or matches "2" or matches "3"</CrispExpression>
</EvaluationParameter>

evaldesc:
This evaluation checks the soil's wind erodibility group (WEG).  Where the soil property "WIND ERODIBILITY GROUP (TX)" is:

	 match "1" or "2' the soil is not suited and the degree of suitability index is expressed as the number 0.
	 else matches "3", "4", "4L", 5, 6, or 7 the soil is suited and the degree of suitability index is expressed as the number 1.0.

This evaluation checks the soil's wind erodibility group (WEG).  Where the soil property "WIND ERODIBILITY GROUP (TX)" is:

	 matches "5", "6", "7" or "8" the soil is suited and the degree of suitability index is expressed as the number 1.0.
	 matches "1", "2", "3", "4" or "4L" the soil is not suited and the degree of suitability index is expressed as the number 0.

This evaluation checks the soil's wind erodibility group (WEG).  Where the soil property "WIND ERODIBILITY GROUP (TX)" is:

	 matches "6", "7" or "8" the soil is suited and the degree of suitability index is expressed as the number 1.0.
	 matches "1", "2", "3", "4", "4L", or "5" the soil is not suited and the degree of suitability index is expressed as the number 0.

evalname: Depth to Water Table 60 to 90cm in growing season (TX)
evaldesc:
The evaluation checks for the presence of a wet or saturated layer during the growing season and if present indexes the depth.  This index expresses the degree to which "WETNESS" is a limiting feature.  Where the soil property "DEPTH TO HIGH WATER TABLE, Growing Season (TX)" is:

	 =< 60cm the soil is limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as the number 1.0.
	  > 60cm and < 90cm the soil is somewhat limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as a number between 0 and 1.0.
	 => 90cm the soil is not limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as the number 0.
propname: DEPTH TO HIGH WATER TABLE, Irr. Growing Season (TX)

evaldesc:
This evaluation checks the Ksat of the thickest soil layer and indexes the degree to which Ksat is limiting.  Where the soil property "KSAT, THICKEST LAYER, 25 TO 150CM OR FIRST RESTRICTION (TX)" is:
	   > 42 micrometers/second the soil is limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as the number 1.0.
	  =< 42 micrometers/second the soil is not limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as the number 0.
propname: KSAT, THICKEST LAYER, 25 TO 150CM OR FIRST RESTRICTION (TX)

evaldesc:
This evaluation checks the % passing the #200 sieve of the thickest soil layer and indexes the degree to which Ksat is limiting.  Where the soil property "PASSING 200 SIEVE; THICKEST LAYER 25 TO 150CM (TX)" is:
	  => 20 and =< 30 the soil is limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as the number 1.0.
	   < 20 or > 30 the soil is not limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as the number 0.

This evaluation checks the % passing the #200 sieve of the thickest soil layer and indexes the degree to which Ksat is limiting.  Where the soil property "PASSING 200 SIEVE; THICKEST LAYER 25 TO 150CM (TX)" is:
	   < 20 the soil is limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as the number 1.0.
	  => 20 the soil is not limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as the number 0.

This evaluation checks the % passing the #200 sieve of the thickest soil layer and indexes the degree to which Ksat is limiting.  Where the soil property "PASSING 200 SIEVE; THICKEST LAYER 25 TO 150CM (TX)" is:
	   > 30 the soil is limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as the number 1.0.
	  =< 30 the soil is not limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as the number 0.

The surface horizon percent clay content indexes the degree to which Clay content is limiting.  Where the soil property "CLAY PERCENT SURFACE LAYER (TX)" is:

	=> 60% the soil is limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as the number 1.0.
	 > 27 and < 60% the soil is somewhat limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as a number between 0 and 1.0.
	=< 27% the soil is not limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as the number 0.

The evaluation indexes the degree to which Clay content of the surface layer contributes to the soil wind erosion potential.  Where the soil property "CLAY PERCENT SURFACE LAYER (TX)" is:

	=> 40% Clay, the degree of contribution is high and the index is expressed as the number 1.0.
	 > 12 and < 40% Clay, the degree of contribution is moderate and the index is expressed as a number between 0 and 1.0.
	=< 12% Clay, the degree of contribute is low and the index is expressed as the number 0.

The evaluation indexes the surface layer Clay content's membership in the Clayey FSG.  Where the soil property "CLAY PERCENT SURFACE LAYER (TX)" is:

	< 35% Clay, the soil is a full member of the Loamy FSG and the membership index is expressed as the number 0.0.
	=> 35% Clay, the soil is a non-member of the Loamy FSG and the membership index is expressed as the number 1.0.

The evaluation indexes the surface layer Clay content's membership in the Clayey FSG.  Where the soil property "CLAY PERCENT SURFACE LAYER (TX)" is:

	 < 35% Clay, the soil is a full member of the Loamy FSG and the membership index is expressed as the number 1.0.
	=> 35% Clay, the soil is a non-member of the Loamy FSG and the membership index is expressed as the number 0.

The evaluation indexes the surface layer Clay content's membership in the Clayey FSG.  Where the soil property "CLAY PERCENT SURFACE LAYER (TX)" is:

	=< 12% Clay, the soil is a full member of the Loamy FSG and the membership index is expressed as the number 1.0.
	 > 12% Clay, the soil is a non-member of the Loamy FSG and the membership index is expressed as the number 0.

The surface horizon percent clay content indexes the degree to which Clay content is limiting.  Where the soil property "CLAY PERCENT SURFACE LAYER (TX)" is:

	=> 40% the soil is limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as the number 1.0.
	 > 27 and < 40% the soil is somewhat limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as a number between 0 and 1.0.
	=< 27% the soil is not limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as the number 0.

The surface horizon percent clay content indexes the degree to which Clay content is limiting.  Where the soil property "CLAY PERCENT SURFACE LAYER (TX)" is:
	 
	  => 40 the soil is limited and the degree of limitation is expressed as the number 1.0.
	   < 40 the soil is not limited and the degree of limitation is expressed as the number 0.

The surface horizon percent clay content indexes the degree to which Clay content is limiting.  Where the soil property "CLAY PERCENT SURFACE LAYER (TX)" is:

	=> 60% the soil is limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as the number 1.0.
	 > 40 and < 60% the soil is somewhat limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as a number between 0 and 1.0.
	=< 40% the soil is not limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as the number 0.

The surface horizon percent clay content indexes the degree to which Clay content is limiting.  Where the soil property "CLAY PERCENT SURFACE LAYER (TX)" is:
	 
	  => 35 the soil is limited and the degree of limitation is expressed as the number 1.0.
	   < 35 the soil is not limited and the degree of limitation is expressed as the number 0.

The surface horizon percent clay content indexes the degree to which Clay content is limiting.  Where the soil property "CLAY PERCENT SURFACE LAYER (TX)" is:
	 
	  => 60 the soil is limited and the degree of limitation is expressed as the number 1.0.
	   < 60 the soil is not limited and the degree of limitation is expressed as the number 0.

This evaluation checks soil erodibility factor of the surface layer and indexes the degree to which erodibility is limiting.  Where the soil property "EROSION FACTOR SURFACE LAYER (TX)" is:
	 
	 => .40 the soil is limited and the degree of limitation is expressed as the number 1.0.
	  > .22 and < .40 the soil is somewhat limited and the degree of limitation is expressed as a number between 0 and 1.0.
	 =< .22 the soil is not limited and the degree of limitation is expressed as the number 0.

This evaluation checks soil erodibility factor of the surface layer and indexes the degree to which erodibility is limiting.  Where the soil property "EROSION FACTOR SURFACE LAYER (TX)" is:
	 
	  > .32 the soil is limited and the degree of limitation is expressed as the number 1.0.
	 =< .32 the soil is not limited and the degree of limitation is expressed as the number 0.

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
  Where the value of soil property texture_class is cos, s, fs, vfs, locs, ls, lfs, lvfs in the surface layer and the surface layer is >= 51cm or 20", the evaluation returns a value of 1.

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
  Where the value of soil property texture_class is cos, s, fs, vfs, locs in the surface layer and the surface layer is < 51cm or 20", the evaluation returns a value of 1.

This evaluation checks the soil's clay content within a depth of 50 to 180cm and indexes the degree to which clay content is limiting.  Where the soil property "CLAY PERCENT IN DEPTH 50-180CM (TX)" is:
	 => 60% the soil is limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as the number 1.0.
	  > 40 and < 60 the soil is somewhat limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as a number between 0 and 1.0.
	 =< 40% the soil is not limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as the number 0.

This evaluation checks the soil's bulk density within a depth of 50 to 150cm and indexes the degree to which bulk density is limiting.  Where the soil property "BULK DENSITY MAXIMUM IN DEPTH 50-150cm (TX)" is:
	 => 1.8 the soil is limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as the number 1.0.
	  < 1.8 the soil is not limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as the number 0.

This evaluation checks the soil surface reaction (pH).  The surface horizon ph_1_1_water check and evaluated.

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
 
  Where the surface soil component horizon property ph_1_1_water is less than 5.0 the evaluation is absolutely true and "TOO ACID" is a restrictive feature.
     AND
  Where the surface soil component horizon property ph_1_1_water is greater than 6.5 the evaluation is absolutely false and "TOO ACID" is not a restrictive feature.

As the depth to a  restrictive layer decreases then the soil hydrologic group approaches group "D".  At depths > than 20 inches (50cm) the hydrologic groups B and C are possible.  Hydrologic group A is possible at depths > 40 inches (100cm). 

The fuzzy space is defined as depth to restrictive layer < 50cm and > 100cm (< 20 inches and > 40 inches).
propname: DEPTH TO FIRST WATER RESTRICTIVE LAYER

evaldesc:
This evaluation checks for a moderately sloping condition.  The high, low, and representative values for Slope are selected.

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
  Where the soil property slope_gradient > 15 the evaluation is absolutely false and the restrictive feature is slope.
     OR
  Where the soil property slope_gradient < 8 the evaluation is absolutely true and the restrictive feature is not slope.

If no data is entered then the property is NULL and the default condition is used.

Ames Description Prior to 1996:

1___________________________________________________________________
                       |             LIMITS             |RESTRICTIVE
+                       ________________________________
     PROPERTY          |  SLIGHT  | MODERATE |  SEVERE  |  FEATURE
                       |          |          |          |
+___________________________________________________________________
 
 8. SLOPE (PCT)            <8         8-15       >15     SLOPE
 
 
 
 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________
 
 The low and high values in the slope range given on the Soils-5 are examined.
 
    A high slope > 15 gets a SEVERE rating.
    A low slope < 15 and a high slope > 8 gets a MODERATE rating.
    A low slope < 8 gets a SLIGHT rating.
 
 Phasing will be done using slope terms if more than one rating is given.

This evaluation tests the minimum Ksat above the restrictive layer and returns the evaluation where the following is true.  As Ksat decreases the hydrologic soil group approaches "D"

This evaluation causes any soil having ksat less than 40um/s to return a fuzzy number of 1.  Higher ksat is evaluated on the curve developed to represent the log scale relationship of the Ksat class ranges.

The intent is to discriminate against all but the most permeable soils in this part of the interpretation.

Soils with greater than 0 percent surface rock fragments are limiting.

It is absolutely true that with difficulty digging, or as the percentage of surface rock fragments increases, the preservation of bones is less likely because it will be a shallow burial.

This evaluation checks for coarse fragments greater than 10 inches in the soil surface.  The rock_frag_greater_than_10_in is check and evaluated.

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
 
  Where the result of the soil component surface horizon property rock_frag_greater_than_10_in is greater than 15 percent by weight the evaluation is absolutely true and "TOO STONY" is a restrictive feature.
     AND
  Where the result of the soil component surface horizon property rock_frag_greater_than_10_in is less than 5 percent by weight the evaluation is absolutely false and "TOO STONY" is not a restrictive feature.

Ames Description prior to  1996:
 ___________________________________________________________________
                       |             LIMITS             |RESTRICTIVE
+                       ________________________________
     PROPERTY          |  SLIGHT  | MODERATE |  SEVERE  |  FEATURE
                       |          |          |          |
+___________________________________________________________________
 
 13b. WEIGHT PERCENT >10"   <5         5-15       >15    TOO STONY
      (SURFACE LAYER)
  
 Description of Calculation:
 
The values given on the Soils-5 for fraction >10 inches are examined and a high value for each layer is determined.  The high value used in the calculation depends on which of the following conditions is met first.
 
 If a single value of '99' is entered, then an artificial value of 100 is used.
 
 If a single value not equal to '99' is entered, then an artificial value of 0 is used.
 
 Otherwise the high value is used.
 
 A separate weighted average is calculated for each surface layer.
 
       A weighted average > 15 gets a SEVERE rating.
       A weighted average > 5 and <= 15 gets a MODERATE rating.
       A weighted average <= 5 gets a SLIGHT rating.
 
 Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.

evaldesc:
This evaluation checks for the presence of bedrock within a specified depth.  The component data are check for restriction_kind = "bedrock (lithic)" or "bedrock (paralithic)" and restriction_depth_to_top is evaluated.

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
  Where the soil component property restriction_kind = "bedrock (lithic)" or "bedrock (paralithic)" and the restriction_depth_to_top is less then  cm (20 inches) then the evaluation is absolutely true potential for basements is severe.
     AND
  Where the soil component property restriction_kind = "bedrock (lithic)" or "bedrock (paralithic)" and the restriction_depth_to_top is greater then 203 cm (80 inches) then the evaluation is absolutely false and depth to bedrock is not a restrictive feature.
 
 If the low value is valid, then the low value is used.
 
 Otherwise an artificial value of 100 is used. 
           
	   A value <= 20 gets a SEVERE rating.
           A value > 20 and < 40 gets a MODERATE rating.
           A value >= 80 gets a SLIGHT rating.

 12/Evaluate the thickest layer between 10 and 60 inches and also the  bottom layer.  Choose the best rating.  When rating is based on  bottom layer, verify thickness.
 15/100 minus % passing No. 4 sieve > 25.
 16/100 minus % passing No. 4 sieve < 25.



 According to footnote 12, calculations are done for both the thickest layer and the bottom layer.

 Description of Calculation for Thickest Layer:
+______________________________________________

 The layer with the most inches between 10 and 60 inches is determined.  This could be a surface layer or a sublayer.  The unified values given on the Soils-5 are examined for the appropriate layer(s).

 The layer(s) being examined are rated according to the following algorithm:

 If GW, GP, GW-GM, or GP-GM is listed as a unified entry, or if SW, SP, SW-SM or SP-SM is listed as a unified entry and footnote 15 applies (see following description of footnote 15), then a PROBABLE rating is given.

 Otherwise an IMPROBABLE rating is given.

 If the thickest layer is a sublayer, then this property is rated the same as this sublayer's rating.

 If the thickest layer is a surface layer, then this property is rated PROBABLE if there is any PROBABLE surface layer rating.  If there is none, then it is rated IMPROBABLE.

 Restrictive feature terms are assigned appropriately.



 Description of Calculation for Bottom Layer:
+____________________________________________

 If the bottom layer has no data, then this calculation is skipped and the ratings for the thickest layer are chosen.

 Otherwise, this calculation is the same as that for the thickest layer, except it is done for the bottom layer.  The bottom layer,
 like the thickest layer, may be a surface layer or a sublayer.

 Calculations for Footnotes 15 and 16
+____________________________________

 To do the calculations for these footnotes, the values given on the Soils-5 for % passing No. 4 sieve are examined.

 % passing No. 4 sieve
+_____________________

 Assign values to No_4_Lo and No_4_Hi.

 If no data is entered, then No_4_Lo = 0 and No_4_Hi = 0.

 If a single value, say x, is entered, then No_4_Lo = x and  No_4_Hi = x.

 If the entry is a normal range, say x-y, then No_4_Lo = x and  No_4_Hi = y.

 Once these values have been assigned, the following calculations take place.

 100 - No_4_Lo = Lo
 100 - No_4_Hi = Hi

 maximum(Lo,Hi) = max

 If max > 25 then footnote 15 applies.
 If max <= 25 then footnote 16 applies.

 For Property No. 2, UNIFIED, the best ratings must be chosen between those calculated for the thickest layer and the bottom layer.

 If both the thickest and bottom layers are rated PROBABLE, then the bottom layer is chosen.

 If the thickest layer is rated PROBABLE and the bottom layer is rated IMPROBABLE, then the thickest layer is chosen.

 If the bottom layer is rated PROBABLE and the thickest layer is rated IMPROBABLE, then the bottom layer is chosen.

 If neither the thickest or bottom layer is rated PROBABLE, then they must both be rated IMPROBABLE and the bottom layer is chosen.

 If the ratings for the thickest layer were chosen, then the calculations on the following page for Property No. 3, LAYER
 THICKNESS, are done.

cryic, isofrigid, pergelic	July and August

				August, and September

thermic or			March, April, May, 
hyperthermic			June, July, August,

isohyperthermic,		May, June, July, August,

 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________
 
 The low value given on the Soils-5 for percent passing No. 10 sieve is examined for each surface layer.  The value used in the calculation depends on which of the following conditions is met first.
 
 If the low value is valid, then (100 - low value) is used.
 
 Otherwise an artificial value of 0 is used. 
 Each surface layer is rated separately according to the following algorithm: 
     A value > 50 gets a SEVERE rating.
     A value > 25 and <= 50 gets a MODERATE rating.

 Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition: 
  Where the weighted average of the soil property available_water_capacity for all layers within 150cm of the soil surface is >=9.5, the evaluation returns a value of 1.

The intent of this evaluation is to array soils on their available water holding capacity.  The lowest score a soil can receive is a 0.1.  Soils having 2 inches of available water or less will get a .1.  The highest score is a 1 which a soil would need 37 cm of available water to receive.    It is thought that very few soils can get a score of 1, thus, the upper scores will have some spread such that differences can be seen.

evaldesc:
This is a continuous evaluation examining the depth to low pH.  The horizon bulk density data is checked for a layer that has a pH of 3.5 or lower. 

A soil can be a complete or partial member of the set of soils that are limited by the depth to low pH and Restricted rooting is the set's restrictive feature.  If the depth to a low pH layer is less than 50 cm, then the soil is a complete member of the set.  If the depth to a low pH layer is greater than 50 cm and less than 75 cm then the soil is a partial member of the set.  A soil that has a low pH layer at a depth of more than 75 cm is not a member of the set.
propname: DEPTH TO PH <= 3.5 BELOW AN ORGANIC LAYER

	 = 0cm the soil is limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as the number 1.0.
	  > 0cm and < 50cm the soil is somewhat limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as a number between 0 and 1.0.
	 => 50cm the soil is not limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as the number 0.
propname: DPTH TO BULK DENSITY DIFFERENCE >.25 BELOW AN ORGANIC

evalname: Windthrow Depth to High Bulk Density
evaldesc:
This is a continuous evaluation examining the depth to high bulk density.  The horizon bulk density data is checked for a layer that is much denser than an ideal for the sand, silt, and clay content of the horizon.

A soil can be a complete or partial member of the set of soils that are limited by the depth to a dense layer and Restricted rooting is the set's restrictive feature.  If the depth to a dense layer is less than 50 cm (20 inches), then the soil is a complete member of the set.  If the depth to a dense layer is greater than 50 cm and less than 75 cm then the soil is a partial member of the set.  A soil that has a dense layer at a depth of more than 75 cm  is not a member of the set.
propname: DPTH TO BULK DENSITY DIFFERENCE >.25 BELOW AN ORGANIC

evalname: NCCPI - CEC 0-150cm or Bulk Density too High (Soybeans)
evaldesc:
CEC is handled in a manner analogous to AWC.  The amount of exchange for each layer is calculated, adjusted for density, and reduced for any rock fragment content.  The exchage amounts for each layer are then summed for all layers above excessively high bulk density.

A soil having a capacity of 50 meq or higher gets a score of 1, a soil having a capacity of 5 or less gets a score of 0.2.

evalname: pH 7.8 to 8.3 in Depth 20-150cm, wtd ave
evaldesc: This evaluation uses a generic grape growth ph function.

Dissolution of bone minerals is closely related to pH.  Dissolution is much faster in an acidic environment.  The potential of a soil to tend to preserve bones is to some extent a function of pH.  The actual pH in the vicinity of the bones would be difficult to determine.  The pH of the surrounding soil, with mixing during burial, can be estimated.

It is absolutely true that if the soil pH around bones is greater than 6.5, bones will be preserved, while at pH below 5.3, the statement is absolutely false.

Likelihood of bone preservation high	pH >6.5
Some likelihood of bone preservation	pH 5.3 to 6.5
Little likelihood of bone preservation	pH <5.3

evalname: (MI)Clay Percent  > 30% Thickest Layer to a Depth of 40 in
evaldesc:
This evaluation tests for percent of clay in the thickest layer to a depth of 40 inches or above a restrictive layer.

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
 
Where the claytotal is less than 30 percent the evaluation is absolutely true and "TOO CLAYEY" is not a restrictive features.
     AND
Where the claytotal is greater than or equal to 30 percent the evaluation is absolutely false and "TOO CLAYEY" is a restrictive features.

Current version contains major  revisions to the Ames 1996 version.

Ames prior to 1996

 1___________________________________________________________________
                                                         |             LIMITS                                                |  RESTRICTIVE
+                                                          ________________________________
     PROPERTY                            |   GOOD   |   FAIR            |   POOR               |  FEATURE
+___________________________________________________________________
 6. 17/USDA TEXTURE              ---           18/SCL,            SIC, C, SC        TOO CLAYEY
                                                                                 18/CL,
                                                                                 18/SICL
 17/Thickest layer between 0 and 40 inches.

 18/If soil contains >3% organic matter and has less than 35% clay,  rate GOOD.

 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________

 The layer with the most inches between 0 and 40 inches is determined.  This could be a surface layer or a sublayer.  The textures given on the Soils-5 are examined for the appropriate layer(s).

 The layer(s) being examined are rated according to the following algorithm:

 If SIC, C or SC is listed as a texture, then a POOR rating is    given.
 If 18/SCL, 18/CL or 18/SICL is listed as a texture, then a FAIR rating is given.  (See the next page for a description of the    calculation for footnote 18.)
 Otherwise a GOOD rating is given.

 If the thickest layer is a sublayer, then this property is rated the same as this sublayer's rating.

 If the thickest layer is a surface layer, then this property is rated GOOD if there is any GOOD surface layer rating, FAIR if there is any FAIR surface layer rating, and POOR if there is any POOR surface layer rating.  Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.

1

 Calculation of Footnote 18:
+___________________________

 To calculate footnote 18, an organic matter percentage and a clay percentage must be determined for each layer being rated.  The values given on the Soils-5 for organic matter and clay are examined.

 Organic matter
+______________
 Assign a value to OrgMat_Pct.

 For a surface layer, the OrgMat_Pct is the lower value in the range of values for organic matter for this layer.  If this value is blank, then OrgMat_Pct = 0.

 For a sublayer, the OrgMat_Pct is the minimum over all surface layers of the lower value in the range of values for organic matter.  If these values are all blank, then OrgMat_Pct = 0.

 Clay
+____
 Assign a value to Clay_Pct.
 If no data is entered, then Clay_Pct = 100.
 If the entry is a single number, say x, then Clay_Pct = x.
 If the entry is a normal range, say x-y, then Clay_Pct = y.
                     ---------------
 If OrgMat_Pct >= 3 and Clay_Pct <= 35, then rate GOOD.
 Otherwise rate FAIR.
