evaldesc:
This evaluation checks the available water of the soil.  The weight average of the component horizon available_water_capacity is calculated for the soil and the result is check and evaluated.

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
 
  Where the total of each layers weighted average of the soil component horizon property available_water_capacity to a depth of 150cm (60in) is less than 7.5 cm (3 in) the evaluation is absolutely true and "DROUGHTY" is a restrictive feature.
     AND
  Where the total of each layers weighted average of the soil component horizon property available_water_capacity to a depth of 150cm (60in) is greater than 15 cm (6 in) the evaluation is absolutely false and "DROUGHTY" is not a restrictive feature.

Ames Description prior to  1996:
 ___________________________________________________________________
                       |             LIMITS             |RESTRICTIVE
+                       ________________________________
     PROPERTY          |  SLIGHT  | MODERATE |  SEVERE  |  FEATURE
                       |          |          |          |
+___________________________________________________________________
 
 14. AVAILABLE WATER        >6        3-6         <3     DROUGHTY
     (WEIGHT AVE, 0 TO 60")
  
 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________
 
 The values given on the Soils-5 for available water are examined and
 
 If no data is entered, then the layer is skipped.
 
 If the entry is a single number, then the single value entered is used as the average.
 
 If the entry is of the form '<xxxx', then the average is taken using 0 and xxxx.
 
 Otherwise the low value is used.
 
 
 A separate total is calculated for each surface layer and then rated.  The total is the sum of each layer's average value times the number of inches in the layer for layers up to 60".
 
           A value < 3 gets a SEVERE rating.
           A value >= 3 and < 6 gets a MODERATE rating.
           A value >= 6 gets a SLIGHT rating.
 
 If there is a value rated SEVERE, then this property is rated SEVERE.  If there is a value rated MODERATE, then this property is rated MODERATE.  If there is a value rated SLIGHT, then this property is rated SLIGHT.  Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.

This evaluation checks the maximum clay content for all layers within a depth of 50 to 150 cm (20 to 60 inches). 
                                     
Where the maximum clay content is greater than 60% within a depth of 50 to 150 cm (20 to 60 inches) the evaluation is absolutely true and the restrictive feature is TOO CLAYEY.

 5. USDA TEXTURE           ---                 C, SIC                  ---           TOO CLAYEY 
    (20-60") 
 
  Description of Calculation: 
+___________________________ 
 
 The textures given on the Soils-5 are examined for the layers within 20-60 inches.  If surface layers are included in these depths, each is rated separately.  Then each sublayer is rated to determine the worst sublayer rating.  The rating algorithm used on each layer is as follows: 
 
If C or SIC is listed as a texture, then a MODERATE rating is given.  Otherwise a SLIGHT rating is given. 
 
If surface layers are not involved, then this property is rated the same as the worst sublayer rating. 
 
If surface layers are involved, then the following applies.  If the worst sublayer rating is MODERATE, then this property is rated  MODERATE. 
 
If the worst sublayer rating is SLIGHT, then this property is rated  SLIGHT if there is any SLIGHT surface layer rating, and it is rated MODERATE if there is any MODERATE surface layer rating.  Phasing  will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.

evaldesc:
This evaluation checks for the presence of a bedrock (lithic) or bedrock(paralithic) in the soil profile.  This index expresses the degree to which bedrock affects the suitability as a source for cohesive soil liner.  Where:
	bedrock (lithic) or bedrock(paralithic) is not present in the soil profile the degree of suitability 			index is expressed as the number 1.0.
	bedrock (lithic) or bedrock(paralithic) is present in the soil profile the degree of suitability index is 		expressed as the number 0.

This evaluation check percolation capacity of the soil.  The high, low, and representative values for sat_hydraulic_conductivity are selected for the bottom horizon.

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
  Where the soil horizon property sat_hydraulic_conductivity > 14 micrometers/second (2.0 inches/hour)the evaluation is absolutely true and the restrictive feature is seepage.
        AND
  Where the soil horizon property sat_hydraulic_conductivity =< 14.0 micrometers/second (2.00 inches/hour) the evaluation is absolutely false and the restrictive feature is not seepage.

If no data is entered, then an artificial default value(s) is used. 

Ames Description Prior to 1996:
                                                      |                           LIMITS                              |   RESTRICTIVE
     PROPERTY                         |  SLIGHT  | MODERATE |  SEVERE  |  FEATURE
 5. 4/PERMEABILITY                 ---                ---                    >2.0         SEEPAGE
      (IN/HR) (BOTTOM LAYER)
 
 4/Disregard (1) in all Aridisols except Salorthids and Aquic  subgroups, (2) all Aridic subgroups, and (3) all Torri great groups of Entisols except Aquic subgroups.
 
 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________
 
 If not disregarded, the bottom-most layer with a valid permeability entry is found.  This could be a surface layer or a sublayer.  For example, if there are no sublayers, or all the sublayers are missing permeability entries, then the surface layers will be examined. Otherwise, just the bottom single sublayer will be examined.
 
 The values given on the Soils-5 for permeability are examined and a high value determined for the appropriate layer(s).  The high value used for comparison depends on which of the following conditions is
 met first.
 
 If no data is entered, then an artificial value of 0 is used. 
 If the entry is a single number or is of the form '<xx', then the  single value entered is used.
 
 If the entry is of the form '>xx', then an artificial value of 100 
 
 Otherwise the high value is used.
 
 The layer(s) being examined are rated according to the following algorithm: 
           A value > 2.0 gets a SEVERE rating.
           A value <= 2.0 gets a SLIGHT rating.
 
 If the bottom layer is a sublayer, then this property is rated the same as this sublayer's rating.
 
 If the bottom layer is a surface layer, then this property is rated SLIGHT if there is any SLIGHT surface layer rating, and it is rated SEVERE if there is any SEVERE surface layer rating.  Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.
propname: NY KSAT BOTTOM HORIZON ABOVE BEDROCK
NY KSAT BOTTOM HORIZON ABOVE BEDROCK

evaldesc:
7/99 Modification:
This evaluation checks the filtering capacity of the soil.  The maximum high, low, and representative values for sat_hydraulic_conductivity are selected for each horizon between 24 to 72 inches and above any restrictive layer. 

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
  Where the soil horizon property sat_hydraulic_conductivity > 42 micrometers/second (6.0 inches/hr), the evaluaton is absolutely true and the restrictive feature is poor effluent filter field.
        AND
  Where the soil horizon property sat_hydraulic_conductivity <= 42 micrometers/second (6.0 inches/hour), the evaluation is absolutely false and the restrictive feature is not poor effluent filter field.

If no data is entered, then an artificial default value(s) is used.

In 1990 the evaluation depth was extended from a base of 40 inches to a base of 60 inches.

Ames Description Prior to 1996

                                              |                           LIMITS                              |  RESTRICTIVE
     PROPERTY                 |  SLIGHT  | MODERATE |  SEVERE  |  FEATURE
 7. PERMEABILITY          ---                 ---                  >6.0             POOR FILTER
    (IN/HR):    (24-40")            
 
 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________
   
 The values given on the Soils-5 for permeability are examined and a
 high value for each layer is determined.  The high value used for
 comparison depends on which of the following conditions is met
 first.
 
 If no data is entered, then an artificial value of 0 is used.
 
 If the entry is a single number or is of the form '<xx', then the
  single value entered is used.
 
 If the entry is of the form '>xx', then an artificial value of 100
  is used.
 
 Otherwise the high value is used.
 
 The layers within the given depths are examined.  If surface layers are included in these depths, each is rated separately.  Then each sublayer is rated to determine the worst sublayer rating.  The rating algorithm used on each layer is as follows:
 
           A value > 6.0 gets a SEVERE rating.
           A value <= 6.0 gets a SLIGHT rating.
 
 If surface layers are not involved, then this property is rated the
 same as the worst sublayer rating.
 
 If surface layers are involved, then the following applies.  If the
 worst sublayer rating is SEVERE, then this property is rated SEVERE
 and no phasing will be done, regardless of the surface layer
 ratings.
 
 If the worst sublayer rating is SLIGHT, then this property is rated
 SLIGHT if there is any SLIGHT surface layer rating, and it is rated
 SEVERE if there is any SEVERE surface layer rating.  Phasing will be
 done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.
propname: NY KSAT MINIMUM ABOVE RESTRICTIVE LAYER 30 TO 122 CM

This evaluation checks the greater than 3 inch fraction of the soil.  The weighted average of the component horizon rock_frag_3_to_10_in and rock_frag_greater_than_10_in is calculated for the 0 to 100 cm (40in) depth of the soil and the result is checked and evaluated.

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
 
  Where the total of each layers weighted average of the soil component horizon properties rock_frag_3_to_10_in and rock_frag_greater_than_10_in from 0 to a depth of 100cm (40in) is greater than 50% the evaluation is absolutely true and "LARGE STONES" is a restrictive feature.
     AND
  Where the total of each layers weighted average of the soil component horizon properties rock_frag_3_to_10_in and rock_frag_greater_than_10_in from 0 to a depth of 100cm (40in) less than 25% the evaluation is absolutely false and "LARGE STONES" is not a restrictive feature.

If no data is entered, then a default value of 0 is used.

Ames Description prior to  1996:

                                                  |                             LIMITS                            |  RESTRICTIVE
     PROPERTY                     |  SLIGHT  | MODERATE |  SEVERE  |  FEATURE
 9. 1/FRACTION >3 IN       <25                25-50                    >50            LARGE STONES
      (WT PCT)        
 
 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________
 
 The values given on the Soils-5 for fraction 3-10 inches are examined and a high value for each layer is determined.  The high value used in the calculation depends on which of the following conditions is met first.
 
 If a single value of '99' is entered, then an artificial value of 100 is used.
 
 If a single value not equal to '99' is entered, then an artificial value of 0 is used.
 
 Otherwise the high value is used.
 
 A separate weighted average to 40 inches is calculated for each surface layer.
 
           A weighted average > 50 gets a SEVERE rating.
           A weighted average > 25 and <= 50 gets a MODERATE rating.
           A weighted average <= 25 gets a SLIGHT rating.
 
 Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.
propname: NY FRAGMENTS > 75MM WEIGHTED AVE. IN DEPTH 0-122 CM

evaldesc:
This evaluation check percolation capacity of the soil.  The high, low, and representative values for sat_hydraulic_conductivity are selected for each horizon between 24 to 72 inches. 

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
  Where the soil horizon property sat_hydraulic_conductivity < 4.0 micrometers/second (0.60 inches/hour)the evaluation is absolutely true and the restrictive feature is slow percolation.
        AND
  Where the soil horizon property sat_hydraulic_conductivity => 14.0 micrometers/second (2.00 inches/hour) the evaluation is absolutely false and the restrictive feature is not slow percolation.

If no data is entered, then an artificial default value(s) is used. 

Ames Description Prior to 1996:
                                                   |                           LIMITS                              |   RESTRICTIVE
     PROPERTY                      |  SLIGHT  | MODERATE |  SEVERE  |  FEATURE
 7. PERMEABILITY              2.0-6.0          I/0.6-2.0               <0.6         PERCS SLOWLY
    (IN/HR):    (24-60")            

    I/Recheck to see if rating should be SLIGHT.

 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________
 
 This property is calculated as if it were two separate properties.
 The calculation for the first line (PERCS SLOWLY) is:
 
 The values given on the Soils-5 for permeability are examined and a
 low value for each layer is determined.  The low value used for
 comparison depends on which of the following conditions is met
 first.
 
 If no data is entered, then an artificial value of 100 is used.
 
 If the entry is of the form '<xx', then an artificial value of 0 is
  used.
 
 Otherwise the low value is used.
 
 The layers within the given depths are examined.  If surface layers
 are included in these depths, each is rated separately.  Then each
 sublayer is rated to determine the worst sublayer rating.  The
 rating algorithm used on each layer is as follows:

           A value < 0.6 gets a SEVERE rating
           A value >= 0.6 and < 2.0 gets a MODERATE rating.
           A value >= 2.0 gets a SLIGHT rating.
 
 If surface layers are not involved, then this property is rated the
 same as the worst sublayer rating.
 
 If surface layers are involved, then the following applies.  If the
 worst sublayer rating is SEVERE, then this property is rated SEVERE
 and no phasing will be done, regardless of the surface layer
 ratings.
 
 If the worst sublayer rating is MODERATE, then this property is
 rated MODERATE if there is any SLIGHT or MODERATE surface layer
 rating, and it is rated SEVERE if there is any SEVERE surface layer
 rating.  Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one
 rating is given.
 
 If the worst sublayer rating is SLIGHT, then this property is rated
 SLIGHT if there is any SLIGHT surface layer rating, MODERATE if
 there is any MODERATE surface layer rating, and SEVERE if there is
 any SEVERE surface layer rating.  Phasing will be done using texture
 terms if more than one rating is given.

evalname: NY Shallow to Bedrock (30 to 122 cm (12 to 48"))
evaldesc:
This evaluation checks for the presence of bedrock within a specified depth.  The component data are checked for restriction_kind = "bedrock (lithic)" or "bedrock (paralithic)" and restriction_depth_to_top is evaluated.

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
  Where the soil component property restriction_kind = "bedrock (lithic)" or "bedrock (paralithic)" and the restriction_depth_to_top is less than 30 cm (12 inches) then the evaluation is absolutely true and depth to bedrock is a restrictive feature.
     AND
  Where the soil component property restriction_kind = "bedrock (lithic)" or "bedrock (paralithic)" and the restriction_depth_to_top is greater than or equal to 122 cm (48 inches) then the evaluation is absolutely false and depth to bedrock is not a restrictive feature.


Ames Description prior to  1996:
                                                         |                            LIMITS                             |   RESTRICTIVE
     PROPERTY                            |  SLIGHT  | MODERATE |  SEVERE  |  FEATURE
 4. DEPTH TO BEDROCK             >72                40-72                <40            DEPTH TO ROCK
    (IN) 
 
 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________
 
 The values given on the Soils-5 for depth to rock are examined and
 the low value determined.  The low value used for comparison depends
 on which of the following conditions is met first.
 
 If the entry is '>60', then an artificial value of 100 is used.
 
 If the low value is valid, then the low value is used.
 
 Otherwise an artificial value of 100 is used. 
           A value < 40 gets a SEVERE rating.
           A value >= 40 and < 72 gets a MODERATE rating.
           A value >= 72 gets a SLIGHT rating.

evalname: NY Shallow to Dense Material (30 to 122 cm (12 to 48"))
evaldesc:
This evaluation checks for the presence of a component restriction within a specified depth.  The component data are checked for restriction_kind =   "fragipan", "duripan", "petrocalcic", "ortstein",  or "densic material" and restriction_depth_to_top is evaluated.

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
  Where the soil component property restriction_kind =  "fragipan", "duripan", "petrocalcic", "ortstein",  or "densic material" and the restriction_depth_to_top is less than 30 cm (12 inches) then the evaluation is absolutely true and depth to "CEMENTED PAN" is a restrictive feature.
     AND
  Where the soil component property restriction_kind =  "fragipan", "duripan", "petrocalcic", "ortstein",  or "petrogypsic" and the restriction_depth_to_top is greater than or equal to 122 cm (48 inches) then the evaluation is absolutely false and depth to pan or densic is not a restrictive feature.


Ames Description prior to  1996:

                                                            |                          LIMITS                               |  RESTRICTIVE
     PROPERTY                               |  SLIGHT  | MODERATE |  SEVERE  |  FEATURE
 5. DEPTH TO CEMENTED          >72                  40-72               <40            CEMENTED PAN
    PAN (IN) 
 
 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________
 
 The low value in the range of values given on the Soils-5 for depth
 to cemented pan is examined.  The value used for comparison depends
 on which of the following conditions is met first.
 
 If the low value is valid, then the low value is used.
 
 Otherwise an artificial value of 100 is used. 
           A value < 40 gets a SEVERE rating.
           A value >= 40 and < 72 gets a MODERATE rating.
           A value >= 72 gets a SLIGHT rating.

evalname: NY Wet, Ground Water Near Surface
evaldesc:
This evaluation checks for a saturated or wet condition within a depth of 180 cm (6 feet) of the soil surface.  The water moisture status for all layers are examined and those saturated or wet layers are evalutated for depth.

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
  Where soil_moisture_status is wet and the depth to soil_moist_depth_to_top is less than 30 cm (1 foot) the evaluation is absolutely true.
   OR
  Where soil_moisture_status is wet and the depth to  soil_moist_depth_to_top  is greater than or equal to 122 cm (4 feet) the evaluation is absolutely false.

If the soil_moisture_status is not wet or null, then the property assumption is that soil_moist_depth_to_top is NULL and no water table is present.

Ames Description Prior to 1996:
                                                       |                            LIMITS                             |   RESTRICTIVE
     PROPERTY                          |  SLIGHT  | MODERATE |  SEVERE  |  FEATURE
 3b:  WATER TABLE (FT)         >6                    4-6                       <4            WETNESS
 
The low value in the range of values given on the Soils-5 for depth to high water table is examined.  The value used for comparison depends on which of the following conditions are met first.
 
 If no data is entered, then an artificial value of 99.9 is used.
 
 Otherwise the low value is used. 
           A value < 4 gets a SEVERE rating.
           A value >= 4 and < 6 gets a MODERATE rating.
           A value >= 6 gets a SLIGHT rating.

This evaluation checks for the presence of cemented pan ("fragipan", "duripan", "petrocalcic", "ortstein",  or "petrogypsic") and if present evaluates the depth to the restrictive feature.

A soil can be a complete or partial member of the set of soils that are limited by the depth to cemented pan and DEPTH TO CEMENTED PAN is the set's restrictive feature.  If the depth to cemented pan is less than 50cm (20 inches), then the soil is a complete member of the set.  If the depth to cemented pan is greater than 50cm (20 inches) and less than 150cm (60 inches) then the soil is a partial member of the set.  A soil that has cemented pan at a depth of more than 150cm (60 inches) is not a member of the set.

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition: 
Where the soil property  frag3to10_r is null for all rows in the chorizon table, the evaluation returns a value of null.  If frag3to10_r is not null, a value of zero is returned.  This is done to make components lacking horizon data return a null and so be "not rated".

evaldesc:
This evaluation checks the available water of the soil.  The total avialable water is calculated for the soil and the result is check and evaluated.

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
 
  Where the total available water to a depth of 150cm (60in) is less than 7.5 cm (3 in) the evaluation is absolutely false and adequate water is not available.
     AND
  Where the total avaiilable water to a depth of 150cm (60in) is greater than 15 cm (6 in) the evaluation is absolutely true and adequate water is available
Ames Description prior to  1996:
 ___________________________________________________________________
                       |             LIMITS             |RESTRICTIVE
+                       ________________________________
     PROPERTY          |  SLIGHT  | MODERATE |  SEVERE  |  FEATURE
                       |          |          |          |
+___________________________________________________________________
 
 14. AVAILABLE WATER        >6        3-6         <3     DROUGHTY
     (WEIGHT AVE, 0 TO 60")
  
 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________
 
 The values given on the Soils-5 for available water are examined and
 
 If no data is entered, then the layer is skipped.
 
 If the entry is a single number, then the single value entered is used as the average.
 
 If the entry is of the form '<xxxx', then the average is taken using 0 and xxxx.
 
 Otherwise the low value is used.
 
 
 A separate total is calculated for each surface layer and then rated.  The total is the sum of each layer's average value times the number of inches in the layer for layers up to 60".
 
           A value < 3 gets a SEVERE rating.
           A value >= 3 and < 6 gets a MODERATE rating.
           A value >= 6 gets a SLIGHT rating.
 
 If there is a value rated SEVERE, then this property is rated SEVERE.  If there is a value rated MODERATE, then this property is rated MODERATE.  If there is a value rated SLIGHT, then this property is rated SLIGHT.  Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.

evaldesc:
This evaluation checks aashto_group_index.  The component data are check for aashto_group_index index number.

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
  Where the soil component property aashto_group_index is greaer then 8 then the evaluation is absolutely true and LOW STRENGTH is a restrictive feature.
     AND
  Where the soil component property aashto_group_index is less then 5 then the evaluation is absolutely false and LOW STRENGTH is not a restrictive feature.


Ames Description prior to  1996:
____________________________________________________________________
                                                             |             LIMITS                                              |RESTRICTIVE
+                                                         ________________________________
     PROPERTY                              |  SLIGHT  | MODERATE |  SEVERE     |  FEATURE
 +___________________________________________________________________
 
 6. 5/, 9/, 10/AASHTO                     <5                    5-8                        >8               LOW  STRENGTH
    GROUP INDEX NUMBER                                   
    
 5/If in Kaolinitic family, rate one class better if experience confirms.
 9/Thickest layer between 10 and 40 inches.
 10/GIN=(F-35)[.2+.005(LL-40)]+.01(F-15)(PI-10) where F=% passing No. 200 sieve.  If F<=35 and PI>=11, use only part 2 of equation.  Use median values.
 
 
 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________
 
 The layer with the most inches between 10 and 40 inches is determined.  This could be a surface layer or a sublayer.  The GIN is calculated for the appropriate layer(s) according to the given algorithm.
 
 To calculate the GIN, median values are needed for the following: percent passing No. 200 sieve (F), liquid limit (LL), and plasticity index (PI).  A median is calculated by adding the low and high values, then dividing by 2, unless special conditions exist.  The median calculation is given below for each of these three variables.
 
 Percent passing No. 200 sieve:
+______________________________
 
 If no valid data is entered, then an artificial value of 0 is used as the median.
 
 If a single value is entered, then this value is used as the median.
 
 Otherwise the median is calculated using the low and high values.
 

 
 Liquid limit:
+_____________
 
 If the entry is of the form '<xxx', then a median is calculated using 0 and xxx. 
 If the entry is of the form '>xxx', then a median is calculated using xxx and 100.
  If no valid data is entered, then an artificial value of 0 is used as the median. 
 If a single value is entered, then this value is used as the median. 
 Otherwise the median is calculated using the low and high values.
 
 Plasticity index:
+_________________
 
 If the entry is of the form '<xxx', then a median is calculated using 0 and xxx. 
 If the entry is of the form '>xxx', then a median is calculated using xxx and 100. 
 If the entry is of the form 'NP', then an artificial value of 0 is used as the median. 
 
 If the entry is of the form 'NP-xxx', then a median is calculated using 0 and xxx. 
 If no valid data is entered, then an artificial value of 0 is used as the median. 
 If a single value is entered, then this value is used as the median. 
 Otherwise the median is calculated using the low and high values. 
 After the GIN is calculated, the layer(s) being examined are rated according to the following algorithm: 
    If GIN > 8, then a SEVERE rating is given.
    If GIN > 5 and <= 8, then a MODERATE rating is given.
    If GIN <= 5, then a SLIGHT rating is given.
 
 If the thickest layer is a sublayer, then this property is rated the same as this sublayer's rating.  If minerology on the Soils-5 equals '28' (Kaolinitic), then a MODERATE rating is upgraded to SLIGHT, and a SEVERE rating is upgraded to MODERATE.
 
 If the thickest layer is a surface layer, then this property is rated SLIGHT if there is any SLIGHT surface layer rating, MODERATE if there is any MODERATE surface layer rating, and SEVERE if there is any SEVERE surface layer rating.  If minerology on the Soils-5 equals '28' (Kaolinitic), then a MODERATE rating is upgraded to SLIGHT, and a SEVERE rating is upgraded to MODERATE.  Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.

evalname: NY Percolation (1.4 to 4.0 um/sec) 30 to 122cm (12 to 48")
evaldesc:
This evaluation check percolation capacity of the soil.  The high, low, and representative values for sat_hydraulic_conductivity are selected for each horizon between 24 to 72 inches. 

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
  Where the soil horizon property sat_hydraulic_conductivity < 4.0 micrometers/second (0.60 inches/hour)the evaluation is absolutely true and the restrictive feature is slow percolation.
        AND
  Where the soil horizon property sat_hydraulic_conductivity => 14.0 micrometers/second (2.00 inches/hour) the evaluation is absolutely false and the restrictive feature is not slow percolation.

If no data is entered, then an artificial default value(s) is used. 

Ames Description Prior to 1996:
                                                   |                           LIMITS                              |   RESTRICTIVE
     PROPERTY                      |  SLIGHT  | MODERATE |  SEVERE  |  FEATURE
 7. PERMEABILITY              2.0-6.0          I/0.6-2.0               <0.6         PERCS SLOWLY
    (IN/HR):    (24-60")            

    I/Recheck to see if rating should be SLIGHT.

 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________
 
 This property is calculated as if it were two separate properties.
 The calculation for the first line (PERCS SLOWLY) is:
 
 The values given on the Soils-5 for permeability are examined and a
 low value for each layer is determined.  The low value used for
 comparison depends on which of the following conditions is met
 first.
 
 If no data is entered, then an artificial value of 100 is used.
 
 If the entry is of the form '<xx', then an artificial value of 0 is
  used.
 
 Otherwise the low value is used.
 
 The layers within the given depths are examined.  If surface layers
 are included in these depths, each is rated separately.  Then each
 sublayer is rated to determine the worst sublayer rating.  The
 rating algorithm used on each layer is as follows:

           A value < 0.6 gets a SEVERE rating
           A value >= 0.6 and < 2.0 gets a MODERATE rating.
           A value >= 2.0 gets a SLIGHT rating.
 
 If surface layers are not involved, then this property is rated the
 same as the worst sublayer rating.
 
 If surface layers are involved, then the following applies.  If the
 worst sublayer rating is SEVERE, then this property is rated SEVERE
 and no phasing will be done, regardless of the surface layer
 ratings.
 
 If the worst sublayer rating is MODERATE, then this property is
 rated MODERATE if there is any SLIGHT or MODERATE surface layer
 rating, and it is rated SEVERE if there is any SEVERE surface layer
 rating.  Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one
 rating is given.
 
 If the worst sublayer rating is SLIGHT, then this property is rated
 SLIGHT if there is any SLIGHT surface layer rating, MODERATE if
 there is any MODERATE surface layer rating, and SEVERE if there is
 any SEVERE surface layer rating.  Phasing will be done using texture
 terms if more than one rating is given.
propname: NY KSAT (1.4 - 4.0) MINIMUM ABOVE RESTRICTIVE FEATURE <122CM

This evaluation checks the minimum soil pH to a depth of 120cm and indexes the degree, which pH is optimum for plant growth.  When the pH of the soil is more acid then the optimum pH range, there is reduced availability of nutrients and heavy metals concentrations may limit plant growth.  Where the soil property "SOIL REACTION 1-1 WATER; MINIMUM, 0 TO 120CM (TX)" is:

	 = 6.3 the soil pH is optimum and the degree of suitability is expressed as the number 1.0.
	 < 6.3 the soil is less then optimum and the degree of suitability is expressed as a number between 0.45 and 1.0.

This evaluation checks the soil's pH to a depth of 100cm and indexes the degree to which pH is limiting.  Where the soil property "SOIL REACTION 1-1 WATER; MINIMUM, 0 TO 120CM (TX)" is:

	 =< 4.5 the soil is limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as the number 1.0.
	  > 4.5 and < 6.0 the soil is somewhat limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as a number between 0 and 1.0.
	 => 6.0 the soil is not limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as the number 0.

Where the soil property "SOIL REACTION 1-1 WATER; MAXIMUM, 0 TO 120CM (TX)" is:

	 = 6.3 the soil pH is optimum and the degree of suitability is expressed as the number 1.0.
	 > 6.3 the soil is less then optimum and the degree of suitability is expressed as a number between 0.45 and 1.0.

evaldesc:
This evaluation checks the landscapes flooding interaction during the growing season and indexes the degree to which flooding frequency and duration are is limiting.  For this interpretive rule flooding interaction is represented by converting flooding class and frequency to numeric values and multiplying those values to obtain the numeric value for the interaction of frequency and duration.  Assigned numeric values are:

Flooding Frequency Class		Flooding Duration Class
"frequent" then 0.85			"long" then 0.95  
"very frequent" then 0.70 		"very long" then 0.85 
Else 1.0				Else 1.0

Example frequent long flooding would be given a value of .85 * 0.95 = 0.808

Where the soil property "FLOODING INTERACTION - Growing Season (TX)" is:
	 
	 = 1.0 landscape hydrologic condition is optimum for plant growth and the degree of limitation is expressed as the number 1.0.
	 < 1.0 and > 0 landscape hydrologic condition is less then optimum for plant growth and the degree of limitation is expressed as a number between 0.59 and 1.0.

This evaluation checks the landscapes ponding interaction during the growing season and indexes the degree to which flooding frequency and duration are is limiting.  For this interpretive rule ponding interaction is represented by converting ponding class and frequency to numeric values and multiplying those values to obtain the numeric value for the interaction of frequency and duration.  Assigned numeric values are:

Ponding Frequency Class			Ponding Duration Class
"none" or null then  1.00		"null", "very brief" then 1.00
"rare" then 0.975			"brief" then 0.95  
"occasional" then 0.90			"long" then 0.85  
"frequent" then 0.75 			"very long" then 0.75 

Example occasional long ponding would be given a value of .90 * 0.85 = 0.765

Where the soil property "PONDING INTERACTION - Growing Season (TX)" is:
	 
	 = 1.0 landscape hydrologic condition is optimum for plant growth and the degree of limitation is expressed as the number 1.0.
	 < 1.0 and > 0 landscape hydrologic condition is less then optimum for plant growth and the degree of limitation is expressed as a number between 0.56 and 1.0.

The intent of this evaluation is to array soils on their available water holding capacity.  The lowest score a soil can receive is a 0.1.  Soils having 2 inches of available water or less will get a .1.  The highest score is a 1 which a soil would need 37 cm of available water to receive.    It is thought that very few soils can get a score of 1, thus, the upper scores will have some spread such that differences can be seen.

evaldesc:
This evaluation checks for the presence of occasional flooding on poorly and very poorly drained soils and indexes the value.  This index expresses the degree of relationship between flooding and crop productivity.  Where flooding is:
	= ocassional the degree of suitability index is expressed as the number 0.
	= very frequent, frequent, rare, or none the degree of suitability index is expressed as the number 1.

This evaluation uses the MAP/MAAT ration to represent the effect of climate on the production capacity or growth potential of the soil.  MAP/MAAT ratio is indexed to evaluate the degree to which climate affects plant growth.  Where the soil property "MAP/MAAT RATIO (TX)" is:

	=> 60 soil climate is considered not dry and this condition is expressed as the number 0.
	 < 60 soil climate is considered dry and this condition is express and the number 1.0.

This evaluation uses the MAP/MAAT ratio to represent the effect of climate on the production capacity or growth potential of the soil.  MAP/MAAT ratio is indexed to evaluate the degree to which climate affects plant growth.  Where the soil property "MAP/MAAT RATIO (TX)" is:

	=> 60 the soil climate is optimum and the degree of suitability is expressed as the number 1.0.
	=> 0 and < 60 the soil's climate is less then optimum and the degree of suitability is expressed as a number between 1.0 and 0.5.

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition: 
  Where the sum of the thickness is >=29cm for all horizons within 150cm of the surface that have an rv value of the soil property sat_hydraulic_conductivity (ksat) < 9.2 (moderate permeability or slower), the evaluation returns a value of 1.

This evaluation checks the landscapes flooding interaction during the growing season and indexes the degree to which flooding frequency and duration are is limiting.  For this interpretive rule flooding interaction is represented by converting flooding class and frequency to numeric values and multiplying those values to obtain the numeric value for the interaction of frequency and duration.  Assigned numeric values are:

Assigned numeric values are:

Flooding Frequency Class		Flooding Duration Class
"rare" then 0.975			"brief" then 0.975
"occasional" then 0.95			"long" then 0.95 
"frequent" then 0.85 			"very long" then 0.85
"very frequent" then 0.70		Else 1.0
Else 1.0				 

Example frequent long flooding would be given a value of .85 * 0.95 = 0.808

Where the soil property "FLOODING INTERACTION BENIFITIAL - Growing Season (TX)" is:

	 < 1.0 and > .80  flooding on drier landscapes is optimum for plant growth and the degree of limitation is expressed as the number 1.0.
	 = 1.0 or <= .80  flooding on drier landscape is less then optimum for plant growth and the degree of limitation is expressed as the number 0.

evaldesc:
This evaluation checks aashto_group_index.  The component data are check for aashto_group_index index number.

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
  Where the soil component property aashto_group_index is greaer then 8 then the evaluation is absolutely true and LOW STRENGTH is a restrictive feature.
     AND
  Where the soil component property aashto_group_index is less then 5 then the evaluation is absolutely false and LOW STRENGTH is not a restrictive feature.


Ames Description prior to  1996:
____________________________________________________________________
                                                             |             LIMITS                                              |RESTRICTIVE
+                                                         ________________________________
     PROPERTY                              |  SLIGHT  | MODERATE |  SEVERE     |  FEATURE
 +___________________________________________________________________
 
 6. 5/, 9/, 10/AASHTO                     <5                    5-8                        >8               LOW  STRENGTH
    GROUP INDEX NUMBER                                   
    
 5/If in Kaolinitic family, rate one class better if experience confirms.
 9/Thickest layer between 10 and 40 inches.
 10/GIN=(F-35)[.2+.005(LL-40)]+.01(F-15)(PI-10) where F=% passing No. 200 sieve.  If F<=35 and PI>=11, use only part 2 of equation.  Use median values.
 
 
 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________
 
 The layer with the most inches between 10 and 40 inches is determined.  This could be a surface layer or a sublayer.  The GIN is calculated for the appropriate layer(s) according to the given algorithm.
 
 To calculate the GIN, median values are needed for the following: percent passing No. 200 sieve (F), liquid limit (LL), and plasticity index (PI).  A median is calculated by adding the low and high values, then dividing by 2, unless special conditions exist.  The median calculation is given below for each of these three variables.
 
 Percent passing No. 200 sieve:
+______________________________
 
 If no valid data is entered, then an artificial value of 0 is used as the median.
 
 If a single value is entered, then this value is used as the median.
 
 Otherwise the median is calculated using the low and high values.
 

 
 Liquid limit:
+_____________
 
 If the entry is of the form '<xxx', then a median is calculated using 0 and xxx. 
 If the entry is of the form '>xxx', then a median is calculated using xxx and 100.
  If no valid data is entered, then an artificial value of 0 is used as the median. 
 If a single value is entered, then this value is used as the median. 
 Otherwise the median is calculated using the low and high values.
 
 Plasticity index:
+_________________
 
 If the entry is of the form '<xxx', then a median is calculated using 0 and xxx. 
 If the entry is of the form '>xxx', then a median is calculated using xxx and 100. 
 If the entry is of the form 'NP', then an artificial value of 0 is used as the median. 
 
 If the entry is of the form 'NP-xxx', then a median is calculated using 0 and xxx. 
 If no valid data is entered, then an artificial value of 0 is used as the median. 
 If a single value is entered, then this value is used as the median. 
 Otherwise the median is calculated using the low and high values. 
 After the GIN is calculated, the layer(s) being examined are rated according to the following algorithm: 
    If GIN > 8, then a SEVERE rating is given.
    If GIN > 5 and <= 8, then a MODERATE rating is given.
    If GIN <= 5, then a SLIGHT rating is given.
 
 If the thickest layer is a sublayer, then this property is rated the same as this sublayer's rating.  If minerology on the Soils-5 equals '28' (Kaolinitic), then a MODERATE rating is upgraded to SLIGHT, and a SEVERE rating is upgraded to MODERATE.
 
 If the thickest layer is a surface layer, then this property is rated SLIGHT if there is any SLIGHT surface layer rating, MODERATE if there is any MODERATE surface layer rating, and SEVERE if there is any SEVERE surface layer rating.  If minerology on the Soils-5 equals '28' (Kaolinitic), then a MODERATE rating is upgraded to SLIGHT, and a SEVERE rating is upgraded to MODERATE.  Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.
propname: AASHTO GI IN DEPTH 0-50CM, WTD AVE

Slopes in-between are most desireable since less soil is required to be excavated and personal stability on the slope is adequate.

7/99 Modification:
This evaluation checks the filtering capacity of the soil.  The maximum high, low, and representative values for sat_hydraulic_conductivity are selected for each horizon between 24 to 72 inches and above any restrictive layer. 

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
  Where the soil horizon property sat_hydraulic_conductivity > 42 micrometers/second (6.0 inches/hr), the evaluaton is absolutely true and the restrictive feature is poor effluent filter field.
        AND
  Where the soil horizon property sat_hydraulic_conductivity <= 42 micrometers/second (6.0 inches/hour), the evaluation is absolutely false and the restrictive feature is not poor effluent filter field.

If no data is entered, then an artificial default value(s) is used.

In 1990 the evaluation depth was extended from a base of 40 inches to a base of 60 inches.

Ames Description Prior to 1996

                                              |                           LIMITS                              |  RESTRICTIVE
     PROPERTY                 |  SLIGHT  | MODERATE |  SEVERE  |  FEATURE
 7. PERMEABILITY          ---                 ---                  >6.0             POOR FILTER
    (IN/HR):    (24-40")            
 
 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________
   
 The values given on the Soils-5 for permeability are examined and a
 high value for each layer is determined.  The high value used for
 comparison depends on which of the following conditions is met
 first.
 
 If no data is entered, then an artificial value of 0 is used.
 
 If the entry is a single number or is of the form '<xx', then the
  single value entered is used.
 
 If the entry is of the form '>xx', then an artificial value of 100
  is used.
 
 Otherwise the high value is used.
 
 The layers within the given depths are examined.  If surface layers are included in these depths, each is rated separately.  Then each sublayer is rated to determine the worst sublayer rating.  The rating algorithm used on each layer is as follows:
 
           A value > 6.0 gets a SEVERE rating.
           A value <= 6.0 gets a SLIGHT rating.
 
 If surface layers are not involved, then this property is rated the
 same as the worst sublayer rating.
 
 If surface layers are involved, then the following applies.  If the
 worst sublayer rating is SEVERE, then this property is rated SEVERE
 and no phasing will be done, regardless of the surface layer
 ratings.
 
 If the worst sublayer rating is SLIGHT, then this property is rated
 SLIGHT if there is any SLIGHT surface layer rating, and it is rated
 SEVERE if there is any SEVERE surface layer rating.  Phasing will be
 done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.
propname: KSAT HIGHEST MIN ABOVE RESTR, BELOW O, 60 TO 150 CM

evalname: Depth to root limiting bulk density 50 to 100cm
evaldesc:
This evaluation is checks the depth of  the first layer that has bulk density limiting for root growth.
 
Where the depth to the first layer with a bulk_density_one_third_bar greater than a root limiting density is greater than 100cm the evaluation is absolutely true and  HIGH BULK DENSITY is not a restrictive feature. 
    AND
Where the depth to the first layer with a bulk_density_one_third_bar greater than a root limiting density is less than 50cm the evaluation is absolutely false and HIGH BULK DENSITY is a restrictive feature.


Depth to a root limiting layer: >100cm is not limiting
				50 to 100 cm is somewhat limiting
				<50 cm is limiting
				
The restrictive feature is area reclaim.


The root limiting bulk density is calculated from published data.  The description of the process is given in the Property description.

evalname: Wet, Ground Water Near Surface, Below O (120 - 180cm)
evaldesc:
This evaluation checks for a saturated or wet condition within a depth of 180 cm (6 feet) of the soil surface.  The water moisture status for all layers are examined and those saturated or wet layers are evalutated for depth.

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
  Where soil_moisture_status is wet and the depth to soil_moist_depth_to_top is less than 120 cm (4 feet) the evaluation is absolutely true.
   OR
  Where soil_moisture_status is wet and the depth to  soil_moist_depth_to_top  is greater than 180 cm (6 feet) the evaluation is absolutely false.

If the soil_moisture_status is not wet or null, then the property asumption is that soil_moist_depth_to_top is NULL and no water table is present.

Ames Description Prior to 1996:
                                                       |                            LIMITS                             |   RESTRICTIVE
     PROPERTY                          |  SLIGHT  | MODERATE |  SEVERE  |  FEATURE
 3b:  WATER TABLE (FT)         >6                    4-6                       <4            WETNESS
 
The low value in the range of values given on the Soils-5 for depth to high water table is examined.  The value used for comparison depends on which of the following conditions are met first.
 
 If no data is entered, then an artificial value of 99.9 is used.
 
 Otherwise the low value is used. 
           A value < 4 gets a SEVERE rating.
           A value >= 4 and < 6 gets a MODERATE rating.
           A value >= 6 gets a SLIGHT rating.
propname: HIGH WATER TABLE DEPTH MINIMUM, BELOW O

evaldesc:

The fuzzy space is as follows:		0-3cm slight
					3-12cm subsidence problem
					12-18cm severe subsidence problem
					>18cm very severe subsidence problem

evalname: Shallow to Bedrock, 100 to 180cm, Below O
evaldesc:
This evaluation checks for the presence of bedrock within a specified depth.  The component data are check for restriction_kind = "bedrock (lithic)" or "bedrock (paralithic)" and restriction_depth_to_top is evaluated.

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
  Where the soil component property restriction_kind = "bedrock (lithic)" or "bedrock (paralithic)" and the restriction_depth_to_top is less then 100 cm (40 inches) then the evaluation is absolutely true and depth to bedrock is a restrictive feature.
     AND
  Where the soil component property restriction_kind = "bedrock (lithic)" or "bedrock (paralithic)" and the restriction_depth_to_top is greater then 182 cm (72 inches) then the evaluation is absolutely false and depth to bedrock is not a restrictive feature.


Ames Description prior to  1996:
                                                         |                            LIMITS                             |   RESTRICTIVE
     PROPERTY                            |  SLIGHT  | MODERATE |  SEVERE  |  FEATURE
 4. DEPTH TO BEDROCK             >72                40-72                <40            DEPTH TO ROCK
    (IN) 
 
 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________
 
 The values given on the Soils-5 for depth to rock are examined and
 the low value determined.  The low value used for comparison depends
 on which of the following conditions is met first.
 
 If the entry is '>60', then an artificial value of 100 is used.
 
 If the low value is valid, then the low value is used.
 
 Otherwise an artificial value of 100 is used. 
           A value < 40 gets a SEVERE rating.
           A value >= 40 and < 72 gets a MODERATE rating.
           A value >= 72 gets a SLIGHT rating.

evalname: Shallow to Permafrost, 50 to 100cm, Below O
evaldesc:
This evaluation checks for the presence of permafrost and if present evaluates permafrost depth.  The component data are check for restriction_kind = "permafrost" and restriction_depth_to_top is evaluated.

A soil can be a complete or partial member of the set of soils that are limited by the depth to permafrost and PERMAFROST is the set's restrictive feature.  If the depth to permafrost is less than 50 cm (20 inches), then the soil is a complete member of the set.  If the depth to permafrost is greater than 50 cm (20 inches) and less than 100 cm (40 inches) then the soil is a partial member of the set.  A soil that has permafrost at a depth of more than 100 cm (40 inches) is not a member of the set.

evaldesc:
The milliequivalents of exchange of the upper 30cm of soil is evaluated in the range of 0 to 10.  The statement "It is absolutely true that if a soil layer 30cm thick has at least 10 milliequivalents of exchange then cesium and strontium will be sequestered".

Limits:

	milliequivalents of exchange 	0	no sequestering from exchange  
	milliequivalents of exchange 	0-10	some sequestering from exchange  
	milliequivalents of exchange 	>10	high degree of sequestering from exchange.

The milliequivalents of exchange of the upper 30cm of soil is evaluated in the range of 0 to 10.  The statement "It is absolutely true that if a soil layer 30cm thick has at least 10 milliequivalents of exchange then cesium and strontium will be sequestered".

Limits:

	milliequivalents of exchange 	0	no sequestering from exchange  
	milliequivalents of exchange 	0-10	some sequestering from exchange  
	milliequivalents of exchange 	>10	high degree of sequestering from exchange.

The milliequivalents of exchange of the upper 30cm of soil is evaluated in the range of 0 to 10.  The statement "It is absolutely true that if a soil layer 30cm thick has milliequivalents of exchange of zero then cesium and strontium will potentially be bioaccumulated".

Limits:

	milliequivalents of exchange 	0	high potential for bioaccumulation
	milliequivalents of exchange 	0-10	moderate potential for bioaccumulation
	milliequivalents of exchange 	>10	low potential for bioaccumulation.

The calcium carbonate equivalency of the upper 30cm of soil is evaluated in the range of 0 to 10.  The statement "It is absolutely true that if a soil layer 30cm thick has a CCE of at least 10 then cesium and strontium will be sequestered".

Limits:

	CCE	0	no sequestering from CaCO3
	CCE	0-10	some sequestering from CaCO3
	CCE	>10	high degree of sequestering from CaCO3
(Null)

The gypsum content of the upper 30cm of soil is evaluated in the range of 0 to 10.  The statement "It is absolutely true that if a soil layer 30cm thick has a gypsum content of at least 10 then cesium and strontium will be sequestered".

Limits:

	gypsum content	0	no sequestering from gypsum 
	gypsum content	0-10	some sequestering from gypsum
	gypsum content	>10	high degree of sequestering from gypsum

If the soil's gypsum content is high then gypsum is a restrictive feature.

    IN (WT PCT)                                                                                      STONES

 6/Thickest layer between 10 and 60 inches.



 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________

 NOTE:  THE CURRENT CALCULATION FOR THIS PROPERTY IS ACTUALLY A WEIGHTED AVERAGE FROM 10 TO 60 INCHES.

 The values given on the Soils-5 for fraction 3-10 inches are examined and a high value for each layer within 10 to 60 inches is
 determined.  The given depths may or may not include surface layers.   The high value used in the calculation depends on which of the following conditions is met first.

 If a single value of '99' is entered, then an artificial value of 100 is used.

 If a single value not equal to '99' is entered, then an artificial  value of 0 is used.

 Otherwise the high value is used.

 If surface layers are not included, then a weighted average from 10 to 60 inches is calculated and rated.  No phasing is done.

 If surface layers are included, then a separate weighted average from 10 to 60 inches is calculated and rated for each surface
 layer.  Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.

 The rating algorithm is as follows:

    A weighted average > 50 gets an IMPROBABLE rating.
    A weighted average <= 50 gets a PROBABLE rating.

The unified values given on the Soils-5 are examined for each layer.

+______________________________________________

 The layer with the most inches between 10 and 60 inches is determined.  This could be a surface layer or a sublayer.  The unified values given on the Soils-5 are examined for the appropriate layer(s).

 The layer(s) being examined are rated according to the following algorithm:

 If GW, GP, GW-GM, or GP-GM is listed as a unified entry, or if SW, SP, SW-SM or SP-SM is listed as a unified entry and footnote 15 applies (see following description of footnote 15), then a PROBABLE rating is given.

 Otherwise an IMPROBABLE rating is given.

 If the thickest layer is a sublayer, then this property is rated the same as this sublayer's rating.

 If the thickest layer is a surface layer, then this property is rated PROBABLE if there is any PROBABLE surface layer rating.  If there is none, then it is rated IMPROBABLE.

 Restrictive feature terms are assigned appropriately.



 Description of Calculation for Bottom Layer:
+____________________________________________

 If the bottom layer has no data, then this calculation is skipped and the ratings for the thickest layer are chosen.

 Otherwise, this calculation is the same as that for the thickest layer, except it is done for the bottom layer.  The bottom layer,

 % passing No. 4 sieve
+_____________________

 If a single value, say x, is entered, then No_4_Lo = x and  No_4_Hi = x.

 If the entry is a normal range, say x-y, then No_4_Lo = x and  No_4_Hi = y.

 100 - No_4_Lo = Lo

 If max > 25 then footnote 15 applies.
 If max <= 25 then footnote 16 applies.

 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________

 The layer with the most inches between 0 and 40 inches is determined.  This could be a surface layer or a sublayer.  The textures given on the Soils-5 are examined for the appropriate layer(s).

1

 Calculation of Footnote 18:
+___________________________

 Organic matter
+______________
 Assign a value to OrgMat_Pct.

 For a surface layer, the OrgMat_Pct is the lower value in the range of values for organic matter for this layer.  If this value is blank, then OrgMat_Pct = 0.

 For a sublayer, the OrgMat_Pct is the minimum over all surface layers of the lower value in the range of values for organic matter.  If these values are all blank, then OrgMat_Pct = 0.

 Clay
+____
 Assign a value to Clay_Pct.
 If no data is entered, then Clay_Pct = 100.
 If the entry is a single number, say x, then Clay_Pct = x.
 If the entry is a normal range, say x-y, then Clay_Pct = y.
                     ---------------
 If OrgMat_Pct >= 3 and Clay_Pct <= 35, then rate GOOD.
 Otherwise rate FAIR.

evaldesc:
This evaluation checks for the thickest layer's coarse fragments between 3 and 10 inches within a depth of 100cm to 180cm (40 to 72 inches).  The rock_frag_3_to_10_in is check and evaluated.

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
 
Where the thickest layer  rock_frag_3_to_10_in soil property is less then 5 percent by weight the evaluation is absolutely true and "AREA RECLAIMATION" is not a restrictive feature.
     AND
Where the thickest layer  rock_frag_3_to_10_in soil property is greater then 25 percent by weight the evaluation is absolutely false and "AREA RECLAIMATION" is a restrictive feature.

Ames prior to 1996 (8a.)
 
  1___________________________________________________________________
                                          |             LIMITS                            |    RESTRICTIVE
+                                       ________________________________
     PROPERTY             |   GOOD   |   FAIR   |   POOR   |     FEATURE
+___________________________________________________________________
 8. 8/FRACTION >3 IN
    (WT PCT):
 a) (0-40")                           <5               5-25          >25            LARGE STONES
 b) (40-60")                        <15            15-30         >30            AREA RECLAIM

 9. 8/COARSE
    FRAGMENTS (PCT):
 a) (0-40")                          <5                 5-25         >25              SMALL STONES
 b) (40-60")                       <25             25-50         >50              AREA RECLAIM

 8/Sum (100-% passing No. 10 sieve) and fraction >3 in.  Use   dominant condition for restrictive feature.

 Lines 8a and 9a are calculated together, and lines 8b and 9b are calculated together.

 Description of Calculation for lines 8a and 9a:
+_______________________________________________

 The values for % passing No. 10 sieve and fraction 3-10 inches given on the Soils-5 are examined.  These values are used in the calculations of weighted averages from 0-40 inches.

 % passing No. 10 sieve
+______________________

 The low value is examined for each layer within the given depths. The value used for each layer in the calculation depends on which of the following conditions is met first.

 If the low value is valid, then (100 - low value) is used.

 Otherwise an artificial value of 0 is used.

 Fraction 3-10 inches
+____________________

 The values are examined for each layer within the given depths and a high value is determined.  The high value used for each layer in the calculation depends on which of the following conditions is met first.

 If a single value of '99' is entered, then an artificial value of  100 is used.

 If a single value not equal to '99' is entered, then an artificial  value of 0 is used.

 Otherwise the high value is used.

 A separate weighted average is calculated for each surface layer for both % passing No. 10 sieve and fraction 3-10 inches.  For each surface layer, the two weighted averages are added together (call this SUM) and rated.

 To determine the dominant condition, a new weighted average from 0-40 inches is calculated for both % passing No. 10 sieve and fraction 3-10 inches.  The surface layer value used in each calculation is the maximum value over all surface layers.  If the weighted average for fraction 3-10 inches is >= the weighted average for % passing No. 10, then the restrictive term used is LARGE STONES.  Otherwise it is SMALL STONES.

           A SUM > 25 gets a POOR rating.
           A SUM > 5 and <= 25 gets a FAIR rating.
           A SUM <= 5 gets a GOOD rating.

 Description of Calculation for lines 8b and 9b:
+_______________________________________________

 This calculation is similar to that above, except we will assume that no surface layers are involved.

 A separate weighted average from 40-60 inches is calculated for both % passing No. 10 sieve and fraction 3-10 inches.  The two weighted averages are added together (call this SUM).

 If the weighted average for fraction 3-10 inches is >= the weighted average for % passing No. 10 sieve, then the following ratings apply:

           A SUM > 30 gets a POOR rating.
           A SUM > 15 and <= 30 gets a FAIR rating.
           A SUM <= 15 gets a GOOD rating.
 Otherwise the following ratings apply:
           A SUM > 50 gets a POOR rating.
           A SUM > 25 and <= 50 gets a FAIR rating.
           A SUM <= 25 gets a GOOD rating.
                     ---------------
 It is possible that Property No. 4, DEPTH TO BULK DENSITY, Property No. 8b, FRACTION >3 IN (40-60") and Property No. 9b, COARSE FRAGMENTS (40-60") may all have the same restrictive term, AREA RECLAIM.  At this point, a check must be made to ensure that this term will only appear in the final output at most once.

 If No. 4 is marked POOR, then No. 8b and No. 9b are cancelled out. Else if No. 8b is marked POOR, then No. 9b is cancelled out.  The same procedure is repeated for FAIR.

This evaluation checks for the thickest layer's coarse fragments between 3 and 10 inches in the upper 100cm (40 inches) of the soil.  The rock_frag_3_to_10_in is check and evaluated.

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
 
Where the thickest layer  rock_frag_3_to_10_in soil property is less then 5 percent by weight the evaluation is absolutely true and "ROCK FRAGMENTS" are not a restrictive feature.
     AND
Where the thickest layer  rock_frag_3_to_10_in soil property is greater then 25 percent by weight the evaluation is absolutely false and "ROCK FRAGMENTS" are a restrictive feature.

Ames prior to 1996 (8a.)
 
  1___________________________________________________________________
                                          |             LIMITS                            |    RESTRICTIVE
+                                       ________________________________
     PROPERTY             |   GOOD   |   FAIR   |   POOR   |     FEATURE
+___________________________________________________________________
 8. 8/FRACTION >3 IN
    (WT PCT):
 a) (0-40")                           <5               5-25          >25            LARGE STONES
 b) (40-60")                        <15            15-30         >30            AREA RECLAIM

 9. 8/COARSE
    FRAGMENTS (PCT):
 a) (0-40")                          <5                 5-25         >25              SMALL STONES
 b) (40-60")                       <25             25-50         >50              AREA RECLAIM

 8/Sum (100-% passing No. 10 sieve) and fraction >3 in.  Use   dominant condition for restrictive feature.

 Lines 8a and 9a are calculated together, and lines 8b and 9b are calculated together.

 Description of Calculation for lines 8a and 9a:
+_______________________________________________

 The values for % passing No. 10 sieve and fraction 3-10 inches given on the Soils-5 are examined.  These values are used in the calculations of weighted averages from 0-40 inches.

 % passing No. 10 sieve
+______________________

 The low value is examined for each layer within the given depths. The value used for each layer in the calculation depends on which of the following conditions is met first.

 If the low value is valid, then (100 - low value) is used.

 Otherwise an artificial value of 0 is used.

 Fraction 3-10 inches
+____________________

 The values are examined for each layer within the given depths and a high value is determined.  The high value used for each layer in the calculation depends on which of the following conditions is met first.

 If a single value of '99' is entered, then an artificial value of  100 is used.

 If a single value not equal to '99' is entered, then an artificial  value of 0 is used.

 Otherwise the high value is used.

 A separate weighted average is calculated for each surface layer for both % passing No. 10 sieve and fraction 3-10 inches.  For each surface layer, the two weighted averages are added together (call this SUM) and rated.

 To determine the dominant condition, a new weighted average from 0-40 inches is calculated for both % passing No. 10 sieve and fraction 3-10 inches.  The surface layer value used in each calculation is the maximum value over all surface layers.  If the weighted average for fraction 3-10 inches is >= the weighted average for % passing No. 10, then the restrictive term used is LARGE STONES.  Otherwise it is SMALL STONES.

           A SUM > 25 gets a POOR rating.
           A SUM > 5 and <= 25 gets a FAIR rating.
           A SUM <= 5 gets a GOOD rating.

 Description of Calculation for lines 8b and 9b:
+_______________________________________________

 This calculation is similar to that above, except we will assume that no surface layers are involved.

 A separate weighted average from 40-60 inches is calculated for both % passing No. 10 sieve and fraction 3-10 inches.  The two weighted averages are added together (call this SUM).

 If the weighted average for fraction 3-10 inches is >= the weighted average for % passing No. 10 sieve, then the following ratings apply:

           A SUM > 30 gets a POOR rating.
           A SUM > 15 and <= 30 gets a FAIR rating.
           A SUM <= 15 gets a GOOD rating.
 Otherwise the following ratings apply:
           A SUM > 50 gets a POOR rating.
           A SUM > 25 and <= 50 gets a FAIR rating.
           A SUM <= 25 gets a GOOD rating.
                     ---------------
 It is possible that Property No. 4, DEPTH TO BULK DENSITY, Property No. 8b, FRACTION >3 IN (40-60") and Property No. 9b, COARSE FRAGMENTS (40-60") may all have the same restrictive term, AREA RECLAIM.  At this point, a check must be made to ensure that this term will only appear in the final output at most once.

 If No. 4 is marked POOR, then No. 8b and No. 9b are cancelled out. Else if No. 8b is marked POOR, then No. 9b is cancelled out.  The same procedure is repeated for FAIR.

 ___________________________________________________________________
                       |             LIMITS             |RESTRICTIVE

 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________
 
 The values given on the Soils-5 for fraction > 10 inches are examined and a high value for each layer is determined.  The high value used in the calculation depends on which of the following conditions is met first.
 
 If a single value of '99' is entered, then an artificial value of 100 is used.

           A weighted average > 5 and <= 15 gets a MODERATE rating.

 Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.

evaldesc:
The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
  Where the soil property surface_frag_size is >=250cm and the sum of the corresponding soil property surface_frag_cover_percent is <=0.1%, the evaluation returns a value of 0 and TOO STONY is absolutely not a restrictive feature.  

  If the surface_frag_cover_percent is between 0.1% and 3%, the evaluation returns a value between 0 and 1 and TOO STONY is a moderately restrictive feature.  

  If the surface_frag_cover_percent is > 3%, the evaluation returns a value of 1 and TOO STONY is absolutely a severe restrictive feature.

This evaluation checks the values of greater than  3" (75mm) fraction for the surface horizon. 

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
 
  Where the total of the soil component horizon coarse fragment property > 75mm is greater than 75% the evaluation is absolutely true and "LARGE STONES" is a restrictive feature.
     AND
  Where the total of the soil component horizon coarse fragment property > 75mm is less than 25% the evaluation is absolutely false and "LARGE STONES" is not a restrictive feature.

Intent is  rocks > 75mm in diameter between 15 and 60% by volume in the surface layer.  Conversion to by weight is  approximately 25 to 75%.  Criteria was modified to reflect intent.  4/99 rdn.

Ames Description prior to  1996:

                                                            |                             LIMITS                                  |  RESTRICTIVE
     PROPERTY                               |  SLIGHT  |   MODERATE   |  SEVERE    |  FEATURE
 4. USDA TEXTURE                          ---          STV, BYV,           STX, BYX,    LARGE STONES
    MODIFIER (SURFACE                                  CB, FL                  CBX, FLX, 
    LAYER)                                                                                                CBV, FLV,
                                                                                                                     CNX, CRX
                                                                                                                      SHX, SYX
 Description of Calculation:

 The modifiers and textures given on the Soils-5 for each surface layer are examined.

 The surface layers are each rated separately using the following algorithm.

 If STX, BYX, CBX, FLX, CBV, FLV, CNX, CRX, SHX or SYX is listed as a modifier, then a SEVERE rating is given.

 If STV, BYV, CB or FL is listed as a modifier, then a MODERATE rating is given.

 Otherwise a SLIGHT rating is given.

 This property is rated SLIGHT if there is any SLIGHT surface layer rating, MODERATE if there is any MODERATE surface layer rating, and SEVERE if there is any SEVERE surface layer rating.  Phasing will be done using modifier terms (texture is used if no modifier is entered) if more than one rating is given.

evaldesc:
Moisture in clayey soils can cause them to be difficult to work.  Since the amount of time the soil is moist varies from place to place, the clayeyness does not always have the same impact on workability.  In udic areas, the likelihood of the soil being wet on a given day is much higher than in arid areas, and so the clayeyness is more limiting.  The rating is used to adjust the fuzzy number returned by the clay content property.

ustic		  0.5		somewhat limiting
udic		  0.8		somewhat limiting
perudic		  1.0		limiting
peraquic	  1.0		limiting
aquic		  1.0		limiting

This evaluation checks the soil's maximum Ksat to a depth of 90cm or restrictive feature and indexes the degree to which Ksat is limiting.  Where the soil property "KSAT MAXIMUM, 0-90CM OR FIRST RESTRICTION (TX)" is:

	=> 141.0 micrometers/second the soil is limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as the number 1.0.

evaldesc:
7/99 Modification:
This evaluation checks the filtering capacity of the soil.  The maximum high, low, and representative values for sat_hydraulic_conductivity are selected for each horizon between 24 to 72 inches and above any restrictive layer. 

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
  Where the soil horizon property sat_hydraulic_conductivity > 42 micrometers/second (6.0 inches/hr), the evaluaton is absolutely true and the restrictive feature is poor effluent filter field.
        AND
  Where the soil horizon property sat_hydraulic_conductivity <= 42 micrometers/second (6.0 inches/hour), the evaluation is absolutely false and the restrictive feature is not poor effluent filter field.

If no data is entered, then an artificial default value(s) is used.

In 1990 the evaluation depth was extended from a base of 40 inches to a base of 60 inches.

Ames Description Prior to 1996

                                              |                           LIMITS                              |  RESTRICTIVE
     PROPERTY                 |  SLIGHT  | MODERATE |  SEVERE  |  FEATURE
 7. PERMEABILITY          ---                 ---                  >6.0             POOR FILTER
    (IN/HR):    (24-40")            
 
 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________
   
 The values given on the Soils-5 for permeability are examined and a
 high value for each layer is determined.  The high value used for
 comparison depends on which of the following conditions is met
 first.
 
 If no data is entered, then an artificial value of 0 is used.
 
 If the entry is a single number or is of the form '<xx', then the
  single value entered is used.
 
 If the entry is of the form '>xx', then an artificial value of 100
  is used.
 
 Otherwise the high value is used.
 
 The layers within the given depths are examined.  If surface layers are included in these depths, each is rated separately.  Then each sublayer is rated to determine the worst sublayer rating.  The rating algorithm used on each layer is as follows:
 
           A value > 6.0 gets a SEVERE rating.
           A value <= 6.0 gets a SLIGHT rating.
 
 If surface layers are not involved, then this property is rated the
 same as the worst sublayer rating.
 
 If surface layers are involved, then the following applies.  If the
 worst sublayer rating is SEVERE, then this property is rated SEVERE
 and no phasing will be done, regardless of the surface layer
 ratings.
 
 If the worst sublayer rating is SLIGHT, then this property is rated
 SLIGHT if there is any SLIGHT surface layer rating, and it is rated
 SEVERE if there is any SEVERE surface layer rating.  Phasing will be
 done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.

This evaluation tests the depth to a restrictive layer where the following is true.

The crisp evaluation is depth to restrictive layer < 100cm (40 inches).

The weighted average of the component horizon silt + very fine sand content to a depth of 30cm (12"), indexes the degree to which silt is a contributing factor to the water erosion potential of the soil.  Where the soil property "SILT IN DEPTH 0-30CM (TX)" is:

	 => 70 the soil has high potential for water erosion and that potential is expressed as the number 1.0.
	 > 10 and < 70 the soil has a moderate potential for water erosion and that potential is expressed as a number between 0 and 1.0.
	 =< 10 the soil has a low potential for water erosion and that potential is expressed as the number 0.0.

This evaluation checks the soil's minimum Ksat to a depth of 30cm and indexes the degree to which surface Ksat contributes to the soil's water erosion potential.  Where the soil property "KSAT, MINIMUM IN DEPTH 0-30CM (TX)" is:

	  =< 0.42 micrometers/second the soil has high potential for water erosion and that potential is expressed as the number 1.0.
	 > 0.42 and < 42.0 micrometers/second the soil has a moderate potential for water erosion and that potential is expressed as a number between 0 and 1.0.
	 => 42.0 micrometers/second the soil has a low potential for water erosion and that potential is expressed as the number 0.0.

This evaluation checks the soil's weighted average organic matter content between a depth of 0 to 25cm or a restrictive layer and indexes the degree to which the soil's organic matter contributes to the soil's water erosion potential.  Where the soil property "ORGANIC MATTER WEIGHTED AVE. 0-30CM ABOVE RESTRICTION (TX)" is:

	 = 0 the soil has high potential for water erosion and that potential is expressed as the number 1.0.
	 > 0 and < 30 the soil has a moderate potential for water erosion and that potential is expressed as a number between 0 and 1.0.
	 => 30 the soil has a low potential for water erosion and that potential is expressed as the number 0.0.

This evaluation checks for a saturated or wet condition within a depth of 100cm (40 inches) of the soil surface.  The water moisture status is examined and those saturated or wet conditions are evalutated for depth.

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
  Where soil_moisture_status is saturated or wet and the depth to soil_moist_depth_to_top is less than 100 cm (40 inches) the evaluation is absolutely true and WETNESS is a restrictive feature.
   OR
  Where soil_moisture_status is saturated or wet and the depth to  soil_moist_depth_to_top  is greater than >= 180 cm (72 inches) the evaluation is absolutely false  and WETNESS is not a restrictive feature.
  
If the soil_moisture_status is not saturated or wet, then the property asumption is that soil_moist_depth_to_top is NULL and no water table is present.
propname: MA-DEPTH TO HIGH WATER TABLE MINIMUM

evalname: MA-Ksat Wt.Avg. Above a Rest. Layer for retention (0-40)
evaldesc:
This evaluation tests the Ksat weighted average above a restricting layer in the soil profile.

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
 
Where the Ksat weighted average passing is less than 4 micrometers/sec the evaluation is absolutely true and slow percolation is a restrictive feature.
     AND
Where the Ksat weighted average passing is greater than 40 micrometers/sec the evaluation is absolutely false and slow percolation is not a restrictive feature.
