evaldesc:
This evaluation tests for percent of sand in the thickest layer.

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
 
Where the result of the calculation sieveno200 -  sieveno4 is greater than 95 percent by weight the evaluation is absolutely true and "EXCESS FINES or GRAVEL" are not  restrictive features.
     AND
Where the result of the calculation sieveno200 -  sieveno4 is less than 50 percent by weight the evaluation is absolutely false and "EXCESS FINES or GRAVEL" are restrictive features.

Current version contains major  revisions to the Ames 1996 version.

Ames prior to 1996

1___________________________________________________________________
                                                                |                                         LIMITS            | RESTRICTIVE
+                                                              ________________________________
     PROPERTY                                   |    PROBABLE   |   IMPROBABLE   |  FEATURE
                                                               |     SOURCE        |     SOURCE              |
+___________________________________________________________________

 2. 12/UNIFIED                                 SW, SP, SW-SM,
                                                                SP-SM

                                                               13/GW, 13/GP,
                                                              13/GW-GM,
                                                              13/GP-GM

                                                                                                     14/GW, 14/GP,    SMALL
                                                                                                     14/GW-GM,        STONES
                                                                                                    14/GP-GM

                                                                                                    PT                            EXCESS  HUMUS

                                                                                                   ALL OTHER        EXCESS  FINES

 12/Evaluate the thickest layer between 10 and 60 inches and also the bottom layer.  Choose the best rating.  When rating is based on  bottom layer, verify thickness.
 13/% passing No. 4 sieve minus % passing No. 200 sieve > 25.
 14/% passing No. 4 sieve minus % passing No. 200 sieve < 25.



 According to footnote 12, calculations are done for both the thickest layer and the bottom layer.

 Description of Calculation for Thickest Layer:
+______________________________________________

 The layer with the most inches between 10 and 60 inches is determined.  This could be a surface layer or a sublayer.  The unified values given on the Soils-5 are examined for the appropriate layer(s).

 The layer(s) being examined are rated according to the following algorithm:

 If SW, SP, SW-SM, or SP-SM is listed as a unified entry, or if GW, GP, GW-GM or GP-GM is listed as a unified entry and footnote 13 applies (see following description of footnote 13), then a PROBABLE rating is given.

 Otherwise an IMPROBABLE rating is given.

 If the thickest layer is a sublayer, then this property is rated the same as this sublayer's rating.

 If the thickest layer is a surface layer, then this property is rated PROBABLE if there is any PROBABLE surface layer rating.  If there is none, then it is rated IMPROBABLE.

 Restrictive feature terms are assigned appropriately.



 Description of Calculation for Bottom Layer:
+____________________________________________

 If the bottom layer has no data, then this calculation is skipped and the ratings for the thickest layer are chosen.

 Otherwise, this calculation is the same as that for the thickest layer, except it is done for the bottom layer.  The bottom layer, like the thickest layer, may be a surface layer or a sublayer.

1

 Calculations for Footnotes 13 and 14
+____________________________________

 To do the calculations for these footnotes, the values given on the Soils-5 for % passing No. 4 sieve and % passing No. 200 sieve are examined.

 % passing No. 4 sieve
+_____________________

 Assign values to No_4_Lo and No_4_Hi.

 If no data is entered, then No_4_Lo = 100 and No_4_Hi = 100.

 If a single value, say x, is entered, then No_4_Lo = x and No_4_Hi = x.

 If the entry is a normal range, say x-y, then No_4_Lo = x and No_4_Hi = y.

 % passing No. 200 sieve
+_______________________

 Assign values to No_200_Lo and No_200_Hi.

 If no data is entered, then No_200_Lo = 0 and No_200_Hi = 0.

 If a single value, say x, is entered, then No_200_Lo = x and No_200_Hi = x.

 If the entry is a normal range, say x-y, then No_200_Lo = x and  No_200_Hi = y.


 Once these values have been assigned, the following calculations take place.

 No_4_Lo - No_200_Lo = Lo
 No_4_Hi - No_200_Hi = Hi

 maximum(Lo,Hi) = max

 If max > 25 then footnote 13 applies.
 If max <= 25 then footnote 14 applies.

For Property No. 2, UNIFIED, the best ratings must be chosen between those calculated for the thickest layer and the bottom layer.

 If both the thickest and bottom layers are rated PROBABLE, then the bottom layer is chosen.

 If the thickest layer is rated PROBABLE and the bottom layer is rated IMPROBABLE, then the thickest layer is chosen.

 If the bottom layer is rated PROBABLE and the thickest layer is rated IMPROBABLE, then the bottom layer is chosen.

 If neither the thickest or bottom layer is rated PROBABLE, then they must both be rated IMPROBABLE and the bottom layer is chosen.

 If the ratings for the thickest layer were chosen, then the calculations on the following page for Property No. 3, LAYER THICKNESS, are done.

 layer.  Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.

 The rating algorithm is as follows:

    A weighted average > 50 gets an IMPROBABLE rating.
    A weighted average <= 50 gets a PROBABLE rating.

 If a single value not equal to '99' is entered, then an artificial  value of 0 is used.

 Otherwise the high value is used.

 If surface layers are not included, then a weighted average from 10 to 60 inches is calculated and rated.  No phasing is done.

 If surface layers are included, then a separate weighted average from 10 to 60 inches is calculated and rated for each surface
 layer.  Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.

 The rating algorithm is as follows:

    A weighted average > 50 gets an IMPROBABLE rating.
    A weighted average <= 50 gets a PROBABLE rating.

Deeper soils have more ability to store water, air and nutrients. Soils with restrictive layers many times increase runoff because of low permeability or ksat, have less volume to sore nutrients, may have fractured bedrock that allows leaching into cave systems and ground water, and are less productive for removal of phosphorus by crops.

Fragipans do restrict downward movement of water and air and also restrict rooting depth. Since the slow permeability of fragipans greatly increases runoff, the restrictive layer has already provided a large reduction in rating value. We should consider not reducing the rating by depth to restrictive layer of fragipans because of the heavy reduction due to component runoff values. The runoff ratings provide a large portion of the ratings.

This evaluation check the seepage potential of the soil surface.  The high, low, and representative values for sat_hydraulic_conductivity are selected for the soil surface and evaluated.  Duff layers are ignored.

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
  Where the soil surface horizon property sat_hydraulic_conductivity > 14.0 micrometers/second (2 inches/hour) the evaluation is absolutely true and the restrictive feature is seepage.
        AND
  Where the soil surface horizon property sat_hydraulic_conductivity < 1.0 micrometers/second (0.20 inches/hour) the evaluation is absolutely false and the restrictive feature is not seepage.



Ames Description Prior to 1996:
 ___________________________________________________________________
                       |             LIMITS             |RESTRICTIVE
+                       ________________________________
     PROPERTY          |  SLIGHT  | MODERATE |  SEVERE  |  FEATURE
                       |          |          |          |
+___________________________________________________________________
 
 3. PERMEABILITY           <0.2       .2-.6      >.6     SEEPAGE
    (SURFACE LAYER, IN/HR)
 
 
 
 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________
 
 The values given on the Soils-5 for permeability are examined and a high value for each surface layer is determined.  The high value used for comparison depends on which of the following conditions is met first.
 
 If no data is entered, then an artificial value of 0 is used.
 
 If the entry is a single number or is of the form '<xx', then the single value entered is used.
 
 If the entry is of the form '>xx', then an artificial value of 100 is used.
 
 Otherwise the high value is used.
 
 Each surface layer is rated separately according to the following algorithm:
 
           A value > .6 gets a SEVERE rating.
           A value > .2 and <= .6 gets a MODERATE rating.
           A value <= .2 gets a SLIGHT rating.
 
 If there is a surface layer with a SEVERE rating, then this property rating, then this property is rated MODERATE.  If there is a surface layer with a SLIGHT rating, then this property is rated SLIGHT.  Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.

This evaluation checks the soil surface reaction (pH).  The surface horizon ph_1_1_water check and evaluated.  In this Vermont version, duff layers are ignored.  Also, the break between very limited and somewhat limited has been changed from 5.0 to 4.5. 

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
 
  Where the surface soil component horizon property ph_1_1_water is less than 4.5 the evaluation is absolutely true and "TOO ACID" is a restrictive feature.
     AND
  Where the surface soil component horizon property ph_1_1_water is greater than 6.5 the evaluation is absolutely false and "TOO ACID" is not a restrictive feature.



Ames Description prior to  1996:
 ___________________________________________________________________
                       |             LIMITS             |RESTRICTIVE
+                       ________________________________
     PROPERTY          |  SLIGHT  | MODERATE |  SEVERE  |  FEATURE
                       |          |          |          |
+___________________________________________________________________
 
 15. SOIL REACTION (pH)    >6.5      5.0-6.5    <5.0     TOO ACID
     (SURFACE LAYER)

This evaluation checks the soil surface reaction (pH).  The surface horizon ph_1_1_water check and evaluated. 
In this Vermont version, duff layers are ignored. 
Modified 7/98 to reflect the criteria in the Ag Waste Mang. Handbook

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
 
  Where the surface soil component horizon property ph_1_1_water is less than 3.5 the evaluation is absolutely true and "TOO ACID" is a restrictive feature.
     AND
  Where the surface soil component horizon property ph_1_1_water is greater than 6.5 the evaluation is absolutely false and "TOO ACID" is not a restrictive feature.

Ames Description prior to  1996:
 ___________________________________________________________________
                       |             LIMITS             |RESTRICTIVE
                       ________________________________
     PROPERTY          |  SLIGHT  | MODERATE |  SEVERE  |  FEATURE
                       |          |          |          |
+___________________________________________________________________
 
 15. SOIL REACTION (pH)    >6.0      5.0-6.0    <5.0     TOO ACID

 
 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________
 
 The values given on the Soils-5 for soil reaction are examined for each surface layer.  A low value is determined for each surface layer depending on which of the following conditions is met first.
 
 If the entry is of the form '<xx', then an artificial value of 0 is  used.
 
 If the entry is a normal range, then the low value is used.
 
 If the entry is a single number or is of the form '>xx', then the  single value entered is used.
 
 Otherwise an artificial value of 10 is used.
 
 The minimum value over all surface layers is determined.
 
      A minimum value < 5.0 gets a SEVERE rating.
      A minimum value >= 5.0 and < 6.0 gets a MODERATE rating.
      A minimum value >= 6.0 gets a SLIGHT rating.

 The values given on the Soils-5 for clay and CEC are examined and an

 Clay:
+_____
 
 If no data is entered, then the layer is skipped.

evaldesc:
This evaluation checks for coarse fragments between 3 and 10 inches in the bottom layer.  The rock_frag_3_to_10_in is checked and evaluated.

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
 
Where the result of the soil horizon property rock_frag_3_to_10_in is greater than 35 percent by weight the evaluation is absolutely true and "PERCENT COARSE FRAGMENTS" is a restrictive feature.
     AND
Where the result of the soil horizon property rock_frag_3_to_10_in is less than 0 percent by weight the evaluation is absolutely false and "PERCENT COARSE FRAGMENTS" is not a restrictive feature.

Current version contains major  revisions to the Ames 1996 version.

Ames Description prior to  1996:

1___________________________________________________________________
                                       |             LIMITS                                        |RESTRICTIVE
+                                    ________________________________
     PROPERTY          |    PROBABLE   |   IMPROBABLE   |  FEATURE
                                      |     SOURCE         |             SOURCE     |
+___________________________________________________________________

 4. 6/FRACTION >3            <50                         >50                          LARGE
    IN (WT PCT)                                                                                      STONES

 6/Thickest layer between 10 and 60 inches.



 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________

 NOTE:  THE CURRENT CALCULATION FOR THIS PROPERTY IS ACTUALLY A WEIGHTED AVERAGE FROM 10 TO 60 INCHES.

 The values given on the Soils-5 for fraction 3-10 inches are examined and a high value for each layer within 10 to 60 inches is
 determined.  The given depths may or may not include surface layers.   The high value used in the calculation depends on which of the following conditions is met first.

 If a single value of '99' is entered, then an artificial value of 100 is used.

 If a single value not equal to '99' is entered, then an artificial  value of 0 is used.

 Otherwise the high value is used.

 If surface layers are not included, then a weighted average from 10 to 60 inches is calculated and rated.  No phasing is done.

 If surface layers are included, then a separate weighted average from 10 to 60 inches is calculated and rated for each surface
 layer.  Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.

 The rating algorithm is as follows:

    A weighted average > 50 gets an IMPROBABLE rating.
    A weighted average <= 50 gets a PROBABLE rating.

 1___________________________________________________________________

                                                                                         ALL OTHER                    EXCESS  FINES

 12/Evaluate the thickest layer between 10 and 60 inches and also the  bottom layer.  Choose the best rating.  When rating is based on  bottom layer, verify thickness.
 15/100 minus % passing No. 4 sieve > 25.
 16/100 minus % passing No. 4 sieve < 25.



 According to footnote 12, calculations are done for both the thickest layer and the bottom layer.

 Description of Calculation for Thickest Layer:
+______________________________________________

 The layer with the most inches between 10 and 60 inches is determined.  This could be a surface layer or a sublayer.  The unified values given on the Soils-5 are examined for the appropriate layer(s).

 The layer(s) being examined are rated according to the following algorithm:

 If GW, GP, GW-GM, or GP-GM is listed as a unified entry, or if SW, SP, SW-SM or SP-SM is listed as a unified entry and footnote 15 applies (see following description of footnote 15), then a PROBABLE rating is given.

 Otherwise an IMPROBABLE rating is given.

 If the thickest layer is a sublayer, then this property is rated the same as this sublayer's rating.

 If the thickest layer is a surface layer, then this property is rated PROBABLE if there is any PROBABLE surface layer rating.  If there is none, then it is rated IMPROBABLE.

 Restrictive feature terms are assigned appropriately.



 Description of Calculation for Bottom Layer:
+____________________________________________

 If the bottom layer has no data, then this calculation is skipped and the ratings for the thickest layer are chosen.

 Otherwise, this calculation is the same as that for the thickest layer, except it is done for the bottom layer.  The bottom layer,
 like the thickest layer, may be a surface layer or a sublayer.

 Calculations for Footnotes 15 and 16
+____________________________________

 To do the calculations for these footnotes, the values given on the Soils-5 for % passing No. 4 sieve are examined.

 % passing No. 4 sieve
+_____________________

 Assign values to No_4_Lo and No_4_Hi.

 If no data is entered, then No_4_Lo = 0 and No_4_Hi = 0.

 If a single value, say x, is entered, then No_4_Lo = x and  No_4_Hi = x.

 If the entry is a normal range, say x-y, then No_4_Lo = x and  No_4_Hi = y.

 Once these values have been assigned, the following calculations take place.

 100 - No_4_Lo = Lo
 100 - No_4_Hi = Hi

 maximum(Lo,Hi) = max

 If max > 25 then footnote 15 applies.
 If max <= 25 then footnote 16 applies.

 For Property No. 2, UNIFIED, the best ratings must be chosen between those calculated for the thickest layer and the bottom layer.

 If both the thickest and bottom layers are rated PROBABLE, then the bottom layer is chosen.

 If the thickest layer is rated PROBABLE and the bottom layer is rated IMPROBABLE, then the thickest layer is chosen.

 If the bottom layer is rated PROBABLE and the thickest layer is rated IMPROBABLE, then the bottom layer is chosen.

 If neither the thickest or bottom layer is rated PROBABLE, then they must both be rated IMPROBABLE and the bottom layer is chosen.

 If the ratings for the thickest layer were chosen, then the calculations on the following page for Property No. 3, LAYER
 THICKNESS, are done.

evaldesc:
Edited-changed property script to one that actually evaluates to 60".  Do not use this property script in areas where a restrictive layer may be present. CMB

This evaluation check percolation capacity of the soil.  The high, low, and representative values for sat_hydraulic_conductivity are selected for each horizon to a depth of 60 inches. 

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
  Where the soil horizon property sat_hydraulic_conductivity <= 1.0 micrometers/second (0.20 inches/hour)the evaluation is absolutely true and the restrictive feature is slow percolation.
        AND
  Where the soil horizon property sat_hydraulic_conductivity => 4.0 micrometers/second (0.60 inches/hour) the evaluation is absolutely false and the restrictive feature is not slow percolation.

If no data is entered, thn an artificial default value(s) is used. 

Ames Description Prior to 1996:
 ___________________________________________________________________
                       |             LIMITS             |RESTRICTIVE
+                       ________________________________
     PROPERTY          |  SLIGHT  | MODERATE |  SEVERE  |  FEATURE
                       |          |          |          |
+___________________________________________________________________
 
 2a. PERMEABILITY        0.6-2.0     0.2-0.6     <0.2    PERCS
     (0-60", IN/HR)                                      SLOWLY
The values given on the Soils-5 for permeability are examined and a low value for each layer is determined.  The low value used for comparison depends on which of the following conditions is met first.  If no data is entered, then an artificial value of 100 is used.
 
If the entry is of the form '<xx', then an artificial value of 0 is used. Otherwise the low value is used.
The layers within the given depths are examined.  The surface layers are each rated separately.  The lowest value found from all the sublayers is rated.  The rating algorithm used is as follows:
 
A value < 0.2 gets a SEVERE rating.
A value >= 0.2 and < 0.6 gets a MODERATE rating.
A value >= 0.6 gets a SLIGHT rating.
 
If the sublayer rating is SEVERE, then this property is rated SEVERE and no phasing will be done, regardless of the surface layer ratings. If the sublayer rating is MODERATE, then this property is rated MODERATE if there is any SLIGHT or MODERATE surface layer rating, and it is rated SEVERE if there is any SEVERE surface layer rating. Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.
 
If the sublayer rating is SLIGHT, then this property is rated SLIGHT if there is any SLIGHT surface layer rating, MODERATE if there is any MODERATE surface layer rating, and SEVERE if there is any SEVERE surface layer rating. Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
 
 Where the soil component property restriction_kind = "fragipan", "duripan", "petrocalcic", "ortstein",  or "petrogypsic" and the restriction_depth_to_top is less then 50 cm (20 inches) then the evaluation is absolutely true and depth to "CEMENTED PAN" is a restrictive feature.
     AND
  Where the soil component property restriction_kind = "fragipan", "duripan", "petrocalcic", "ortstein",  or "petrogypsic" and the restriction_depth_to_top is greater then 100 cm (40 inches) then the evaluation is absolutely false and depth to "CEMENTED PAN" is not a restrictive feature.


Ames Description prior to  1996:
1___________________________________________________________________

+                       ________________________________
     PROPERTY          |  SLIGHT  | MODERATE |  SEVERE  |  FEATURE
                       |          |          |          |
+___________________________________________________________________

 3. DEPTH TO CEMENTED                                    CEMENTED
    PAN (IN):                                            PAN
     THIN                   >40       20-40       <20
 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________

 The cemented pan hardness and the low value in the range of values given on the Soils-5 for depth to cemented pan are examined.  The value used for comparison depends on which of the following conditions is  met first.

 If the low value is valid, then the low value is used.

 Otherwise an artificial value of 100 is used.

 If the cemented pan hardness equals (thin), then the following
 ratings apply:

           A value < 20 gets a SEVERE rating.
           A value >= 20 and < 40 gets a MODERATE rating.
           A value >= 40 gets a SLIGHT rating.
propname: DEPTH TO CEMENTED PAN THIN, BELOW O HORIZON

evalname: Shrink-Swell Weighted Average 25-100cm or Above Bedrock
evaldesc:
This evaluation checks for soil shrink-swell potential for the thickest layer within 0 to 100cm (40 inches) or the soil surface to bedrock.  The linear_extensibility_percent for the thickest layer is examined and evalutated for depth conditions.

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
  Where linear_extensibility_percent of the thickest layer is greater than 6 the evaluation is absolutely true.
   OR
  Where linear_extensibility_percent of the thickest layer is less than 3 the evaluation is absolutely false.

If the linear_extensibility_percent of the thickest layer is NULL then LE is assumed to be less than 3.

Ames Description Prior to 1996:
                                                      |                            LIMITS                                       |  RESTRICTIVE
     PROPERTY                         |  SLIGHT  | MODERATE |  SEVERE            |  FEATURE
 
 5. 9/SHRINK-SWELL         LOW             MODERATE      HIGH,                  SHRINK-
                                                                                                              VERY HIGH       SWELL
 
 9/Thickest layer between 10 and 40 inches.
 
 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________
 
 The layer with the most inches between 10 and 40 inches is determined.  This could be a surface layer or a sublayer.  The shrink-swell values given on the Soils-5 are examined for the appropriate layer(s).
 
 The layer(s) being examined are rated according to the following algorithm:
 
 If the shrink-swell value equals '1' (HIGH) or '5' (VERY HIGH), then a SEVERE rating is given.  If the shrink-swell value equals '3' (MODERATE), then a MODERATE rating is given. Otherwise a SLIGHT rating is given.
 
 If the thickest layer is a sublayer, then this property is rated the same as this sublayer's rating.
 
 If the thickest layer is a surface layer, then this property is rated SLIGHT if there is any SLIGHT surface layer rating, MODERATE if there is any MODERATE surface layer rating, and SEVERE if there is any SEVERE surface layer rating.  Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.
propname: LEP WTD_AVG 25-100cm OR ABOVE RESTRICTION, BELOW O HORIZON

evaldesc:
This evaluation checks for a saturated or wet condition within a depth of 75 cm (2.5 feet) of the soil surface.  The water moisture status for all layers are examined and those saturated or wet layers are evalutated for depth.

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
  Where soil_moisture_status is wet and the depth to soil_moist_depth_to_top is less than 45 cm (1.5 feet) the evaluation is absolutely true and WETNESS is a restrictive feature.
   OR
  Where soil_moisture_status is wet and the depth to  soil_moist_depth_to_top  is greater than 75 cm (2.5 feet) the evaluation is absolutely false  and WETNESS is not a restrictive feature.

If the soil_moisture_status is not wet or null, then the property asumption is that soil_moist_depth_to_top is NULL and no water table is present.

Ames Description Prior to 1996:
 
                                                        |                            LIMITS                             |  RESTRICTIVE
     PROPERTY                           |  SLIGHT  | MODERATE |  SEVERE  |  FEATURE
 4. WATER TABLE (FT)             >2.5               1.5-2.5                  <1.5        WETNESS
  
 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________
 
The low value in the range of values given on the Soils-5 for depth to high water table is examined.  If a '+' occurs in this field, then there is ponding and a SEVERE rating is given.  Otherwise the value used for comparison depends on which of the following conditions is met first.
 
If no data is entered, then an artificial value of 99.9 is used.
 
Otherwise the low value is used.
 
           A value < 1.5 gets a SEVERE rating.
           A value >= 1.5 and < 2.5 gets a MODERATE rating.
           A value >= 2.5 gets a SLIGHT rating.
propname: HIGH WATER TABLE DEPTH MINIMUM, BELOW O HORIZON

This evaluation checks the soil's bulk density within a depth of 0 to 90cm and indexes the degree to which bulk density is limiting.  Where the soil property "BULK DENSITY MAXIMUM IN DEPTH 0-90cm (TX)" is:
	 => 1.8 the soil is limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as the number 1.0.
  	  > 1.5 and < 1.8 the soil is somewhat limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as a number between 0 and 1.0.
	  < 1.5 the soil is not limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as the number 0.

The intent of this evaluation is to array soils on their available water holding capacity.  The lowest score a soil can receive is a 0.1.  Soils having 2 inches of available water or less will get a .1.  The highest score is a 1 which a soil would need 37 cm of available water to receive.    It is thought that very few soils can get a score of 1, thus, the upper scores will have some spread such that differences can be seen.

- 11/23/2020 - This evaluation used property "NSSC Data":"AWC 0-150cm OR EC >= 8.01" which was found to be utilizing EC>=16. It has been restored to to EC>=8 and a new property created for EC>=16 and the evaluation renamed. If an EC of 8 is required, use property "NSSC Data":"AWC 0-150cm OR EC >= 8.01". -MAA

 Description of Calculation for Thickest Layer:
+______________________________________________

 The layer with the most inches between 10 and 60 inches is determined.  This could be a surface layer or a sublayer.  The unified values given on the Soils-5 are examined for the appropriate layer(s).

evalname: NCCPI_B - Rock Outcrop Present in Map Unit
evaldesc:
This evaluation is looking at the map unit name where it has any portion of the name being Rock outcrop, rocky or very rocky.

The evaluation is an arbitrary linear line that evaluates the map unit name where anything that had Rock outcrop in the name is out of the class and returns a value of 1. Any map unit with "rocky" in the name is a partial member of the class and is given a fuzzy value of 0.3. Any map unit with "very rocky" in the name is also a parital member of the class and is given a fuzzy value of 0.7. Any map unit that does not include these words in their name is considered a member of the class and returns a value of 0.

This is used with PA septic systems for ruling out any components that would have rock outcrops or rocky phases and be unsuitable for septic systems.

evalname: NM - Dust from Gypsum Content 5 to 15 Percent
evaldesc:
This evaluation checks gypsum content.

A soil can be a complete or partial member of the set of soils that are high in gypsum content and gypsum is the set's restrictive feature.  If the gypsum content exceeds 15 percent, then the soil is a complete member of the set.  If the gypsum content slope is greater than 2 percent and less than 15 percent then the soil is a partial member of the set.  A soil that has a gypsum content less than 2 percent is not a member of the set.

evalname: Dust from Silt and Clay Content 20 to 70 Percent Sand, Suit.
evaldesc:
This evaluation checks slope.

A soil can be a complete or partial member of the set of soils that are too steep and SLOPE is the set's restrictive feature.  If the slope is greater than 15 percent, then the soil is a complete member of the set.  If slope is greater than 8 percent and less than 15 percent then the soil is a partial member of the set.  A soil that has slope less than 8 percent is not a member of the set.
propname: WTD_AVG SAND CONTENT 0-50cm OR ABOVE RESTRICTION, NO O

evalname: Dust from Silt and Clay Content 20 to 70 Percent Sand
evaldesc:
This evaluation checks silt and clay content.

A soil can be a complete or partial member of the set of soils that are dusty due to their silt and clay content and SAND CONTENT is the set's restrictive feature.  If the sand content is less than 20 percent, then the soil is a complete member of the set of potentially dusty soils.  If the sand content is between 20 and 70 percent then the soil is a partial member of the set.  A soil that has sand content grteater than 70 percent is not a member of the set.
propname: WTD_AVG SAND CONTENT 0-50cm OR ABOVE RESTRICTION, NO O

evaldesc:
This evaluation checks a dryness index.

A soil can be a complete or partial member of the set of soils that are hot and/or too dry. and DRYNESS INDEX is the set's restrictive feature.  If the dryness index is greater than 3, then the soil is a complete member of the set of soils limited by dryness and the soil is dry.  If dryness index is less than 3 but greater than 0.5, the soil is a partial member of the set.  A soil that has dryness index is less than 0.5 is not a member of the set of soils limited by dryness.

This evaluation checks a dryness index.

A soil can be a complete, partial, or non member of the set of soils that are suitable for a use because they are moist.  If the dryness index is greater than 8 , then the soil is a nonmember of the set of moist soils.  If dryness index is less than 8 but greater than 1, the soil is a partial member of the set of moist soils.  A soil that has dryness index is less than 1 is a complete member of the set of moist soils.

This evaluation is limited so that the fuzzy number can not be lower than 0.5.

evalname: WV Surface stones, poultry disposal compost (pdc)
evaldesc:

The fuzzy space is defined for rock fragments > 250mm and at percent coverages consistent with stony and bouldery classes.

If surface stone cover is greater than 15%, then the rule is absolutely true and surface stones are absolutely a restrictive feature
AND
If surface stones are <0.1%, then the rule is absolutely false and surface stones are absolutely not a restrictive feature.

This evaluation checks the soil's aluminium saturation to a depth of 0 to 10cm or a restrictive layer and indexes the degree to which the soil's aluminium saturation is contributes to the soil's plant growth potential.  Where the soil property "ALUMINIUM SATURATION HORIZON DEPTH <10cm" is:

AL SATURATION
		

Some agricultural crops suffer from aluminum toxicity when the Al saturation is only 10%. Aluminum interferes with the photosynthetic cycle by complexing with phosphate, so with high soluble aluminum the plant is starved for phosphate. Al-toxicity also stunts root growth thereby limiting the amount of soil the plant can exploit for nutrients. Stunted roots can also limit water uptake and can cause plants to wilt with only a few days without water. Some plants (e.g. cassava) have high tolerance to high levels of soluble aluminum. High soluble Al and acidity may adversely affect soil health by inhibiting beneficial organisms. When liming soils with high soluble aluminum the rule of thumb is to add 1.5 tons of CaCO3 per acre for every milliequivalents of soluble aluminum. The pH only needs to be raised to about 5.5 to eliminate the harmful effects of high soluble aluminum. (Source: Dr. Robert Gavenda, PhD; PowerPoint presentation on soil degradation)

About one-third of the tropics (1.5 billion hectares) has sufficiently strong soil acidity for soluble aluminum to be toxic to most crop species. This constraint is defined as having more than 60% Al saturation in some part of the top 50 cm of soil. A soil pH value of less than 5.5 usually indicates this problem (Evans and Kamprath, 1970). Aluminum toxicity is most prevalent in the humid tropics and acid savannas. This constraint is found mainly in soils classified as oxisols, ultisols and closely related inceptisols and is correlated with low nutrient capital reserves. Aluminum toxicity is usually the overwhelming constraint in these soils and must be tackled first, either by modern lime application practices, by using Al-tolerant plant species or by breeding for Al-tolerant varieties (Sanchez and Salinas, 1981). It is relevant to note that aluminum toxicity is rare in most smallholder farming areas of subhumid and semiarid Africa, except for parts of Rwanda, Burundi, Northern Zambia, Southern Congo, KwaZulu Natal Province in South Africa and in some sandy soils of Zimbabwe (Sanchez et al., 1997). Two-thirds of the tropics does not have enough aluminum saturation to worry about. Aluminum toxicity can become a positive soil quality attribute when using Al-tolerant plants in P-deficient soils. The low pH facilitates the dissolution of phosphate rocks, letting, in effect, the H+ ions in the soil do what a superphosphate factory doestreating rock phosphates with acids (Sanchez and Salinas, 1981). High aluminum saturation, as defined by this modifier, is also a positive attribute for rubber and tea production (Smith, 1989).  (Source: Fertility capability soil classification: a tool to help assess soil quality in the tropics by Pedro A. Sancheza,, Cheryl A. Palma, and Stanley W. Buol)

Station Special Circular 53. as reported in Bohn, McNeal, and O'Connor.1981.Soil Chemistry. to construct the evaluation curve. This evaluation is crisp and checks for UNIFIED equal to  "PT".

Where unified_soil_classification equals or "PT" the evaluation is absolutely true.
    AND
Where unified_soil_classification does not equal or "PT" the evaluation is absolutely false.

 Ames prior to 1996
                                                              |             LIMITS             |RESTRICTIVE
     PROPERTY                                 |  SLIGHT  | MODERATE |  SEVERE  |  FEATURE
  7. UNIFIED (ANY DEPTH)              --             OL, OH                  PT             EXCESS HUMUS
  
 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________
 
 The unified values given on the Soils-5 are examined for each layer.
 
 The surface layers are each rated separately.  Then each sublayer is rated to determine the worst sublayer rating.  The rating algorithm used on each layer is as follows:
 
 If PT is listed as a unified entry, then a SEVERE rating is given. If OL or OH is listed as a unified entry, then a MODERATE rating is      given. Otherwise a SLIGHT rating is given.
 
 If the worst sublayer rating is SEVERE, then this property is rated SEVERE and no phasing will be done, regardless of the surface layer ratings.
 
 If the worst sublayer rating is MODERATE, then this property is rated MODERATE if there is any SLIGHT or MODERATE surface layer rating, and it is rated SEVERE if there is any SEVERE surface layer rating. Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.

evaldesc:

If a saturated condition occurs within 60 cm (2 feet) of the soil surface than wetness is a limitation.

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
  Where soil_moisture_status is wet and the depth to soil_moist_depth_to_top is less than 60 cm (2 feet) the evaluation is absolutely true.

evalname: STS - Soil Slippage Potential, Revised - TEST (OH)
evaldesc:
The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
  Soil Slippage Potential is orderer code.  A soil may be a non-member, partial member, or complete member of the set of soils that have slippage potential.  Very few soils are non-members of this set.  The fuzzy space is defined as:
  
  
  Soil slippage potential code 0-1	Not limiting
  Soil slippage potential code 2-4	Somewhat limiting
  Soil slippage potential code 5	Very limiting
  

  Null soil slippage is placed in the not limiting class.


As of 03-21-2019, Ohio doesn't have any components with Soil Slip Potential of moderately low (code 2) or moderately high (code 4).  This rule will give a rating for soils with Soil Slip Potential in these 2 classes; might want to check to see if the output is as expected.

evaldesc:
This evaluation checks the filtering capacity of the soil.  The minimum high, low, and representative values for  sat_hydraulic_conductivity are selected to a depth of 20 inches. 

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
  Where the soil horizon property sat_hydraulic_conductivity >= 42 micrometers/second (6.0 inches/hr), the evaluaton is absolutely true and the restrictive feature is poor effulent filter field.
        AND
  Where the soil horizon property sat_hydraulic_conductivity <= 14 micrometers/second (2.0 inches/hour), the evaluation is absolutely false and the restrictive feature is not poor effulent filter field.

If no data is entered, then an artificial default value(s) is used.

Ames Description Prior to 1996
 ___________________________________________________________________
                       |             LIMITS             |RESTRICTIVE
+                       ________________________________
     PROPERTY          |  SLIGHT  | MODERATE |  SEVERE  |  FEATURE
                       |          |          |          |
+___________________________________________________________________
 
 2.  PERMEABILITY           ---      2.0-6.0     >6.0    POOR FILTER
     (0-60", IN/HR)
  
 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________
 
The values given on the Soils-5 for permeability are examined and a low value for each layer is determined.  The low value used for comparison depends on which of the following conditions is met first. If no data is entered, then an artificial value of 100 is used.  If the entry is of the form '<xx', then an artificial value of 0 is used.  Otherwise the low value is used.
 
The layers within the given depths are examined.  The surface layers are each rated separately.  The lowest value found from all the sublayers is rated.  The rating algorithm used is as follows:
 
   A value >= 6.0 gets a SEVERE rating.
   A value >= 2.0 and < 6.0 gets a MODERATE rating.
 
If the sublayer rating is SEVERE, then this property is rated SEVERE and no phasing will be done, regardless of the surface layer ratings.
 
If the sublayer rating is MODERATE, then this property is rated MODERATE if there is any SLIGHT or MODERATE surface layer rating, and it is rated SEVERE if there is any SEVERE surface layer rating.  Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.
propname: MDA KSAT HIGHEST MINIMUM, 0-50CM OR FIRST RESTRICTION

This evaluation check percolation capacity of the soil.  The high, low, and representative values for sat_hydraulic_conductivity are selected for each horizon to a depth of 20 inches. 

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
  Where the soil horizon property sat_hydraulic_conductivity <= 1.0 micrometers/second (0.20 inches/hour)the evaluation is absolutely true and the restrictive feature is slow percolation.
        AND
  Where the soil horizon property sat_hydraulic_conductivity => 4.0 micrometers/second (0.60 inches/hour) the evaluation is absolutely false and the restrictive feature is not slow percolation.

If no data is entered, thn an artificial default value(s) is used. 

Ames Description Prior to 1996:
 ___________________________________________________________________
                       |             LIMITS             |RESTRICTIVE
+                       ________________________________
     PROPERTY          |  SLIGHT  | MODERATE |  SEVERE  |  FEATURE
                       |          |          |          |
+___________________________________________________________________
 
 2a. PERMEABILITY        0.6-2.0     0.2-0.6     <0.2    PERCS
     (0-60", IN/HR)                                      SLOWLY
The values given on the Soils-5 for permeability are examined and a low value for each layer is determined.  The low value used for comparison depends on which of the following conditions is met first.  If no data is entered, then an artificial value of 100 is used.
 
If the entry is of the form '<xx', then an artificial value of 0 is used. Otherwise the low value is used.
The layers within the given depths are examined.  The surface layers are each rated separately.  The lowest value found from all the sublayers is rated.  The rating algorithm used is as follows:
 
A value < 0.2 gets a SEVERE rating.
A value >= 0.2 and < 0.6 gets a MODERATE rating.
A value >= 0.6 gets a SLIGHT rating.
 
If the sublayer rating is SEVERE, then this property is rated SEVERE and no phasing will be done, regardless of the surface layer ratings. If the sublayer rating is MODERATE, then this property is rated MODERATE if there is any SLIGHT or MODERATE surface layer rating, and it is rated SEVERE if there is any SEVERE surface layer rating. Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.
 
If the sublayer rating is SLIGHT, then this property is rated SLIGHT if there is any SLIGHT surface layer rating, MODERATE if there is any MODERATE surface layer rating, and SEVERE if there is any SEVERE surface layer rating. Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.

 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________
 
 If not disregarded, the bottom-most layer with a valid permeability entry is found.  This could be a surface layer or a sublayer.  For example, if there are no sublayers, or all the sublayers are missing permeability entries, then the surface layers will be examined. Otherwise, just the bottom single sublayer will be examined.
 
 The values given on the Soils-5 for permeability are examined and a high value determined for the appropriate layer(s).  The high value used for comparison depends on which of the following conditions is
 met first.

evalname: WV AASHTO Group Index Thickest Layer, 0-41cm (pdc)
evaldesc:
This evaluation checks aashto_group_index.  The component data are check for aashto_group_index index number.

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
  Where the soil component property aashto_group_index is greater than 16 then the evaluation is absolutely true and LOW STRENGTH is a restrictive feature.
     AND
  Where the soil component property aashto_group_index is less then 5 then the evaluation is absolutely false and LOW STRENGTH is not a restrictive feature.


Ames Description prior to  1996:
____________________________________________________________________
                                                             |             LIMITS                                              |RESTRICTIVE
+                                                         ________________________________
     PROPERTY                              |  SLIGHT  | MODERATE |  SEVERE     |  FEATURE
 +___________________________________________________________________
 
 6. 5/, 9/, 10/AASHTO                     <5                   4-16                        >16               LOW  STRENGTH
    GROUP INDEX NUMBER                                   
    
 5/If in Kaolinitic family, rate one class better if experience confirms.
 9/Thickest layer between 10 and 40 inches.
 10/GIN=(F-35)[.2+.005(LL-40)]+.01(F-15)(PI-10) where F=% passing No. 200 sieve.  If F<=35 and PI>=11, use only part 2 of equation.  Use median values.
 
 
 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________
 
 The layer with the most inches between 0 and 16 inches is determined.  This could be a surface layer or a sublayer.  The GIN is calculated for the appropriate layer(s) according to the given algorithm.
 
 To calculate the GIN, median values are needed for the following: percent passing No. 200 sieve (F), liquid limit (LL), and plasticity index (PI).  A median is calculated by adding the low and high values, then dividing by 2, unless special conditions exist.  The median calculation is given below for each of these three variables.
 
 Percent passing No. 200 sieve:
+______________________________
 
 If no valid data is entered, then an artificial value of 0 is used as the median.
 
 If a single value is entered, then this value is used as the median.
 
 Otherwise the median is calculated using the low and high values.
 

 
 Liquid limit:
+_____________
 
 If the entry is of the form '<xxx', then a median is calculated using 0 and xxx. 
 If the entry is of the form '>xxx', then a median is calculated using xxx and 100.
  If no valid data is entered, then an artificial value of 0 is used as the median. 
 If a single value is entered, then this value is used as the median. 
 Otherwise the median is calculated using the low and high values.
 
 Plasticity index:
+_________________
 
 If the entry is of the form '<xxx', then a median is calculated using 0 and xxx. 
 If the entry is of the form '>xxx', then a median is calculated using xxx and 100. 
 If the entry is of the form 'NP', then an artificial value of 0 is used as the median. 
 
 If the entry is of the form 'NP-xxx', then a median is calculated using 0 and xxx. 
 If no valid data is entered, then an artificial value of 0 is used as the median. 
 If a single value is entered, then this value is used as the median. 
 Otherwise the median is calculated using the low and high values. 
 After the GIN is calculated, the layer(s) being examined are rated according to the following algorithm: 
    If GIN > 16, then a SEVERE rating is given.
    If GIN > 5 and <= 16, then a MODERATE rating is given.
    If GIN <= 5, then a SLIGHT rating is given.
 
 If the thickest layer is a sublayer, then this property is rated the same as this sublayer's rating.  If mineralogy on the Soils-5 equals '28' (Kaolinitic), then a MODERATE rating is upgraded to SLIGHT, and a SEVERE rating is upgraded to MODERATE.
 
 If the thickest layer is a surface layer, then this property is rated SLIGHT if there is any SLIGHT surface layer rating, MODERATE if there is any MODERATE surface layer rating, and SEVERE if there is any SEVERE surface layer rating.  If mineralogy on the Soils-5 equals '28' (Kaolinitic), then a MODERATE rating is upgraded to SLIGHT, and a SEVERE rating is upgraded to MODERATE.  Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.

This evaluation checks the soil's maximum percent gypsum within a depth of 0 to 50cm and indexes the degree to which gypsum is limiting.  Where the soil property "GYPSUM MAXIMUM 0-50CM OR FIRST RESTRICTION (TX)" is:

	 => 40% the soil is limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as the number 1.0.

	 =< 1% the soil is not limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as the number 0.

This evaluation looks for content of rock fragments within 122cm (48 inches) that occupy 50 to 90 percent of the soil volume. The reprentative value, low and high values are returned from the Property script WV - FRAGMENTS 2mm-75mm MAXIMUM IN DEPTH <122cm.

This is a sigmoid curve where rock fragment content greater than 90% is rated as 1, meaning that this condition severely limits septic system operation. Rock fragment contents less than 50% are absolutely in the class and have no limitation for septic systems and are rated as 0. The range from 50 to 90 percent are given a fuzzy rating between 0 and 1.

evalname: NY-Bulk Density, Bottom or Last Layer Above Rest. Feature
evaldesc:
This evaluation tests the bulk density of the last layer in the soil or the last layer above a restricting layer.

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
 
Where the bulk density is more than 1.8 the evaluation is absolutely true and dense layer is a restrictive feature.
     AND
Where the bulk density is less than 1.63 the evaluation is absolutely false and dense layer is not a restrictive feature.
propname: NY-BULK DENSITY OF BOTTOM LAYER ABOVE RESTRICTIVE LAYER

evaldesc:
This evaluation tests the depth to a restrictive layer where the following is true.

The crisp evaluation is depth to restrictive layer < 100cm (40 inches).

This evaluation checks for a saturated or wet condition within a depth of 100cm (40 inches) of the soil surface.  The water moisture status is examined and those saturated or wet conditions are evalutated for depth.

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
  Where soil_moisture_status is saturated or wet and the depth to soil_moist_depth_to_top is less than 100 cm (40 inches) the evaluation is absolutely true and WETNESS is a restrictive feature.
   OR
  Where soil_moisture_status is saturated or wet and the depth to  soil_moist_depth_to_top  is greater than >= 180 cm (72 inches) the evaluation is absolutely false  and WETNESS is not a restrictive feature.
  
If the soil_moisture_status is not saturated or wet, then the property asumption is that soil_moist_depth_to_top is NULL and no water table is present.
propname: NY-DEPTH TO HIGH WATER TABLE MINIMUM

This evaluation looks for content of rock fragments within 107cm (42 inches) that occupy 50 to 90 percent of the soil volume. The reprentative value, low and high values are returned from the Property script WV - FRAGMENTS 2mm-75mm MAXIMUM IN DEPTH <107cm.

This is a sigmoid curve where rock fragment content greater than 90% is rated as 1, meaning that this condition severely limits septic system operation. Rock fragment contents less than 50% are absolutely in the class and have no limitation for septic systems and are rated as 0. The range from 50 to 90 percent are given a fuzzy rating between 0 and 1.

This evaluation looks for content of rock fragments within 61cm (24 inches) that occupy 50 to 90 percent of the soil volume. The reprentative value, low and high values are returned from the Property script WV - FRAGMENTS 2mm-75mm MAXIMUM IN DEPTH <61cm.

This is a sigmoid curve where rock fragment content greater than 90% is rated as 1, meaning that this condition severely limits septic system operation. Rock fragment contents less than 50% are absolutely in the class and have no limitation for septic systems and are rated as 0. The range from 50 to 90 percent are given a fuzzy rating between 0 and 1.

This evaluation rates the top of the fragipan as a restriction to the proper functioning of a septic system. This is a crisp evaluation where the threshold depth to the top of a fragipan is 122cm (48 inches). When the top of the fraipan is less than 122cm then it is rated as a 1 (the most limiting). All depths below 122cm are rated as 0 which are not limiting.

This evaluation rates the top of the fragipan as a restriction to the proper functioning of a septic system. This is a sigmoid curve where the threshold depth to the top of a fragipan is 91 to 107cm (36-42 inches). When the top of the fraipan is less than 91cm then it is rated as a 1 (the most limiting). When the top of the fraipan is deeper than 107cm then it is rated as a 0 (the least limiting). A fuzzy rating is given between the depths of 91 and 107cm.

All depths below 61cm are rated as 0 which are not limiting.

This evaluation rates the top of the fragipan as a restriction to the proper functioning of a septic system. The intent of this evaluation is to array soils on their available water holding capacity.  The lowest score a soil can receive is a 0.1. It is thought that very few soils can get a score of 1, thus, the upper scores will have some spread such that differences can be seen.

evalname: Ground Water Within 152 cm of the Surface (MN)
evaldesc:
This evaluation checks for a saturated or wet condition within a depth of 152cm of the soil surface.  The water moisture status for all layers are examined and those saturated or wet layers are evalutated for depth.

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
  Where soil_moisture_status is wet and the depth to soil_moist_depth_to_top is less than or equal to 152cm the evaluation is absolutely true (1).
  
  Where soil_moisture_status is wet and the depth to soil_moist_depth_to_top is greater than >= 152cm the evaluation is absolutely false (0).

If the soil_moisture_status is not wet or null, then the property asumption is that soil_moist_depth_to_top is NULL and no water table is present.
propname: DEPTH TO HIGH H2O TABLE APPARENT MINIMUM

evaldesc:

Where unified_soil_classification equals "OL", "OH", or "PT" the evaluation is absolutely true (1) and EXCESS HUMUS is a restrictive feature.
    AND
Where unified_soil_classification does not equal "OL", "OH", or "PT" the evaluation is absolutely false (0) and EXCESS HUMUS is not a restrictive feature.

evaldesc:
This evaluation checks for a saturated or wet condition within a depth of 180 cm (6 feet) of the soil surface.  The water moisture status for all layers are examined and those saturated or wet layers are evalutated for depth.

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
  Where soil_moisture_status is wet and the depth to soil_moist_depth_to_top is less than 120 cm (4 feet) the evaluation is absolutely true.
   OR
  Where soil_moisture_status is wet and the depth to  soil_moist_depth_to_top  is greater than 180 cm (6 feet) the evaluation is absolutely false.

If the soil_moisture_status is not wet or null, then the property asumption is that soil_moist_depth_to_top is NULL and no water table is present.

Ames Description Prior to 1996:

 ___________________________________________________________________
                       |             LIMITS             |RESTRICTIVE
+                       ________________________________
     PROPERTY          |  SLIGHT  | MODERATE |  SEVERE  |  FEATURE
                       |          |          |          |
+___________________________________________________________________
 
 3b:  WATER TABLE (FT)       >6         4-6       <4      WETNESS
 
The low value in the range of values given on the Soils-5 for depth to high water table is examined.  The value used for comparison depends on which of the following conditions are met first.
 
 If no data is entered, then an artificial value of 99.9 is used.
 
 Otherwise the low value is used.
 
           A value < 4 gets a SEVERE rating.
           A value >= 4 and < 6 gets a MODERATE rating.

evalname: Copy of SIC kg/m2 2 meter logarithmic
evaldesc:
Evaluates SIC on a logarithmic basis to a depth of two meter or to the occurrence of bedrock or other certain types of restrictive layers. 

IMPORTANT: This rule is not designed nor intended to be used in a regulatory manner. It was designed for educational and broad management purposes.

SBSouthard 3/2009

1. Soil inorganic carbon result is in kg/m2 to the depth of the soil.  Conversion to pounds/acre: (kg/m) X (2.2 lbs/kg) X (4047 m2/acre); so, kg/m X 8903 = pounds SIC/acre. Likewise, kg/m2 * 4.4515 = tons/acre.

2. This rule evaluates to 2 meter depth or to representative top depth of any bedrock kind, any petro horizon and any duripan. Other restrictions were not coded into the depth to restriction subproperty used in the main interpretation property script because the concern is not rooting depth restrictions but total amount of SIC stored in soils on a volumetric basis. It was decided to include sequestered soil inorganic carbon that may exist below a strongly contrasted particle size. 

3. The calculation is reported on a volumetric whole soil basis, corrected for representative rock fragments in database, the representative amount of soil passing the #10 sieve, rock fragment particle density, and the representative 1/3 bar density of the soil. The soil inorganic carbon is converted from horizon soil inorganic matter content stored as a weight percent of the < 2mm fraction of the soil and recalculated on a whole soil basis. 

4. The NPS SIC class rule was designed using an arbitrary linear curve in the associated evaluation. The curve was designed so that the "fuzzy value" multiplied by 1000 gives you that actual amount SIC calculated for the component in the NASIS data.

Data issues:

1. NULL 1/3 bulk density may exist for mineral horizons and this calculation will assign a bulk density value of 0.2 because in most cases NULL 1/3 bulk density in the data occurs with O horizons. In these cases the amount of SIC will be underestimated.

2. Particle densities vary over the country but 2.65 was used universally. More complex default queries could be written using parent material. It is not apparent if map results with broad SOC classes would reflect the extra effort to refine particle densities. This will result in either overestimation or underestimation of SIC depending on rock type.

3. If soil inorganic matter in the database is NULL, SIC is assumed to be zero.
propname: SOC (kg/m2) to 2 m bedrock/duripan or petro* (NPS)
SOC (kg/m2) to 2 m bedrock/duripan or petro* (NPS)

evaldesc:
Evaluates SOC to a depth of two meter or to the occurrence of bedrock or other certain types of restrictive layers. 

SBSouthard 3/2009

1. Soil organic carbon result is in kg/m2 to the depth of the soil.  Conversion to pounds/acre: (kg/m) X (2.2 lbs/kg) X (4047 m2/acre); so, kg/m X 8903 = pounds SOC/acre. Likewise, kg/m2 * 4.4515 = tons/acre.

2. This rule evaluates to 2 meter depth or to representative top depth of any bedrock kind, any petro horizon and any duripan. Other restrictions were not coded into the depth to restriction subproperty used in the main interpretation property script because the concern is not rooting depth restrictions but total amount of SOC stored in soils on a volumetric basis. It was decided to include sequestered soil organic carbon that may exist below a strongly contrasted particle size. In a Fluvent, for example, or buried old surfaces below tephra deposits there may be large stores of carbon that lie below other kinds of restrictive layers.

3. The calculation is reported on a volumetric whole soil basis, corrected for representative rock fragments in database, the representative amount of soil passing the #10 sieve, rock fragment particle density, and the representative 1/3 bar density of the soil. The soil organic carbon is converted from horizon soil organic matter content stored as a weight percent of the < 2mm fraction of the soil and recalculated on a whole soil basis. 

4. The NPS SOC class rule was designed using an arbitrary linear curve in the associated evaluation. The curve was designed so that the "fuzzy value" multiplied by 1000 gives you that actual amount SOC calculated for the component in the NASIS data.

Data issues:

1. NULL 1/3 bulk density may exist for mineral horizons and this calculation will assign a bulk density value of 0.2 because in most cases NULL 1/3 bulk density in the data occurs with O horizons. In these cases the amount of SOC will be underestimated.

2. Particle densities vary over the country but 2.65 was used universally. More complex default queries could be written using parent material. It is not apparent if map results with broad SOC classes would reflect the extra effort to refine particle densities. This will result in either overestimation or underestimation of SOC depending on rock type.

3. An alternative script could be written to use the horizon rock fragment volume instead of sieves if sieves are NULL. At present, when the #10 sieves are null 100% passing is the default.

4. If soil organic matter in the database is NULL, SOC is assumed to be zero.

evalname: Percent Passing #200 Sieve, Weighted Average 25 to 200cm
evaldesc:
This evaluation tests for percent of sand in the thickest layer.

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
 
Where the result of the calculation sieveno200 -  sieveno4 is greater than 95 percent by weight the evaluation is absolutely true and "EXCESS FINES or GRAVEL" are not  restrictive features.
     AND
Where the result of the calculation sieveno200 -  sieveno4 is less than 50 percent by weight the evaluation is absolutely false and "EXCESS FINES or GRAVEL" are restrictive features.

Current version contains major  revisions to the Ames 1996 version.

Ames prior to 1996

1___________________________________________________________________
                                                                |                                         LIMITS            | RESTRICTIVE
+                                                              ________________________________
     PROPERTY                                   |    PROBABLE   |   IMPROBABLE   |  FEATURE
                                                               |     SOURCE        |     SOURCE              |
+___________________________________________________________________

 2. 12/UNIFIED                                 SW, SP, SW-SM,
                                                                SP-SM

                                                               13/GW, 13/GP,
                                                              13/GW-GM,
                                                              13/GP-GM

                                                                                                     14/GW, 14/GP,    SMALL
                                                                                                     14/GW-GM,        STONES
                                                                                                    14/GP-GM

                                                                                                    PT                            EXCESS  HUMUS

                                                                                                   ALL OTHER        EXCESS  FINES

 12/Evaluate the thickest layer between 10 and 60 inches and also the bottom layer.  Choose the best rating.  When rating is based on  bottom layer, verify thickness.
 13/% passing No. 4 sieve minus % passing No. 200 sieve > 25.
 14/% passing No. 4 sieve minus % passing No. 200 sieve < 25.



 According to footnote 12, calculations are done for both the thickest layer and the bottom layer.

 Description of Calculation for Thickest Layer:
+______________________________________________

 The layer with the most inches between 10 and 60 inches is determined.  This could be a surface layer or a sublayer.  The unified values given on the Soils-5 are examined for the appropriate layer(s).

 The layer(s) being examined are rated according to the following algorithm:

 If SW, SP, SW-SM, or SP-SM is listed as a unified entry, or if GW, GP, GW-GM or GP-GM is listed as a unified entry and footnote 13 applies (see following description of footnote 13), then a PROBABLE rating is given.

 Otherwise an IMPROBABLE rating is given.

 If the thickest layer is a sublayer, then this property is rated the same as this sublayer's rating.

 If the thickest layer is a surface layer, then this property is rated PROBABLE if there is any PROBABLE surface layer rating.  If there is none, then it is rated IMPROBABLE.

 Restrictive feature terms are assigned appropriately.



 Description of Calculation for Bottom Layer:
+____________________________________________

 If the bottom layer has no data, then this calculation is skipped and the ratings for the thickest layer are chosen.

 Otherwise, this calculation is the same as that for the thickest layer, except it is done for the bottom layer.  The bottom layer, like the thickest layer, may be a surface layer or a sublayer.

1

 Calculations for Footnotes 13 and 14
+____________________________________

 To do the calculations for these footnotes, the values given on the Soils-5 for % passing No. 4 sieve and % passing No. 200 sieve are examined.

 % passing No. 4 sieve
+_____________________

 Assign values to No_4_Lo and No_4_Hi.

 If no data is entered, then No_4_Lo = 100 and No_4_Hi = 100.

 If a single value, say x, is entered, then No_4_Lo = x and No_4_Hi = x.

 If the entry is a normal range, say x-y, then No_4_Lo = x and No_4_Hi = y.

 % passing No. 200 sieve
+_______________________

 Assign values to No_200_Lo and No_200_Hi.

 If no data is entered, then No_200_Lo = 0 and No_200_Hi = 0.

 If a single value, say x, is entered, then No_200_Lo = x and No_200_Hi = x.

 If the entry is a normal range, say x-y, then No_200_Lo = x and  No_200_Hi = y.


 Once these values have been assigned, the following calculations take place.

 No_4_Lo - No_200_Lo = Lo
 No_4_Hi - No_200_Hi = Hi

 maximum(Lo,Hi) = max

 If max > 25 then footnote 13 applies.
 If max <= 25 then footnote 14 applies.

For Property No. 2, UNIFIED, the best ratings must be chosen between those calculated for the thickest layer and the bottom layer.

 If both the thickest and bottom layers are rated PROBABLE, then the bottom layer is chosen.

 If the thickest layer is rated PROBABLE and the bottom layer is rated IMPROBABLE, then the thickest layer is chosen.

 If the bottom layer is rated PROBABLE and the thickest layer is rated IMPROBABLE, then the bottom layer is chosen.

 If neither the thickest or bottom layer is rated PROBABLE, then they must both be rated IMPROBABLE and the bottom layer is chosen.

 If the ratings for the thickest layer were chosen, then the calculations on the following page for Property No. 3, LAYER THICKNESS, are done.

	 => 40% the soil is limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as the number 1.0.
	  > 1 and < 40% the soil is somewhat limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as a number between 0 and 1.0.
	 =< 1% the soil is not limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as the number 0.

evaldesc:
The evaluation indexes the hydric rating for the soil component. The index expresses the degree to which hydric soil is a limitation.

hydric rating = yes	Rating value = 1.0
hydric rating = no 	Rating value = 0.5

This evaluation checks total subsidence and indexes the degree to which total subsidence is limiting.  Where the soil property "SUBSIDENCE TOTAL (TX)" is:

	 => 30 the soil is limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as the number 1.0.
	 > 0 and < 30 the soil is somewhat limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as a number between 0 and 1.0.
	 = 0 the soil is not limited and the degree of limitation index is expressed as the number 0.

This evaluation is crisp and checks the texture_modifier_and_class for all layers. 
 
Where texture_class equals coarse sands, fine sands, very fine sands or sandy gravel for any layer the evaluation is absolutely true and the restrictive feature is CUTBANKS CAVE.
    AND
Where texture_class does not equal coarse sands, fine sands, very fine sands or sandy gravel or is NULL for all layers the evaluation is absolutely false and the restrictive feature is not CUTBANKS CAVE.
 
 
 Ames Description prior to 1996: 

                                   	    |             LIMITS      		               |RESTRICTIVE
     PROPERTY       	    |  SLIGHT  | MODERATE |  SEVERE  |  FEATURE
 4. USDA TEXTURE       	              ---                COS, S,     CUTBANKS
    (20-60")                                  		                 FS, VFS,    CAVE
                                             		                 LCOS, LS,
			                                       LFS, LVFS,
			                                       G, SG
 
 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________
 
The textures given on the Soils-5 are examined for the layers within 20-60 inches.  If surface layers are included in these depths, each is rated separately.  Then each sublayer is rated to determine the worst sublayer rating.  The rating algorithm used on each layer is as follows:
 
If COS, S, FS, VFS, LCOS, LS, LFS, LVFS, G, or SG is listed as a texture, then a SEVERE rating is given.

Otherwise a SLIGHT rating is given.
 
If surface layers are not involved, then this property is rated the same as the worst sublayer rating.
 
If surface layers are involved, then the following applies.  If the worst sublayer rating is SEVERE, then this property is rated SEVERE and no phasing will be done, regardless of the surface layer ratings.
 
If the worst sublayer rating is MODERATE, then this property is rated MODERATE if there is any SLIGHT or MODERATE surface layer rating, and it is rated SEVERE if there is any SEVERE surface layer
 rating.  Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.
 
If the worst sublayer rating is SLIGHT, then this property is rated SLIGHT if there is any SLIGHT surface layer rating, MODERATE if there is any MODERATE surface layer rating, and SEVERE if there is any SEVERE surface layer rating.  Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given. rating, and it is rated SEVERE if there is any SEVERE surface layer rating.  Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.

evalname: GRL-RPI-Rock Outcrop Present in Map Unit
evaldesc:
Copied from NCCPI_B - Rock Outcrop Present in Map Unit

This evaluation is looking at the map unit name where it has any portion of the name being Rock outcrop, rocky or very rocky.

The evaluation is an arbitrary linear line that evaluates the map unit name where anything that had Rock outcrop in the name is out of the class and returns a value of 1. Any map unit with "rocky" in the name is a partial member of the class and is given a fuzzy value of 0.3. Any map unit with "very rocky" in the name is also a parital member of the class and is given a fuzzy value of 0.7. Any map unit that does not include these words in their name is considered a member of the class and returns a value of 0.

This is used with PA septic systems for ruling out any components that would have rock outcrops or rocky phases and be unsuitable for septic systems.

This evaluation tests for percent of sand in the surface layer.

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
 
Where the result of the calculation sieveno200 -  sieveno4 is greater than 90 percent by weight the evaluation is absolutely true and "TOO SANDY" is a restrictive features.
     AND
Where the result of the calculation sieveno200 -  sieveno4 is less than 70 percent by weight the evaluation is absolutely false and "TOO SANDY" is not a restrictive features.

Current version contains major revisions to the Ames 1996 version. 
Whereas a conversion was made from the USDA Textures as criteria to percent sand as determined from the sieve size data.  This conversion accommodates the intent and purpose of the fuzzy logic technology and will improve the quality of the interpretative product.  rdn 4/99.


Ames prior to 1996

                                                      |                                     LIMITS                             |   RESTRICTIVE
     PROPERTY                         |  SLIGHT  |   MODERATE   |  SEVERE       |  FEATURE
 10. USDA TEXTURE                      ---       LCOS, VFS          COS, S, FS      TOO SANDY
     (SURFACE LAYER)                                 28/LFS, 28/LS

 28/Rate SLIGHT if finer textured material is within 20 inches of  the surface.

 Description of Calculation:

 The textures given on the Soils-5 for each surface layer are examined.

 The surface layers are each rated separately using the following algorithm:

     If COS, S, or FS is listed as a texture, then a SEVERE rating  is given.
     If LCOS, VFS, 28/LFS, or 28/LS is listed as a texture, then a  MODERATE rating is given.  (See the next page for a  description of         the calculation of footnote 28.)
     Otherwise a SLIGHT rating is given.

 If there is a surface layer with a SEVERE rating, then this property is rated SEVERE.  If there is a surface layer with a MODERATE
 rating, then this property is rated MODERATE.  If there is a surface layer with a SLIGHT rating, then this property is rated SLIGHT.
 Phasing will be done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.

 Calculations for Footnote 28
+____________________________

 The calculations to determine if finer textured material is within 20 inches of the surface are the same as if the following property
 had been calculated.

evaldesc:
7/99 Modification:
This evaluation checks the filtering capacity of the soil.  The maximum high, low, and representative values for sat_hydraulic_conductivity are selected for each horizon between 24 to 72 inches and above any restrictive layer. 

The fuzzy space is defined as the condition:
  Where the soil horizon property sat_hydraulic_conductivity > 42 micrometers/second (6.0 inches/hr), the evaluaton is absolutely true and the restrictive feature is poor effluent filter field.
        AND
  Where the soil horizon property sat_hydraulic_conductivity <= 42 micrometers/second (6.0 inches/hour), the evaluation is absolutely false and the restrictive feature is not poor effluent filter field.

If no data is entered, then an artificial default value(s) is used.

In 1990 the evaluation depth was extended from a base of 40 inches to a base of 60 inches.

Ames Description Prior to 1996

                                              |                           LIMITS                              |  RESTRICTIVE
     PROPERTY                 |  SLIGHT  | MODERATE |  SEVERE  |  FEATURE
 7. PERMEABILITY          ---                 ---                  >6.0             POOR FILTER
    (IN/HR):    (24-40")            
 
 Description of Calculation:
+___________________________
   
 The values given on the Soils-5 for permeability are examined and a
 high value for each layer is determined.  The high value used for
 comparison depends on which of the following conditions is met
 first.
 
 If no data is entered, then an artificial value of 0 is used.
 
 If the entry is a single number or is of the form '<xx', then the
  single value entered is used.
 
 If the entry is of the form '>xx', then an artificial value of 100
  is used.
 
 Otherwise the high value is used.
 
 The layers within the given depths are examined.  If surface layers are included in these depths, each is rated separately.  Then each sublayer is rated to determine the worst sublayer rating.  The rating algorithm used on each layer is as follows:
 
           A value > 6.0 gets a SEVERE rating.
           A value <= 6.0 gets a SLIGHT rating.
 
 If surface layers are not involved, then this property is rated the
 same as the worst sublayer rating.
 
 If surface layers are involved, then the following applies.  If the
 worst sublayer rating is SEVERE, then this property is rated SEVERE
 and no phasing will be done, regardless of the surface layer
 ratings.
 
 If the worst sublayer rating is SLIGHT, then this property is rated
 SLIGHT if there is any SLIGHT surface layer rating, and it is rated
 SEVERE if there is any SEVERE surface layer rating.  Phasing will be
 done using texture terms if more than one rating is given.
propname: KSAT HIGHEST MINIMUM ABOVE RESTRICTIVE LAYER 120 to 180cm
